# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Kingdom Roofing Systems
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely | Refreshed: April 28, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in the spring of 2012 by Daniel Young and Ryan Martlage

, Kingdom Roofing Systems is a multi-location Central Indiana exterior remodeling contractor. 

They operate three registered locations: Marion (HQ), Bloomington, and 6964 Corporate Dr, Indianapolis, IN 46278.

 

They hold GAF Master Elite status — an honor held by only 2% of roofing contractors nationwide — and are also an Owens Corning Platinum Preferred contractor

, giving them dual top-tier manufacturer credentialing that is a core pillar of their pitch.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale

**Confidence: medium.** 

PitchBook lists Kingdom Roofing Systems at 40 total employees.

 An older profile from Zionsville Monthly reported closer to 30, suggesting modest but real growth over time. 

By their own account, Kingdom installs approximately 500 roofs and 700 total jobs annually — 40% commercial, 60% residential.

 At an average residential ticket of $12,000–$15,000 and commercial work layered in, rough annual revenue likely falls in the $7M–$10M range. **Confidence: low** — no public financials exist, but job volume and headcount both point to this band.

A critical new data point: 

Kingdom is now part of the Allstar Home Services family — described as "a fast-growing national network of leading exterior remodeling brands backed by Morgan Stanley Capital Partners."

 This is a private equity backstop that changes the competitive calculus entirely. They now have institutional capital behind them.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active recruiting is concentrated on the revenue side. 

ZipRecruiter shows an open role for a "High-Income Sales Opportunity — Roofing and Exterior Remodeling Sales Representative" in Indianapolis, advertising uncapped commission, paid training, and pre-qualified leads.

 

A commercial sales representative role is also posted statewide with a $60K–$70K base plus up to 5% commission, alongside a commercial site supervisor opening.

 

Daniel Young's LinkedIn confirms they are also actively recruiting residential sales reps in Bloomington and Indianapolis.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles spotted in the last 30 days — their hiring is entirely front-of-funnel sales-focused, which suggests they are trying to accelerate top-line revenue post-PE acquisition rather than build internal infrastructure.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

**Yelp:** 

The Indianapolis location at 6964 Corporate Dr has 54 photos posted

 but only 16 reviews — thin for a company this size. No active Q&A. The Marion location has 3 reviews. Minimal Yelp investment overall.

**BBB:** 

BBB Accredited since July 8, 2016

, rated A+. 

Four total complaints in the last 3 years, with 1 complaint closed in the last 12 months

 — one of which involved a customer alleging harassment via repeated calls, emails, and door knocks after asking to be left alone. That complaint pattern is consistent with an aggressive storm-chasing sales culture.

**Facebook:** 

The Facebook page lists 88% recommendation rate across 100 reviews

 — meaningfully lower than their Google presentation.

**Angi/HomeAdvisor:** Mixed signals. Positive installation reviews sit alongside complaints about lawn damage, wrong nail sizing, and shingles coming loose the day of installation. At least one reviewer on Angi gave a 1-star account citing failed warranty follow-through and a $795 inspection fee demand. The gap between their 4.7 Google score and the rougher texture on Angi and BBB indicates review-funneling toward Google.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Kingdom has an established SEO history. 

Their past agency (Paper Box SEO) documented that by optimizing their Google Business Profile and acquiring more reviews, Kingdom achieved a 219% increase in organic leads over one year.

 They have dedicated location-specific service pages (e.g., [kingdomroofingsystems.com/indianapolis-roof-replacement/](https://kingdomroofingsystems.com/indianapolis-roof-replacement/)) and a separate landing page domain at `kingdomgreatdeals.com` — a classic tactic to run conversion-optimized paid landing pages separately from the main domain. 

They also have a branded mobile app for project tracking, warranty storage, and referral rewards

 — a sticky post-sale retention tool that contributes to backlink and brand signal diversity. Blog content appears thin and not recently updated. Schema markup on service pages is present but AEO optimization (FAQ schema, conversational query targeting) is not evident. Their dual-manufacturer certification pages (GAF + Owens Corning) create authoritative content nodes that likely pull manufacturer backlink equity.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Kingdom Roofing Systems does surface in AI-generated responses for general Central Indiana roofing queries, primarily due to their volume of third-party citations across BBB, Angi, Owens Corning's contractor directory, and their Zionsville Monthly press feature. In tests for "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," they are mentioned alongside other established local names, largely because their dual GAF Master Elite + Owens Corning Platinum Preferred credentials are machine-readable and frequently cited. They are not dominant in AI answers for suburban submarkets like Fishers, Noblesville, or Zionsville — those results skew toward competitors with more hyperlocal page content and recent review velocity. Their near-zero recent review activity (1 in 90 days) is a direct AI-visibility liability: generative engines weight recency of social proof signals.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where Kingdom beats Raptor:** Dual manufacturer elite status (GAF Master Elite + Owens Corning Platinum Preferred simultaneously) is a credential Raptor cannot currently match on both fronts, and Kingdom deploys it loudly. Their branded customer app and PE-backed scale give them operational infrastructure advantages for multi-location coverage. Their commercial division (40% of volume) gives them revenue diversification Raptor doesn't have.

**Where Raptor beats Kingdom:** 664 reviews at a true 5.0 vs. Kingdom's 304 at 4.7 — that's a meaningful trust gap, especially in AI-cited results. Kingdom's off-Google review profile is inconsistent (BBB complaints, Angi negatives, 88% Facebook rec rate) suggesting the 4.7 is their ceiling, not their floor. Kingdom's review velocity is essentially dead (1 review in 90 days) while Raptor's pipeline remains active.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Kingdom's aggressive door-to-door and follow-up sales culture is generating documented harassment complaints on BBB — Raptor should make "no-pressure, no-chase" a specific, named differentiator in ads and on the website while Kingdom's complaints are live and searchable.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **The dual-domain paid landing page play.** Kingdom runs `kingdomgreatdeals.com` as a stripped-down conversion page separate from their main domain — isolating paid traffic from organic and enabling aggressive A/B testing without touching core SEO. Cameron should evaluate whether Raptor's paid campaigns warrant a dedicated CRO-optimized landing domain or at minimum isolated landing pages with independent conversion tracking.

2. **The branded customer app as a referral engine.** 

Kingdom's app lets customers track projects, store warranties, and make referrals to earn rewards

 — turning every completed job into a passive lead-gen node. Raptor doesn't need a custom app to replicate this; a well-structured referral program with text/email delivery and a reward mechanism (gift card, check, or Raptor-branded perk) would capture the same mechanic at a fraction of the build cost.

3. **Monitor their PE-backed expansion closely.** 

Kingdom is now inside the Allstar Home Services / Morgan Stanley Capital Partners portfolio

 — meaning they have access to centralized marketing resources, brand playbooks, and acquisition capital. Watch for sudden jumps in their ad spend on Meta Ad Library, new submarket GBP listings (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville), or a rebrand push. When PE money hits a regional home-services brand, the first 12 months usually bring a paid media surge. Raptor needs to be fortified in those suburban GBP rankings before that budget arrives.

## 1. Who They Are



Owner Corey Cates has been in roofing since 2006, originally picking up the trade on a Hurricane Katrina mission trip in Louisiana. He graduated with a Biology degree from Indiana University and founded Weathertight Roofing in May 2012.

 Rough revenue estimate: with sub-permit-threshold residential jobs factored in and a three-location footprint, $2M–$4M ARR is a reasonable range. **Confidence: low.** They are almost certainly running leaner than their "three locations" marketing implies.

 — low engagement for a 13-year-old company. No Facebook Ad Library ads were surfaced in searches, suggesting either no active paid social spend or very limited/dark targeting.

, which is a credibility signal worth noting, though the BBB profile shows no complaint volume publicly visible. The Yelp profile exists (yelp.com/biz/weathertight-roofing-fishers) but returned no review data in search results — likely very thin. 

Manta shows zero reviews.

 The pattern here is classic review-funneling: all social proof is concentrated on Google, with every other platform essentially dark. That is a vulnerability — a single negative Google review would hurt them more than a diversified competitor.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

[Weathertightroofingllc.com](https://weathertightroofingllc.com) has a multi-page site with service-specific pages for commercial roofing, metal roofing, gutters/siding, and location-named URLs (Muncie, Noblesville, Lawrence, Fishers).

 — this is genuinely differentiated UX content that Google rewards. However, no blog or content marketing cadence was found; the site reads as a brochure, not an authority hub.

, which generates a legitimate third-party citation. Domain authority is likely modest (estimated DA 15–25 range) given the absence of local press backlinks or content-driven inbound links. Their location-page strategy (targeting "Noblesville," "Lawrence," "Muncie" in title tags) is a standard local SEO tactic but the pages lack substantive geo-specific content. No schema markup evidence found. AEO posture is minimal — no FAQ schema, no structured data that would feed generative engines.

Based on available search data and the structure of their digital presence, Weathertight Roofing is unlikely to be cited by name in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini responses to queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," or "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville." The factors that drive generative engine citation — authoritative blog content, local press coverage, structured FAQ data, strong third-party directory presence — are all absent or underdeveloped. Their Birdeye and Service Atlas profiles exist and could generate some signal, but 

Service Atlas simply mirrors their Google review count and rating

 without original content that LLMs would index as authoritative. This is a wide-open opportunity for Raptor: any competitor with active AEO content targeting these exact queries wins by default right now.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** GAF Master Elite certification is a credentialed differentiator they actively market, and their HOVER-based 3D visualization is a sales tool Raptor should evaluate. Their multi-city location page structure gives them modest geographic spread in organic search.

**Where Raptor beats them:** Raptor carries 664 reviews vs. Weathertight's 290 — more than double the social proof volume at the same 5.0 rating. Raptor's review velocity (data-tracked weekly) is a compounding moat. Weathertight's 30-day review pace of 8 reviews is anemic and suggests either a narrowing project pipeline or a broken review-ask process. Their Facebook page at under 1,000 likes after 13 years signals no real social investment.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their entire reputation infrastructure sits on a single platform (Google), with zero review depth anywhere else — one crisis-level Google review could crater their LSA ranking overnight.

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

Weathertight promotes HOVER as a tool to accurately measure roofs and let customers visualize their home on an interactive 3D model with different products and colors, which they claim removes homeowner hesitation around the project.

 If Raptor is not using HOVER or a comparable tool (e.g., EagleView, RoofSnap), this is a close-rate lever worth evaluating — especially on premium replacement jobs.

Weathertight claims over 20 years of experience handling insurance claims and specifically markets their ability to guide clients through the process with honesty and communication.

 This is a high-intent audience segment (storm damage homeowners) that Raptor could own more explicitly with dedicated landing pages and targeted paid search.

3. **Multi-Location Page Architecture.** Their practice of building out geo-targeted service pages for Noblesville, Lawrence, Muncie, and Fishers is worth auditing against Raptor's own site structure. ## Erie Home — Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: April 26, 2025**

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Erie Home was founded in 1976

 and operates under the legal entity Erie Construction Mid-West, LLC, with 

headquarters in Toledo, Ohio.

 

The company provides residential roofing and basement waterproofing services, including metal roofing, asphalt shingle roofs, foundation repair, and air quality solutions.

 Their differentiation hook is proprietary stone-coated steel metal roofing — 

also known as Erie Roofing, Erie Metal Roofing, or Erie Basement Solutions, the company is best known for its metal roofs made from stone-coated steel stamped to resemble traditional roofing materials.

 Indianapolis is one of their standard market rollout locations, not a flagship — it's a branch office within a national machine.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



Erie Home eclipses $450M in annual revenue and operates across 40 states in over 75 U.S. cities.

 A more recent Indeed job posting self-reports even higher: 

"with over 100 locations and $600M+ in annual revenue."

 **Confidence: medium** — these are self-reported figures from recruiting materials and LinkedIn, not audited financials. 

LinkedIn lists 725 employees company-wide,

 though Apollo.io estimates closer to 840. The Indianapolis branch is a fraction of that headcount — likely 15–30 local W2 staff with subcontracted installation crews. **Confidence: low** on the local headcount specifically. 

ZoomInfo also flagged that Erie Home has entered into an agreement to be acquired by Leaf Home,

 which is the most significant strategic development to watch — a post-acquisition integration could disrupt the Indy branch's local responsiveness for 12–18 months.

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Current active LinkedIn postings include Sales Representatives (Cedar Park, TX; Round Rock, TX; Springfield, MO) and Roofing Installation Crews Wanted across multiple markets including Carmel, NY, Yonkers, NY, Champaign, IL, and Omaha, NE.

 No Indianapolis-specific open roles surfaced on LinkedIn or Indeed in the last 30 days. The dominant hiring pattern across all platforms — 

hiring immediately for roofing subcontractors, seeking reliable roofing crews for consistent year-round work

 — confirms their install model relies on 1099 subcontractor crews rather than W2 craftsmen. This is worth noting: they are not building local ownership into their labor model. No marketing, ops leadership, or branch manager postings flagged for Indianapolis.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The review platform spread on Erie Home is one of the most dramatic discrepancies in the Indy market. On Google (Indianapolis branch): 274 reviews at 4.6 stars — serviceable but unexceptional. The national picture tells a more useful story for Raptor's positioning. 

Erie Home's Yelp rating sits at just 1.8 stars from 41 reviews

 — a massive gap from their Google number that signals aggressive review funneling to Google and GBP while Yelp collects the bleed-through from dissatisfied buyers. 

BBB records show 377 total complaints filed in the last three years nationally, with 136 of those in the past 12 months alone.

 

The Indianapolis BBB listing shows an A+ rating

, but that grade is largely complaint-response rate, not satisfaction. 

Sales presentations run 3–4 hours, and the sales team follows up persistently — one customer documented 116 calls in 16 days.

 Facebook Ad Library shows Erie running national creative, not geo-targeted Indy-specific ads, suggesting their paid social is centralized and not locally optimized.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**

Erie Home's domain ([eriehome.com](https://eriehome.com)) carries strong national authority built through a network of city-specific landing pages. 

The Indianapolis location page targets communities like Carmel, Greenwood, and Lawrence by name

 — standard location page SEO play, but not deeply differentiated content. They rank for broad terms like "metal roofing Indianapolis" on the strength of domain authority, not local content depth. Their blog is thin and largely product-focused rather than educational or trust-building. No evidence of active local press backlinks (Indianapolis Star, IBJ, Indy Business) or community partnerships that would build local relevance signals. Their GBP UTM structure (`utm_source=gbp&utm_medium=roofing&utm_campaign=Indianapolis`) shows they are tracking GBP traffic deliberately — they understand the channel. Schema markup is present on core service pages. The AEO gap is real: their content does not answer specific Indy homeowner questions (hail season timelines, permit requirements, HOA restrictions in Hamilton County), which is exactly where a local operator can out-rank them for long-tail and AI-cited queries.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Erie Home surfaces in AI search results for national queries like "best metal roofing companies" primarily because of their scale, review volume across BBB/GuildQuality/Trustpilot, and editorial coverage from [This Old House](https://www.thisoldhouse.com/roofing/reviews/erie-roofing) and [Today's Homeowner](https://todayshomeowner.com/roofing/reviews/erie-roofing/). For hyper-local queries — "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville" — Erie Home is not reliably cited by ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini as a named local recommendation. Their local AEO footprint is weak because they have no locally-authored content, no Indy-specific community signals, and no GBP Q&A optimization. This is a direct opening for Raptor: structured, locally-specific FAQ content optimized for AI retrieval will leapfrog Erie's generic national landing pages in generative results.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Erie beats Raptor:** National brand recognition, financing infrastructure ($0-down offers, third-party lenders), and a proprietary metal roofing product line that can anchor a premium upsell conversation. Their 274 Google reviews also provide surface-level social proof for homeowners who stop at the star count. **Where Raptor beats Erie:** Review quality and velocity tell the real story — Raptor's 664 reviews at a 5.0 vs. Erie's 274 at 4.6, with Erie pulling in only 9 reviews in 90 days, signals a stalled or declining customer feedback engine. Erie's 0.97 owner response rate sounds disciplined, but 

their BBB responses are cookie-cutter, often starting with "Erie Home apologizes for any inconvenience this may have caused"

 — the same boilerplate pattern bleeds into Google. Raptor's authentic, specific responses are a meaningful differentiator. **Most exploitable weakness:** Erie's Yelp rating of 1.8 stars paired with documented high-pressure 3-4 hour sales tactics is an open door — Raptor should be showing up in "Erie Home complaints Indianapolis" and "Erie Home vs local roofer" search and AI results with trust-based content.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **The financing lead magnet.** 

Erie is actively promoting "$0 down on a new roof" as a 2025 campaign hook.

 Whether or not Raptor matches the offer, Cameron should test financing-forward ad creative in Meta and Google — Erie's national data confirms it converts at the top of funnel in this price-sensitive market.

2. **The multi-brand SEO structure.** Erie runs parallel landing pages under aliases (Erie Metal Roofs, Erie Construction, Erie Basement Solutions) to capture different search intents. Raptor doesn't need multiple brands, but building separate, deeply-answered service pages for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, and Zionsville — each with locally-specific content rather than swapped city names — would replicate the traffic capture without the brand fragmentation risk.

3. **Monitor the Leaf Home acquisition closely.** 

Jenilee Common is slated to become CEO of the combined Erie/Leaf Home entity post-close.

 Acquisitions of this size create 6–18 months of internal chaos — rep turnover, territory confusion, billing disputes. The window to capture Erie's unhappy Indianapolis customers with targeted search and retargeting campaigns will open predictably when the deal closes. Set a Google Alert for "Erie Home Leaf Home acquisition" and have a conquest campaign ready to deploy.

**SITUATION ASSESSMENT**

We have a structural advantage that Raptor cannot replicate overnight: 

Amos Exteriors has been a trusted name in Central Indiana since 1971, with more than 50 years of experience as a family-owned and operated company.

 

Raptor, by contrast, only rebranded from "Raptor Restoration" as recently as January 2025.

**PART 1 — THREE SPECIFIC VULNERABILITIES TO EXPLOIT**

**Vulnerability 1: Their brand identity is less than 18 months old.**


Raptor Restoration rebranded to Raptor Roofing in January 2025, describing it as a "strategic transformation" accompanied by an entirely new website.

 That means a significant portion of their review equity and online authority was built under a different brand name. Homeowners searching for accountability and longevity will not find a 50-year track record — they will find a company that changed its name last year. This is exploitable in every channel where we can speak to tenure.

**Vulnerability 2: Public post-installation complaints exist on the BBB record — and they show a pattern.**


A BBB complaint against Raptor states that after a new roof was installed, broken boards and unsecured end caps were visible, and after two weeks the customer still had not received a response or a fix.

 This is their exact brand promise — "we don't outsource accountability" — cracking in public. 

Meanwhile, our own BBB record contains a complaint about a siding project where an undersized crew took over a week to complete 80% of the work, damaged insulation foam was not repaired as contracted, and gutters were not scheduled — causing the home to experience rain without gutters installed.

 We are not clean here either. We must internally address these execution gaps before we go on offense, or we hand Raptor the same ammunition.

**Vulnerability 3: They are entirely dependent on Google LSA and Google Ads — a single-channel lead structure with no off-platform loyalty layer.**
Their lead flow lives or dies on Google's auction. 

In LSA, higher bids win placement. If competitors outbid them, Google hands them the spot. There is no creative workaround — you either match the market rate or accept lower visibility.

 They have built no documented referral program, no neighborhood-level organic presence outside sponsored posts, and no second-channel CRM to re-engage past customers. **Their growth is rented, not owned.** That is a ceiling we can break through.

GAF Master Elite. Amos Exteriors — The Name Indianapolis Has Trusted Since Before Raptor Existed."* 

On LSA specifically, if their budgets are capped, Google feeds open-budget competitors first — so we run uncapped LSA budgets during peak storm weeks and outrank them for position at the exact moment homeowners are searching.

 Budget authorization needed: minimum $8,000/month in combined LSA and Search for 90 days.

Fresh reviews drive sustained LSA visibility. Businesses maintaining steady review flow stay visible, while those letting reviews go stale see sudden drops in lead volume. Reviews display directly in the LSA interface, making them doubly crucial for both ranking and conversion.

 We have nearly 5x their review volume. We need to make that number impossible to ignore. Real people, real roofs, real zip codes called out in the caption. Raptor's 666 reviews will feel like a footnote.

## Cochran Exteriors — Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: April 28, 2026**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 2010, Cochran Exteriors has built its reputation around exterior renovation in Indiana.

 

The company is co-owned by Ross Cochran and John Cochran

, making it a family-owned operation with a named Marketing Manager (Andrew Beck) already on staff — a signal they take brand seriously. 

They operate out of Indiana, Illinois (Schaumburg), and Kentucky (Lexington)

, positioning them as a regional multi-state player, not just an Indy shop. Their primary pitch is full exterior scope: 

roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, and more

, which dilutes their roofing identity but expands average job value.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



RocketReach puts Cochran at 44 employees and $6.8 million in annual revenue (2025 data).

ZoomInfo flags Cochran as actively seeking a Sales Manager in Indianapolis.

 That is a mid-level ops/revenue role that typically precedes a structured sales team expansion or territory push.

LinkedIn shows an open Commercial Estimator role in Indianapolis

, consistent with their growing commercial book of business.
- 

Greg joined the Cochran team in 2025 as Brand President, with a background in home services and a focus on client experience.

 A brand president hire in 2025 is not a maintenance move — that is a growth posture signal.
- 

David VanOstrand also joined in 2025 as a Sales Representative.



The combination of Brand President + Sales Manager search + Commercial Estimator suggests a deliberate 2025–2026 scaling push across both residential sales and commercial revenue.

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, Cochran lists 54 reviews at the 8461 Castlewood Dr address.

 That is a thin Yelp footprint relative to their 1,173 Google reviews — a textbook review-funneling gap. Sentiment on third-party platforms runs rougher than Google suggests.



On BBB, they hold an A+ accreditation

 and 

operate from two registered locations: Indianapolis and a Greenwood office at 48 N. Emerson Ave.

 However, BBB complaints reveal recurring themes: 

one reviewer warns to "avoid this company" and states the warranty "isn't worth the paper it was written on."

 

Another HomeAdvisor reviewer describes their entire experience as "difficult, frustrating, and stressful" from sales to project completion.





On Nextdoor, Cochran comes highly recommended with customers praising professionalism and quality.

 They maintain a claimed Nextdoor business page and appear to post there actively. No Facebook Ad Library data was available in these results — worth a manual pull at [facebook.com/ads/library](https://www.facebook.com/ads/library).

Cochran's web presence is structured with intent. 

Their roofing pages include specific local cost data — roof replacement in Indianapolis ranging $16,000–$24,000 — and a call to action for a free assessment.

 That is a clear attempt to capture cost-intent queries in organic search, which is smart AEO practice. 

They also deploy a free Indiana roof cost calculator

, a lead-gen tool that likely generates strong time-on-page signals and captures mid-funnel traffic. 

Cochran holds an Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor designation and is a certified vinyl siding installer with NRCA membership

 — credentials they surface on Houzz and likely on-site for E-E-A-T signals. Their LinkedIn content cadence includes recurring #TipTuesday and #ServiceSpotlight posts, indicating a managed social/content calendar, not ad hoc posting. ## Competitive Intelligence Brief — Bone Dry Roofing (Loc 2 / Indianapolis HQ)
**Refreshed: April 26, 2026 | Dashboard: Cameron Blakely, Raptor Roofing**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989 by Gene Judd, who got his start swinging hammers alongside his parents out of a small garage in Speedway, Indiana.

 

Headquartered in Indianapolis, Bone Dry Roofing operates 20 locations and runs an 81% residential / 19% commercial split under Gene Judd as President.

 

The company has grown aggressively through acquisition, with the Bone Dry Family of Companies now spanning 15 branded roofing locations plus subsidiaries including Roof One, Bone Dry Commercial Roofing, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors across eight states.

 Their differentiator is institutional scale dressed up as a family operation — not a franchise, but an M&A rollup playing local in every market.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale

**Confidence: high** on revenue range; **medium** on employee count given multi-entity structure.



Per *Roofing Contractor* Magazine's 2023 Contractor of the Year profile, Bone Dry reported 2022 annual revenue of $121 million across 20 locations with approximately 500 employees company-wide.

 More recent data pushes that figure higher: 

ZoomInfo notes that Bone Dry's 2023 revenue exceeded $183 million,

 and 

LeadIQ places the current revenue range at $100M–$250M.

 

Of the 2022 $121M total, approximately $36 million — roughly 30% — came from the original Indianapolis office alone,

 making the Loc 2 GBP the single highest-volume location in the network. Applying that 30% share to a ~$183M 2023 base implies the Indy location alone approaches $55M annually. That's not a local competitor — that's a regional institution operating in Raptor's backyard.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Bone Dry currently carries 79 open jobs across Indeed company-wide.

 Active Indianapolis-area postings include: 

Roofing Service Technician, Roofing Sales Representative (Residential Division), and Sales Representative for the Commercial Roofing Division.

 

An IEG Sales Representative role (Interior, Exterior, and Gutters) is also live, targeting homeowners across the full exterior service stack.

 Notably, 

an Accounts Receivable Clerk posting in Indianapolis and an Assistant General Manager search in Detroit are also active,

 suggesting back-office scaling alongside field expansion. No marketing-specific or CMO-equivalent hire flagged for the Indy location in the last 30 days — 

Matt Tyner holds the CMO title company-wide, focused on new market entry and lead volume growth.

 The volume and breadth of sales postings signals an active push to grow the top-of-funnel rep count heading into peak season.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Bone Dry's primary Indianapolis location on Yelp (7735 Winton Dr) shows 75 reviews

 — a thin count relative to 943 on Google, which is a textbook review-funneling signal. Their Google review machine is clearly optimized to route satisfied customers to Google only, leaving Yelp as an unmanaged channel where disgruntled customers tend to self-select. 

BBB profile carries an A+ rating and multiple Angie's List Super Service Award wins on record.

 Community-level partnerships are active: 

Bone Dry partnered with Indy Humane on a pet microchipping event in the Indianapolis area

 and 

donated a full roof and labor to a Nashville first responder alongside Owens Corning and the Nashville Sounds.

 Facebook Ad Library was not directly searchable within this pull, but their tech stack — 

confirmed to include Facebook, LinkedIn, WordPress, and Adobe Premiere Pro

 — indicates active paid social production capability. The Yelp gap (75 reviews vs. 943 on Google) is the clearest vulnerability in their off-Google presence.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

[bonedry.com](https://bonedry.com) is a high-authority domain by home-services standards — multi-state, 35+ years old, Wordpress-based, with dedicated city/location subpages at URLs like [bonedry.com/indianapolis/](https://bonedry.com/indianapolis/). 

Bone Dry was named *Roofing Contractor* Magazine's 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year, generating national trade press backlinks

 that materially boost domain authority. They operate a blog, email newsletter, and location-specific service pages covering roofing, gutters, masonry, solar, siding, and insulation — a topical authority moat that takes years to replicate. 

Their tech stack includes Adobe Premiere Pro, cdnjs, and Webpack,

 indicating video production capacity and a JavaScript-heavy front end (which can hurt crawlability if not carefully managed). The "Bone Dry University" brand and the 2023 national award are both organic link-building assets Raptor has no equivalent of yet. AEO risk: their blog and service pages are exactly the type of structured, high-volume content that LLMs index for local contractor answers.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry Roofing is very likely cited by name in AI-generated responses to queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," and "roofing company Fishers Noblesville." The reasons are structural: 

their own site claims 4.8 stars across over 5,000 reviews in nine states,

 giving LLMs multiple high-confidence data points to pull from. The national trade press citation — 

named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by *Roofing Contractor* Magazine

 — is exactly the third-party authority signal that pushes contractors into AI answer sets. Their multi-location footprint also means they appear in AI answers for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, and Greenwood simultaneously, while Raptor currently competes for those suburb queries with a single GBP. This is the most dangerous asymmetry in the matchup. Raptor needs suburb-specific AEO content (dedicated landing pages, schema markup, localized FAQ content) to compete in AI answer visibility for the collar communities.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Bone Dry beats Raptor:** Review volume (943 vs. 664), brand name recognition built over 35 years, national trade press authority, multi-service upsell depth (solar, masonry, commercial, insulation), and a dedicated CMO running coordinated multi-market paid media. Their Bone Dry University recruitment engine also means they can staff faster than a single-location operator.

**Where Raptor beats Bone Dry:** Rating purity (5.0 vs. 4.9 matters in AI ranking and LSA), owner response rate discipline (Raptor's consistent engagement vs. Bone Dry's institutional size making personal responsiveness harder), and premium positioning — Raptor can credibly claim accountability in a way a 500-person rollup structurally cannot. At Bone Dry's scale, subcontractor and crew consistency questions are real and show up in their longer-tail negative reviews.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their Yelp profile has just 75 reviews against 943 on Google — a classic corporate review-funneling gap that signals they are ignoring platforms where unhappy customers actually land, and where Raptor can establish clear visible superiority.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **The on-site production supervisor model.** 

Bone Dry keeps a production supervisor on-site for the duration of every project, serving as the main point of contact for homeowners.

 They also deliver 

detailed photos and videos throughout the installation process.

 Cameron should formalize and market this same practice explicitly — it's a direct counter to the "accountability" story and it's content-rich for social and review prompts.

2. **The community partnership playbook.** Bone Dry runs cause-tied visibility plays (Indy Humane, first responder roof donations) that generate local press, social engagement, and backlinks with zero paid media spend. Raptor should identify one Indy-area cause partnership per quarter and treat it as both a PR and link-building asset, not just goodwill.

3. **Suburb-specific landing pages with schema.** Bone Dry's domain covers every Indy suburb with dedicated pages. Cameron should prioritize publishing geo-specific pages for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood — each with LocalBusiness schema, FAQ schema targeting AI answer queries, and a distinct testimonial pool — to chip away at Bone Dry's current AEO advantage in those collar markets before the gap widens further.

## 1. Competitor SEO/AEO Benchmarks

**Methodology note:** Exact Ahrefs/Moz domain authority figures are not publicly surfaceable without a paid tool session. Backlink estimates below are derived from visible signals: named appearances on high-DA third-party roundup pages, manufacturer directory listings, press release pickups, PR agency placements, and association pages. Raptor's own data is based on the raptorroofing.com public footprint. All estimates are flagged accordingly.

---

### Bone Dry Roofing — Largest Gap

**Gap 1: Press-driven backlink profile Raptor cannot yet match.**



Bone Dry retained a PR firm (Dittoe PR) for a 16-month campaign covering Indianapolis and Nashville, executing media relations, bylined articles, and expert interviews across trade and national media — a strategy that generated a sustained pipeline of editorial backlinks from high-DA outlets.

 

That campaign produced the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year designation from Roofing Contractor Magazine

, which alone earned links from the magazine's site (estimated DA 55+), their Top 100 Contractors page, and every outlet that covered the award. Raptor has zero comparable press-placed backlinks visible in third-party roundup or news searches. Estimated referring domain gap: ~170 domains (Bone Dry ~185 estimated vs. Raptor ~15 estimated, based on visible signals — search run: "Bone Dry Roofing Indianapolis backlinks press mentions").

**Gap 2: Manufacturer certification pages create a compounding backlink tier Raptor currently lacks.**



Bone Dry partners with both Owens Corning and CertainTeed, holding Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status — tier designations that result in listing pages on both manufacturers' contractor-finder directories.

 Each manufacturer directory listing is a dofollow backlink from a domain with estimated DA 70+ (Owens Corning) and DA 60+ (CertainTeed). That is two perpetual, high-DA backlinks Raptor does not currently hold. 

Bone Dry carries an average rating of 4.8 stars across over 5,000 reviews

, a review volume that itself feeds AEO citation frequency.

**Gap 3: Multi-city programmatic content and GBP footprint.**



GuildQuality records show Bone Dry has surveyed customers in Carmel, Fishers, Westfield, Zionsville, Greenwood, Lafayette, and hundreds of additional cities.

 That translates to individual city-level landing pages, each with a GBP post stream and geo-tagged content. Raptor's public service area listing (Indianapolis, Greenwood, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, and surrounding areas) exists as a footer text string — not as individual optimized city pages with unique content, FAQ schema, or Review schema. This is the single fastest-to-close structural gap on the list.

---

### Indy Roof & Restoration — Second Largest Gap

**Gap 1: Self-publishing strategy creates a closed-loop backlink machine.**



Indy Roof & Restoration publishes comprehensive "best roofers in Indianapolis" roundup articles on their own domain — and in those articles, they position themselves as the definitive recommendation, citing a unique combination of insurance advocacy, financing, and water mitigation.

 These pages rank for high-volume head terms and are then cited by AI engines as authoritative sources for the query. The result: their domain receives backlinks from other roundup aggregators who scrape or reference the content, and their brand name appears in AI citation windows because the AI is reading their own content back. Raptor has no comparable authority content published on raptorroofing.com targeting "best roofers Indianapolis" as a primary keyword page.

**Gap 2: Multi-platform review volume creates citation density AI engines weight.**



Indy Roof & Restoration claims 2,000+ five-star reviews across platforms.

 

They hold BBB A+ status, are an Owens Corning Preferred Contractor, and are Malarkey Certified — with multiple certifications creating multiple manufacturer directory backlinks.

 Note: because Indy Roof already holds Malarkey certification, any Raptor strategy involving Malarkey exclusivity would be inaccurate. Raptor's current review count stands at approximately 533 based on findtrustedroofers.com data — a strong absolute number, but roughly one-quarter of Indy Roof's volume.

**Gap 3: Blog cadence and content depth.**



Indy Roof & Restoration published city-specific content including a Carmel-dedicated page as recently as March 2026

, demonstrating active programmatic publishing. Their blog index shows multiple posts per month with geo-targeted titles. Raptor's blog footprint is not indexed in any third-party roundup or news feed, suggesting either low publish frequency or no external linking to the blog. No Raptor blog post appeared in any of the six AEO test queries.

---

### Cochran Exteriors — Third Largest Gap

**Gap 1: Third-party directory placement drives AEO citations.**



ThreeBestRated.com places Cochran Exteriors in its top-three Indianapolis roofing contractors list, describing the company using its 50-point inspection methodology — the type of structured, citation-worthy content that AI engines pull verbatim.

 

Indy Roof & Restoration's own 2026 roundup includes Cochran, noting their design-forward positioning and 2010 founding.

 Cochran appears by name in at least three of the six AI-surfaced roundup sources tested. Raptor appeared in one (introindianapolis.com).

**Gap 2: Interactive conversion tools create dwell-time signals and backlinks.**



Cochran Exteriors offers a free Indiana roof cost calculator on their site, enabling instant price estimates.

 A calculator tool earns natural backlinks from home improvement blogs and local media when they recommend it as a resource. It also increases dwell time, reduces bounce, and creates a shareable utility that directories link to. Raptor currently has no equivalent interactive content asset.

**Gap 3: Schema and warranty positioning.**



Cochran offers a 50-year warranty backed by marketing copy on their roofing page

, giving AI engines a clean, quotable differentiator. When Perplexity or a Google AI Overview assembles a comparison of Indy roofers, "50-year warranty" is a machine-readable anchor point. Raptor's warranty language is not surfaced in a schema-marked or clearly quotable format on the public-facing pages reviewed.

---

## 2. Tactic of the Week

### Build one high-DA local backlink this week by submitting a "Roofing Cost in Indianapolis 2026" data page to the Indianapolis Business Journal's reader submission / contributed content desk.

**The Why.**



The old quantity-first approach to link building is obsolete. Modern algorithms prioritize relevance and intent, making one link from a local home builders association or regional news outlet carry far more weight than dozens of links from spammy directories.

 IBJ's domain authority is estimated in the 65-70 range based on its position as the primary local business publication for the Indianapolis metro. A single dofollow byline link from IBJ would, in isolation, roughly double Raptor's current estimated high-authority referring domain count. The mechanism is straightforward: Google's local pack and organic rankings for head terms like "roof replacement Indianapolis" are heavily correlated with referring domain quality. 

These off-page signals work together to support local SEO — they help Google understand where your business operates, what services you provide, and how trustworthy your company appears compared to other roofing businesses in the same market, improving organic visibility and ranking potential over time.



No competitor in the Raptor competitive set — including Bone Dry, Indy Roof, or Cochran — currently appears to hold a live IBJ byline backlink based on the search queries run this session. This is a gap in the market, not a guaranteed exclusive, but it appears to be an open lane based on available search data.

**The How.**

Step 1: This week, draft a 700-word contributed article titled something like "What Indianapolis Homeowners Are Actually Paying for Roof Replacement in 2026." Use Raptor's own job data to construct a real cost range by home size and neighborhood (e.g., Carmel 2,200 sq ft average vs. Greenwood 1,800 sq ft average). Real, localized numbers make the piece publishable and make it a natural citation target for future AI queries.

Step 2: Submit to IBJ's contributed content program at ibj.com. IBJ runs regular industry guest pieces. Frame the pitch around consumer education and cost transparency — not a service advertisement. The piece should read as journalism with Raptor as the expert source, not as a promotional brochure.

Step 3: Simultaneously, pitch the same data angle to the IndyStar's home improvement section and the Hamilton County Reporter, targeting the Carmel/Fishers/Noblesville geographic pocket where Raptor is actively serving jobs. Each outlet represents an additional DA 50+ backlink opportunity.

Step 4: Once the piece is live, add the URL to Raptor's Google Search Console as a new backlink so it registers in the crawl queue promptly.

**The Success Metric.**

Within 30 days of publication: (1) Raptor's estimated referring domain count increases by at least 2-3 domains from the media placements; (2) raptorroofing.com moves up 3-5 positions on "roof replacement Indianapolis" organic (not Maps) SERP — track in Google Search Console impressions and average position for that keyword cluster; (3) the IBJ article URL generates measurable referral traffic in GA4 within 14 days of going live. A placement with zero referral traffic within two weeks signals the piece was buried — follow up with the editor about promotion on IBJ's social accounts.

---

## 3. Raptor's AEO Standing

**Queries tested (6):** "best roofers Indianapolis," "top roofing contractor near Greenwood Indiana," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," "roofing company Fishers Indiana," "best rated roofer Noblesville," "Zionsville roof repair."

---

### Competitors Named in AI Search Answers

Based on the third-party roundup pages that Google AI Overviews and Perplexity draw from when answering the above queries, the following competitors were surfaced by name:

**Bone Dry Roofing** — named in four of the six query result sets. 

Third-party content consistently describes Bone Dry as a large regional provider offering single-source services beyond roofing — masonry, gutters, insulation — and notes top-tier manufacturer relationships that support extended warranties.

 This "multi-service regional anchor" framing is exactly the kind of clean, structured language AI engines lift verbatim.

**Indy Roof & Restoration** — named in four of six query result sets. 

Indy Roof & Restoration is described in the roundup content AI reads as the definitive recommendation for the modern homeowner, citing insurance advocacy, 0% financing, and full-service water mitigation as differentiators.

 Their own self-published roundup page is one of the sources AI cites, creating a self-reinforcing loop.

**Cochran Exteriors** — named in three of six. 

Cochran is cited for a distinct design-forward positioning and their 2010 founding, with roundup content noting they appeal to homeowners who view a roof as a component of curb appeal.



**Amos Exteriors** — named in three of six. 

Roundup content cites Amos's presence since 1971 and their GAF Master Elite Contractor status, which authorizes the Golden Pledge Limited Warranty — a specific, machine-readable credential that AI engines can quote as a clear differentiator.



**Big Boy's Construction** — named in two of six. 

Content notes rapid market share growth, focus on insurance claims and storm damage, and GAF Master Elite status despite being a younger brand.



---

### Is Raptor Cited?

Yes, in one of six query result sets. 

The introindianapolis.com roundup places Raptor at number one for 2025, citing service quality, professionalism, community focus, and comprehensive services with insurance support.

 This is meaningful — it means Raptor has at least one high-quality citation anchor in the AI-readable content pool. However, it is a single source, and AI engines weight citation frequency across multiple independent sources. The competitors above appear in four or more sources. Raptor appears in one.

Raptor was not cited by name in any AI-surfaced result for "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," "roofing company Fishers Indiana," "best rated roofer Noblesville," or "Zionsville roof repair."

---

### What Raptor Is Missing Structurally

**1. Citation frequency across independent sources.** AI engines treat multiple independent sources naming a brand as a trust signal. 

Link building for roofers is a strategic process of earning backlinks and mentions from reputable websites; with the emergence of AI within Google's standard search results, brand mentions and backlinks signal that your roofing business is credible, active, and trusted by the community.

 Raptor currently has one strong named citation. It needs four to six independent sources with domain authority above 40 citing it by name in a roofing-specific context.

**2. Review volume threshold.** 

Raptor currently holds a 5.0 rating from approximately 533 reviews on findtrustedroofers.com.

 

Bone Dry holds 5,000+ reviews across nine states with a 4.8 average.

 

Indy Roof & Restoration claims 2,000+ five-star reviews.

 AI engines use review volume as a proxy for market presence. At 533 reviews, Raptor sits below the apparent threshold (estimated ~600-800 for consistent AI citation in competitive queries) that triggers unprompted inclusion.

**3. Missing structured data.** No FAQ schema, no RoofingContractor schema, and no HowTo or Article schema appears in the Raptor pages reviewed. Competitors like Cochran have interactive tools and clearly labeled warranty claims that AI engines can extract as structured answers. Without machine-readable structured data, Raptor's page content cannot be lifted into an AI answer panel even when the content is good.

**4. No Wikipedia or authoritative reference entry.** None of the local roofing competitors have Wikipedia pages, so this is not a competitive gap — but it explains part of the ceiling. AI engines give heavier weight to entities with Wikipedia disambiguation pages. This is a 12-24 month project, not a 14-day one.

---

### One Specific AEO Move for the Next 14 Days

**Add FAQ schema to the five highest-traffic pages on raptorroofing.com this week.**

The mechanism: Google's AI Overviews and Perplexity both preferentially pull FAQ-structured content when assembling answers to "best roofer" and "roof replacement cost" queries. 

Search engines reward sites that clearly label what they offer and where — structured data gives Google clarity, and clarity earns rankings.

 Right now, Raptor's pages contain useful content (warranty info, service area, insurance claim help) that AI engines cannot extract in structured form because it is buried in body copy without schema markup.

Concrete steps: (1) Identify the five pages with the most current organic impressions in Google Search Console — these are almost certainly the homepage, the roof replacement page, the roof repair page, and two city pages. (2) Add a minimum of five FAQ pairs to each page using schema.org/FAQPage markup. Prioritize questions the AI queries above are asking: "How much does a roof replacement cost in Indianapolis?", "How long does a roof replacement take in Carmel Indiana?", "Does Raptor Roofing help with insurance claims?", "What areas does Raptor Roofing serve?", "What is Raptor Roofing's warranty?" (3) Validate each page in Google's Rich Results Test tool before publishing. (4) Request indexing for all five URLs in Google Search Console immediately after publishing.

Thirty-day success metric: At least two of the five pages show a Featured Snippet or People Also Ask appearance in Google Search Console's "Search Appearance" filter. Track AI Overview inclusion by manually running the six test queries above in an incognito Chrome window at the 30-day mark and noting whether Raptor appears by name in the AI-generated summary text.

## Amos Exteriors — Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Updated: April 26, 2025 | Cameron Blakely**

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Owner is Robert Amos; the marketing function is led by Bruce McClain (Director of Marketing) and Jana Perrott (Marketing Manager).

 

They operate with locations in both Indianapolis and Lafayette, IN

, and their scope goes well beyond roofing — siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, and commercial roofing all sit under one roof, making them a full-service exterior contractor rather than a pure-play roofer.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach pegs annual revenue at $28.6 million (2025 figure) with approximately 57 employees.

 Cross-referencing with Prospeo, 

employee count is estimated in the 51–100 range.

 The PPP loan data adds weight: 

Amos Exteriors received an SBA PPP loan of $584,200, retaining 40 jobs

 — suggesting 40+ direct W-2 staff at peak COVID headcount, consistent with 50-60 today inclusive of subcontractors. **Confidence: medium.** Revenue estimate likely reflects storm-surge years; a normalized run-rate is probably $18M–$25M.

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



ZipRecruiter shows an open posting for a Team Lead, Field Marketing in Indianapolis

 — this is the most relevant recent signal. The title suggests they are scaling door-knock / canvassing operations, not investing in inbound digital. 

ZoomInfo flags an active search for an Estimator and Project Manager in Indianapolis.

 No marketing technology, paid media, or digital-first roles are visible across Indeed, LinkedIn, or ZipRecruiter in the last 30 days. The hiring profile reads as a company adding field sales muscle, not a marketing transformation.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform review picture is damning for a company sitting at 3,046 Google reviews. 

Yelp shows only 2.5 stars

 on 19 reviews — a classic review-funneling operation where happy customers are directed exclusively to Google and unhappy ones land on Yelp organically. 

LinkedIn has only 321 followers

, indicating minimal organic social investment. 

Facebook shows 1,383 likes with only 23 talking about this

 — the page is effectively dormant. 

BBB accreditation dates to September 1993 with an A+ rating

, which they lean on heavily in credentialing language. The BBB complaint log, however, contains documented job-delay and post-installation leak issues, including 

a November 2025 complaint where work remained unfinished after a month, with missing gutter components and active leaks going into a rain event.

 No Facebook Ad Library activity was detectable from standard search, suggesting limited or no paid social spend.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Amos Exteriors runs on WordPress with PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — an aging stack. jQuery 1.11.1 is a 2014 release; this signals technical debt that likely affects Core Web Vitals. They have built out a geographic landing page structure (e.g., [amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)), which is a legitimate local SEO play and worth noting. 

Their GAF Master Elite, James Hardie Contractor Alliance, and Gaco Western certifications

 generate legitimate backlinks from manufacturer directories. Dual-location structure (Indy + Lafayette) means they're spreading domain authority across two GBP footprints. Blog content is thin to non-existent based on site structure. No schema signals observed beyond basic business listing markup.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current AI engine behavior (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) for queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," and "top roofing contractor Greenwood Indiana": Amos Exteriors surfaces in AI-generated results due primarily to two factors — the sheer volume of their 3,046 Google reviews and their 54-year operating history, both of which AI models weight heavily as trust proxies. They are likely cited by name in general "top Indianapolis roofers" answers. However, their Yelp 2.5-star rating and absence from recent local press create citation gaps in more nuanced AI answers that cross-reference multiple platforms. Raptor's 5.0 rating at 664 reviews is a cleaner citation signal for quality-focused queries; the gap is raw volume, not legitimacy.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,046 vs 664) dominates local pack rankings and AI citation frequency; 54-year brand history generates institutional trust with older demographics; dual-location footprint (Lafayette) captures a market Raptor does not touch; full exterior services (windows, siding, masonry) create larger average ticket and cross-sell loops; 

dedicated insurance claims specialists

 are a structured, scalable storm-restoration sales process.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** 5.0 vs 4.9 at meaningful volume is a real differentiator for quality-first buyers; zero Google reviews in the last 90 days on Amos's profile is a serious warning sign of a stalled or manipulated review program — Raptor's recency is clean; owner response rate of zero reinforces that Amos leadership is disengaged from the customer conversation post-sale; the BBB complaint trail and Yelp score create a verifiable credibility gap Raptor can exploit in sales conversations.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Amos has a Director of Marketing and a Marketing Manager on payroll yet is generating zero recent Google reviews and running what appears to be a dormant social presence — the marketing investment is not producing measurable digital output, which means their 3,046-review moat is slowly eroding while Raptor's is still being built.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **Geographic landing page architecture.** Amos has built individual URL slugs for each suburb they serve (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, etc.). This is the correct local SEO structure and each page is an AEO citation opportunity. Cameron should audit whether Raptor's current site matches this depth — one thin homepage is not enough to compete for suburb-level AI and search queries.

2. **GAF Master Elite positioning.** 

The GAF Master Elite designation is held by only a small percentage of roofing companies nationwide.

 Amos leads with this credential prominently. If Raptor holds or can pursue this certification, it belongs in every ad headline, GBP description, and AI-optimized FAQ — it is a specific, verifiable differentiator that AI models cite.

3. **Monitor the review velocity gap.** Amos at 0 new reviews in 90 days on a 3,046-review profile is either a platform flag, a process breakdown, or a canvassing team that is no longer closing into review asks. Cameron should track this monthly — if the gap holds, it creates a legitimate "most reviewed AND most recent" narrative for Raptor to own in local pack positioning within 6–12 months at current trajectory.

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**
**TO:** Ownership, Amos Exteriors
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Offensive — Raptor Roofing
**DATE:** May 7, 2026

---

**SITUATION ASSESSMENT**

We have a structural advantage that Raptor cannot replicate overnight: 

Amos Exteriors has been a trusted name in Central Indiana since 1971, with more than 50 years of experience as a family-owned and operated company.

 

Raptor, by contrast, only rebranded from "Raptor Restoration" as recently as January 2025.

 

They have been serving Indianapolis only since 2016.

 We have 3,059 Google reviews at 4.9 stars. They have 666 at 5.0. The volume gap is our weapon. Here is how we use it.

---

**PART 1 — THREE SPECIFIC VULNERABILITIES TO EXPLOIT**

**Vulnerability 1: Their brand identity is less than 18 months old.**


Raptor Restoration rebranded to Raptor Roofing in January 2025, describing it as a "strategic transformation" accompanied by an entirely new website.

 That means a significant portion of their review equity and online authority was built under a different brand name. Homeowners searching for accountability and longevity will not find a 50-year track record — they will find a company that changed its name last year. This is exploitable in every channel where we can speak to tenure.

**Vulnerability 2: Public post-installation complaints exist on the BBB record — and they show a pattern.**


A BBB complaint against Raptor states that after a new roof was installed, broken boards and unsecured end caps were visible, and after two weeks the customer still had not received a response or a fix.

 This is their exact brand promise — "we don't outsource accountability" — cracking in public. 

Meanwhile, our own BBB record contains a complaint about a siding project where an undersized crew took over a week to complete 80% of the work, damaged insulation foam was not repaired as contracted, and gutters were not scheduled — causing the home to experience rain without gutters installed.

 We are not clean here either. We must internally address these execution gaps before we go on offense, or we hand Raptor the same ammunition.

**Vulnerability 3: They are entirely dependent on Google LSA and Google Ads — a single-channel lead structure with no off-platform loyalty layer.**
Their lead flow lives or dies on Google's auction. 

In LSA, higher bids win placement. If competitors outbid them, Google hands them the spot. There is no creative workaround — you either match the market rate or accept lower visibility.

 They have built no documented referral program, no neighborhood-level organic presence outside sponsored posts, and no second-channel CRM to re-engage past customers. **Their growth is rented, not owned.** That is a ceiling we can break through.

---

**PART 2 — THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: "Since 1971" Conquesting on Google LSA and Search**


Amos Exteriors is a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor, locally owned and operated since 1971, with A+ standing with the BBB, NRCA membership, and IAA membership.

 We weaponize every one of those credentials directly against Raptor's freshly minted brand. Launch Google Ads campaigns targeting the exact keyword clusters Raptor bids on — "roofing company Greenwood IN," "Center Grove roofer," "roof replacement Indianapolis" — with ad copy that reads: *"50+ Years. 3,000+ Reviews. GAF Master Elite. Amos Exteriors — The Name Indianapolis Has Trusted Since Before Raptor Existed."* 

On LSA specifically, if their budgets are capped, Google feeds open-budget competitors first — so we run uncapped LSA budgets during peak storm weeks and outrank them for position at the exact moment homeowners are searching.

 Budget authorization needed: minimum $8,000/month in combined LSA and Search for 90 days.

**Campaign 2: Greenwood and Center Grove Neighborhood Takeover**
Raptor has planted their community flag specifically in Greenwood and Center Grove through local sponsorships. **We go into those zip codes and make them ours at the street level.** Deploy door-hanger campaigns across the 46142, 46143, and 46077 zip codes featuring real Amos customer photos, the 3,059-review count, and a QR code linking to a neighborhood-specific landing page. Simultaneously, run hyper-targeted Meta and Nextdoor ads in those exact communities with the creative angle: *"Your Neighbors' Roofer for 50 Years — Not 9."* Sponsor the same youth sports leagues, school events, and community organizations Raptor is sponsoring — outspend them or co-sponsor to dilute their exclusivity claim. A $2,500/month community investment in those two markets will create visible brand friction they cannot ignore.

**Campaign 3: The "3,059 Reasons" Review Superiority Campaign**


Fresh reviews drive sustained LSA visibility. Businesses maintaining steady review flow stay visible, while those letting reviews go stale see sudden drops in lead volume. Reviews display directly in the LSA interface, making them doubly crucial for both ranking and conversion.

 generate legitimate backlinks from manufacturer directories. Dual-location structure (Indy + Lafayette) means they're spreading domain authority across two GBP footprints. ## 1. Who They Are



Gene Judd is the owner and president of Bone Dry Roofing, which he opened in 1989 starting with a truck and a garage office in Speedway, Indiana.

, giving them scale to generate review volume and repeat keyword coverage that smaller operators cannot match. ## 1. Who They Are



Founded in the spring of 2012 by Daniel Young and Ryan Martlage

, Kingdom Roofing Systems is a multi-location Central Indiana exterior remodeling contractor.

, giving them dual top-tier manufacturer credentialing that is a core pillar of their pitch.

## 2. Estimated Scale

**Confidence: medium.** 

PitchBook lists Kingdom Roofing Systems at 40 total employees.

 An older profile from Zionsville Monthly reported closer to 30, suggesting modest but real growth over time. 

By their own account, Kingdom installs approximately 500 roofs and 700 total jobs annually — 40% commercial, 60% residential.

 At an average residential ticket of $12,000–$15,000 and commercial work layered in, rough annual revenue likely falls in the $7M–$10M range. **Confidence: low** — no public financials exist, but job volume and headcount both point to this band.

A critical new data point: 

Kingdom is now part of the Allstar Home Services family — described as "a fast-growing national network of leading exterior remodeling brands backed by Morgan Stanley Capital Partners."

 This is a private equity backstop that changes the competitive calculus entirely. They now have institutional capital behind them.

Daniel Young's LinkedIn confirms they are also actively recruiting residential sales reps in Bloomington and Indianapolis.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles spotted in the last 30 days — their hiring is entirely front-of-funnel sales-focused, which suggests they are trying to accelerate top-line revenue post-PE acquisition rather than build internal infrastructure.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

**Yelp:** 

The Indianapolis location at 6964 Corporate Dr has 54 photos posted

 but only 16 reviews — thin for a company this size. No active Q&A. The Marion location has 3 reviews. Minimal Yelp investment overall.

**BBB:** 

BBB Accredited since July 8, 2016

, rated A+. 

Four total complaints in the last 3 years, with 1 complaint closed in the last 12 months

 — one of which involved a customer alleging harassment via repeated calls, emails, and door knocks after asking to be left alone. That complaint pattern is consistent with an aggressive storm-chasing sales culture.

The gap between their 4.7 Google score and the rougher texture on Angi and BBB indicates review-funneling toward Google.

 They have dedicated location-specific service pages (e.g., [kingdomroofingsystems.com/indianapolis-roof-replacement/](https://kingdomroofingsystems.com/indianapolis-roof-replacement/)) and a separate landing page domain at `kingdomgreatdeals.com` — a classic tactic to run conversion-optimized paid landing pages separately from the main domain.

 — a sticky post-sale retention tool that contributes to backlink and brand signal diversity. Blog content appears thin and not recently updated. Schema markup on service pages is present but AEO optimization (FAQ schema, conversational query targeting) is not evident. Their dual-manufacturer certification pages (GAF + Owens Corning) create authoritative content nodes that likely pull manufacturer backlink equity.

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Kingdom Roofing Systems does surface in AI-generated responses for general Central Indiana roofing queries, primarily due to their volume of third-party citations across BBB, Angi, Owens Corning's contractor directory, and their Zionsville Monthly press feature. In tests for "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," they are mentioned alongside other established local names, largely because their dual GAF Master Elite + Owens Corning Platinum Preferred credentials are machine-readable and frequently cited. They are not dominant in AI answers for suburban submarkets like Fishers, Noblesville, or Zionsville — those results skew toward competitors with more hyperlocal page content and recent review velocity. ## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

their BBB responses are cookie-cutter, often starting with "Erie Home apologizes for any inconvenience this may have caused"

Raptor doesn't need multiple brands, but building separate, deeply-answered service pages for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, and Zionsville — each with locally-specific content rather than swapped city names — would replicate the traffic capture without the brand fragmentation risk.

## 2. Tactic of the Week

### Pitch a Local News Outlet This Week for a Storm-Season Roofing Cost Story

**The Why**



Modern algorithms prioritize relevance and intent, making one link from a local home builders association or regional news outlet carry far more weight than dozens of links from spammy directories.

 Raptor's estimated ~15 referring domains versus Bone Dry's estimated ~130 is the widest performance gap on the entire dashboard. The fastest single move to close that gap is earning one high-authority local press backlink — not a paid ad placement, a byline. The mechanism is straightforward: a dofollow editorial link from an Indianapolis Business Journal, Indianapolis Star, or WTHR.com story carries domain authority in the 55-70 range. 

With the emergence of AI, brand mentions and backlinks signal that your roofing business is credible, active, and trusted by the community

 — which means the same coverage that earns a backlink also seeds the named-entity data that Perplexity, Google AI Overview, and ChatGPT draw on when constructing their recommended-contractor lists.

The timing is perfect. 

The national average roof replacement now costs $19,800, and homeowners are getting sticker shock and asking AI to find the best roofer.

 Every local reporter covering consumer spending is looking for a credentialed local contractor who can explain why roofing costs jumped and what homeowners should do right now. You are that source.

**The How**

1. Write a 150-word expert pitch today — not a press release. Address it to the consumer or business reporter at IBJ, Indianapolis Star, and WTHR's digital desk by name. 2. In the pitch, offer three specific data points: (a) the material cost increase due to shingle manufacturer price hikes, (b) one or two hyperlocal hail events from the 2025 season that drove demand, and (c) a "three questions every homeowner should ask a roofer before getting an estimate" hook — the kind of utility content editors can turn into a listicle or sidebar.

3. Offer a 20-minute phone interview, a job-site photo opportunity, and a quote for attribution. Propose that Raptor Roofing be identified by name and city in the piece.

4. If the reporter bites, confirm in your follow-up that the company website URL (raptorroofing.com) is included in the online version of the story. That URL is the backlink. Do not accept print-only placement; the digital placement is the SEO asset.

5. If IBJ or the Star passes, escalate to Angie's List editorial (DA 75+) or NARI Indianapolis chapter news, both of which accept contractor-sourced expert commentary. 

Roofing companies can earn backlinks by publishing helpful guides, supporting community events, joining trade organizations, sharing project stories, and building partnerships.



**Success Metric — 30 days**

**Updated: April 26, 2025 | Prepared for Cameron Blakely**

## 1. Who They Are



Aaron Christy founded Indy Roof & Restoration in 2018.

, and 

Greg Russell serves as Operations Manager per BBB records.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

 — a fraction of their 2,153 Google reviews. That gap is not accidental; it's textbook review-funneling. Their Google funnel is highly optimized; their Yelp profile is essentially untended, which means any homeowner who starts their search on Yelp sees a thin, mixed signal.

 another discrepancy vs. Google 4.9.

they have been accredited since July 2019

active BBB complaints include allegations of offering repair in exchange for review removal and failure to address property damage caused during a project

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

[indyroofandrestoration.com](https://indyroofandrestoration.com) is a purpose-built SEO asset.

 — that is a structured content governance stack designed specifically to satisfy Google's E-E-A-T signals and improve AEO eligibility. ZoomInfo confirms they run Facebook Pixel, Facebook Web Custom Audiences, and WordPress

 — standard paid social retargeting infrastructure.

, which are credible backlink and trust-signal sources for roofing-specific SEO. Their domain has age (2018–2019 origin), content depth, and structured policies that give them a meaningful authority edge over most local competitors.

No live AI search was available in this pull due to search-limit constraints. However, based on observable signals: their domain's E-E-A-T infrastructure — 

including a published Fact-Checking Policy and Corrections & Updates Policy

 — is exactly the schema-adjacent content signaling that Gemini, ChatGPT Browse, and Perplexity use to vet citation-worthy sources. Combined with 2,153 Google reviews, a WISH-TV local press feature, and BBB A+ accreditation, they are almost certainly being cited in AI responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" queries. Raptor's current AEO exposure on those queries is not yet documented and should be audited immediately against theirs. This is the fastest-moving gap in the competitive set.

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (2,153 vs. 664) dominates every Google Local Pack ranking signal and almost certainly drives their AI citation frequency. Their editorial policy infrastructure is ahead of anything most residential roofers in the market have built. Their insurance-claim navigation positioning gives them a clear hook for storm-damage leads that Raptor does not explicitly own.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 star rating vs. 4.9 is a real differentiator at the premium end of the market — particularly with higher-income homeowners in Carmel, Zionsville, and Westfield who read reviews closely. IRR publicly commits 1% of all revenue to Indiana charities including Habitat for Humanity, Toys for Tots, Isiah117, and Fountains of Hope.

 This is a documented, named pledge — not a vague "we give back" line — and it converts into local press, Nextdoor goodwill, and referral credibility with real estate agents. Raptor should formalize and name any existing charitable activity with the same specificity.
