**CONFIDENTIAL — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Ownership, Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**DATE:** May 14, 2025
**RE:** 90-Day Offensive Strategy — Taking Market Share from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION BRIEF**

We hold 2,195 reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor holds 671 at 5.0. On paper, they have a star-rating edge. In volume — the metric that drives LSA rank, consumer trust, and market perception — we dominate them by more than 3-to-1. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and the number of reviews.

 That asymmetry is our most powerful weapon and we are not using it aggressively enough. Here is how we change that this quarter.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Single-Channel Lead Dependency**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

The contractors getting crushed right now all have the same profile: they built their entire lead generation around one paid channel. When that channel gets more expensive and less effective, they have nowhere to go except spend more.

 

Roofing LSA costs now run $55–$90 per lead, with storm damage queries hitting $150 or more in active weather zones.

 **Raptor is renting leads from Google. We need to make that rent feel unbearable by owning the organic and earned channels they are ignoring.**

**Weakness 2: Thin Geographic Roots Outside Center Grove and Greenwood**

Raptor has deliberately concentrated its community identity in Greenwood and Center Grove. That is smart micro-positioning — but it is also a ceiling. It leaves Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Avon, Brownsburg, and Mooresville comparatively uncontested from their brand. Their own website lists these markets but offers no localized content, no neighborhood-specific proof, no community ties. **Their brand identity is geographically narrow. We can establish dominant local presence in six surrounding submarkets before they react.**

**Weakness 3: A 5.0 Rating Is a Trap — And Their Volume Gap Is Catastrophic**

671 reviews is a thin foundation for a "premium" brand claim in a metro of two million people. A 5.0 with 671 reviews statistically signals a brand that is either early-stage or one that aggressively manages negative reviews out of public view. 

91% of homeowners rely on online reviews before choosing a contractor.

 When a homeowner compares Raptor's 671 reviews to our 2,195, the psychological authority gap is irreversible at the point of decision. **We must make that comparison unavoidable in our ad creative and landing pages.** Additionally, Raptor's brand "accountability" messaging has no third-party verification layer — no GuildQuality profile with external data, no volume of cross-platform reviews. Our depth of proof across platforms is superior; we are simply not weaponizing it.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "2,000+ Reasons" — Volume Dominance Ad Blitz**

Launch a Google Ads and Meta campaign directly targeting Greenwood, Center Grove, Carmel, and Fishers zip codes with a single creative hook: **"2,000+ families in Central Indiana trusted us with their roof. See why."** The ad links to neighborhood-specific landing pages showing real job photos, real homeowner names, and review counts by zip code. This is not a comparison ad — it does not name Raptor. It simply makes our social proof so visible and localized that Raptor's numbers look thin by comparison. Run Performance Max alongside standard search to capture the full funnel. 

Maximize the Google Business Profile with weekly updates, real job photos, accurate service listings, and every review responded to within 24 hours. Businesses with active GBPs saw 28% more discovery search views within 90 days.



**Campaign 2: Nextdoor + Neighborhood Facebook Group Infiltration in Center Grove and Greenwood**

This is their home turf. We take it. Assign two dedicated field marketers to saturate Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor with genuine project posts — before/after photos, real customer names, hyperlocal testimonials. Simultaneously, run Nextdoor Neighborhood Ads in these exact zip codes. 

By targeting specific neighborhoods, especially those where you are already working, you create geographic relevance and social proof. Unlike shared leads from third-party providers, you are not competing with multiple other roofers for the same prospect.

 Every crew truck in those neighborhoods gets a door hanger dropped on adjacent homes. Cost per lead for this channel is a fraction of LSA. **We do not need to outspend Raptor in their backyard. We need to out-show them.**

**Campaign 3: AI Search and GBP Domination Play**

Raptor's website content is thin on educational depth. Ours needs to be the resource Google AI and ChatGPT cite when homeowners ask about Indianapolis roofing. Immediately commission 12 location-specific blog articles targeting: "best roofers in Carmel IN," "hail damage roof claim Greenwood IN," "how long does a roof replacement take in Indianapolis," and equivalent queries for every submarket Raptor claims but doesn't own. 

When ChatGPT or Google AI Mode recommends a contractor, it pulls from websites that answer real questions. "How much does a furnace replacement cost in Charlotte?" beats "We provide quality HVAC service" every single time.

 Pair this with a dedicated Google Business Profile posting schedule — one post every three days, every post geotagged, every post with a real job photo.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a hyper-targeted LSA and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on Raptor's branded adjacent keywords — "Raptor Roofing reviews," "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis," "Raptor Roofing vs" — and route that traffic to a landing page titled: "Comparing Indianapolis Roofers? Here's What 2,195 Reviews Look Like."**

The page shows no competitor names. It shows our review volume, our cross-platform presence, our years in market since 2018, our BBB A+ standing, and a side-by-side of what 671 reviews versus 2,195 reviews actually means in terms of completed jobs and homeowner confidence. 

There is a fixed number of LSA leads in every roofing market, influenced by demand, seasonality, and competition.

 Every lead we intercept from a homeowner researching Raptor is a lead that costs Raptor money — they paid to generate that consumer's awareness, and we convert it.

**Cameron should be uncomfortable not because we are attacking his brand. He should be uncomfortable because we are making his review gap the centerpiece of every homeowner's decision — and he cannot fix 671 versus 2,195 in 90 days.**

This is where we win.

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use only. Recommend immediate budget alignment meeting within 5 business days.*

snapshots.raptor_actions:
**Launch a "Insurance Coverage Audit" lead magnet this week targeting the 2005-2015 housing stock in Greenwood and Center Grove, before SPG turns its Roofing Contractor #92 ranking into paid creative.**

SPG just got a national third-party credential they can wave around (#92 on the 2025 Top 100, up from #128). Trying to out-credential them is a losing game we don't need to play this quarter. The asymmetric counter is to own the single highest-intent conversation no one in this market is having at scale: the RCV-to-ACV cliff and the RPS endorsements insurers are quietly slipping into renewals on roofs as young as 10 years. Greenwood and Center Grove housing stock is sitting right in the 10-20 year sweet spot, which means tens of thousands of homeowners in our service area are about to discover their policy pays half of what they think it does — and the contractor who tells them first wins the relationship before there's even a storm.

Execution this week: build a one-page offer ("Free 15-Minute Insurance Coverage Check — we read your declarations page and inspect your roof, no obligation"), wire it to a dedicated landing page with a Calendly slot, and push it through three channels by Friday: (1) a $1,500 geofenced Meta campaign targeting homeowners 35+ in the 46142/46143/46143 ZIPs, (2) a door-hanger drop on 500 homes in two target subdivisions with the RPS one-pager attached, and (3) an email to the past-customer list asking them to forward to neighbors. The script for reps is the moat — one hour of training, one laminated cheat sheet covering RCV vs ACV vs RPS, percentage-based deductibles. Most competitors are not having this conversation; SPG, Bone Dry, and Amos are still selling shingles.

Success metric this week: 25 booked coverage-check appointments and 8 inspections completed. Track close rate separately — these should run hotter than cold leads because we're showing up as an advocate, not a vendor.

---

**Deploy review-request automation across SMS and email tied to job completion, with a goal of closing the velocity gap on Indy Roof & Restoration (+76/30d) and Amos (+99/30d) within 90 days.**

Here's the uncomfortable number: at +17 reviews in the last 30 days, we are being out-paced 4-to-1 by Amos and 4.5-to-1 by Indy Roof in raw review velocity. Our 5.0 average is the prettiest in the top 10, but Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode are now surfacing one to three businesses by name, and the Roofing Webmasters data shows multi-platform review presence is the single strongest correlator with AI citation. We are leaving citations on the table every week we don't compound. Worse, Indy Roof just published a self-serving "Top 10 Roofing Companies in Indianapolis for 2026" listicle ranking themselves #1 on the strength of their review volume — that's the exact ammo AI systems will scrape and cite.

Execution this week: stand up a review request automation in whatever CRM/comms stack we're already running (NiceJob, Podium, BirdEye, or even just a Zapier-to-Twilio build if budget is tight — under $400/month either way). Trigger: job marked complete in the field. Sequence: SMS at 2 hours post-completion with a direct Google review link, email at 24 hours with the same link plus Facebook and Yelp options, second SMS at 72 hours only if no review posted. Audit Yelp and Facebook profiles in parallel — if either has under 50 reviews, route 30% of the asks there instead of Google to thicken the multi-platform footprint AI is rewarding.

Success metric: hit +30 Google reviews in the next 30 days (nearly doubling current velocity) and add a minimum of 15 reviews split across Yelp and Facebook in the same window. The compounding math gets us past Trojan and Richmond on volume by end of Q2 while widening the quality gap.

---

**Sign a hyperlocal community-anchor partnership this week that Bone Dry's 17-location footprint can never authentically match.**

Bone Dry is a real long-term threat — 30 years of brand recall in this market, 2,400+ reviews on the main location, Owens Corning Platinum and CertainTeed ShingleMaster both. We don't out-spend them on awareness. We out-local them. Bone Dry is headquartered in Indy but operates Colorado to Florida; they cannot credibly be "Greenwood's roofer" no matter how much they spend, and that's the gap to exploit while we're still small enough to be specific.

Execution this week: lock in one anchor partnership in Greenwood or Center Grove that puts the Raptor name in front of homeowners in a non-advertising context. Three candidates to pursue by Friday: (1) title sponsor for Greenwood Freedom Festival or the next Center Grove HS athletic season — even a $5K-$10K commitment gets logo placement and PA reads to thousands of exactly our demo, (2) a co-branded "free roof check before winter" event with a respected local insurance broker who is also seeing the ACV/RPS issue blow up at claim time and wants an honest contractor to refer to, or (3) a standing relationship with two or three top-producing Johnson County realtors to be their default pre-listing roof inspection contractor (free 10-minute inspections in exchange for being the recommended roofer at closing). Option 2 is the highest-leverage because it directly compounds the insurance-audit play in Action 1.

Success metric this week: one signed partnership agreement (verbal commitment + follow-up email is fine) and a calendar date for the first joint touchpoint within 30 days. Measure downstream by tagged lead source over the following 90 days — target 15 partnership-sourced leads in Q2.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**7301 E 46th St, Indianapolis, IN 46226 | [amosexteriors.com](https://www.amosexteriors.com)**
*Refreshed: Tuesday, May 20, 2025*

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company serving homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated since 1971, they hold GAF Master Elite Contractor status and maintain an A+ rating with the BBB, along with memberships in the NRCA and Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They now operate locations in both Indianapolis and Lafayette, IN,

 and their service line extends well beyond roofing — encompassing siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, and commercial exteriors — making them a full-envelope competitor, not just a roofing shop.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach estimates approximately 57 employees and $28.6 million in annual revenue

 (**confidence: low** — third-party modeled data). 

Prospeo pegs headcount at 51–100 employees

 with a separate revenue estimate of $12M. The wide spread between data sources ($12M–$28.6M) is typical for a company this size that doesn't publish financials. The most operationally meaningful data point: 

Amos received an SBA PPP loan of $584,200, retaining 40 jobs,

 which suggests a W-2 headcount floor of ~40 at time of application. 

Their sales department alone is reportedly led by a Director of Sales and includes 21 employees,

 signaling a heavily sales-rep-forward staffing model. Revenue estimate: $15M–$22M. **Confidence: medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



ZoomInfo flags an active search for an Estimator and Project Manager

 in Indianapolis. 

Their careers page is actively recruiting Home Improvement Sales Consultants, with reps expected to run company-provided leads as well as generate their own referrals.

 The more strategically notable signal: 

ZipRecruiter shows a posting for a Team Lead, Field Marketing

 — meaning they are building out a canvassing infrastructure with supervisory structure, not just adding bodies. 

BBB lists a Director of Marketing (Bruce McClain) and a Marketing Manager (Jana Perrott)

 as named contacts, indicating an in-house marketing function that most competitors their size don't maintain. No digital marketing, SEO, or paid media specialist roles were publicly visible in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The Google/Yelp gap here is stark and exploitable. Amos carries 3,094 Google reviews at 4.9 stars but 

holds only a 2.5-star rating on Yelp

 across 

19 Yelp reviews

 — a classic review-funneling setup where satisfied customers are directed exclusively to Google and Yelp is left unmanaged. 

BBB accreditation dates to 9/19/1993

 with an A+ rating, and their BBB page is well-maintained with named contacts. 

Facebook shows 1,383 page likes with 23 talking about the page

 — thin engagement for a company this size, suggesting Facebook is used as a credibility placeholder, not an active community or paid media channel. No active Facebook Ad Library campaigns were surfaced in the search results. On Angi (formerly Angie's List), they hold multiple positive reviews and 

have won the Angie's List Super Service Award.



---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, WP Rocket, Open Graph, and Nginx

 — a WordPress build with basic on-page SEO tooling in place. They have built out a dense location and service-area page architecture: 

service area pages explicitly name Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Geist, Plainfield, Avon, Speedway, Broad Ripple, Greenwood, Franklin, Mooresville, Anderson, and Greenfield.

 This is aggressive local SEO page sprawl — they are hunting every suburb Cameron targets. However, 

their core tech stack runs on jQuery 1.11.1 and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that suggests slow page speed and poor Core Web Vitals, a compounding weakness as Google increasingly weights page experience. No evidence of structured data / schema markup beyond what Yoast auto-generates. No local press backlinks were surfaced. Their AEO posture is thin — no FAQ schema, no "best of" citations in local media, and no visible content designed to answer long-tail conversational queries.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Amos Exteriors is a credible AI citation candidate due to their review volume and 54-year operating history, but their generative engine visibility is structurally weak. Their website runs on aging infrastructure with minimal structured data, no evident third-party editorial coverage (local press, industry publications), and no content formatted for AI extraction. 

Brands are 6.5x more likely to be cited in AI answers through third-party sources than through their own domains,

 and 

domain authority signals — specifically external referring domains — correlate strongly with AI Overview appearances.

 Amos has neither. In manual review of AI-generated responses to prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "top roofing contractor near Carmel Indiana," Amos surfaces due to raw review volume but is not consistently named first or described with specific differentiating language. Their 54-year history and GAF Master Elite status are the two attributes most likely to pull AI citations if they were properly marked up and echoed in third-party sources — they are not doing this deliberately.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,094 vs. 673), brand age and legacy trust signals, broader service line (windows, doors, masonry, painting, commercial), dedicated in-house marketing staff, and a multi-location footprint now extending to Lafayette. **Where Raptor beats Amos:** Perfect 5.0 rating vs. 4.9 (meaningful in AI ranking logic and conversion psychology); zero accountability-outsourcing in the service model vs. Amos's canvasser-driven, high-volume sales rep structure that [per Indeed reviews] sends reps on unqualified 1.5-hour-drive leads; and a cleaner, more premium brand identity vs. Amos's volume-market positioning. **Most exploitable weakness:** 

Inside reviews describe leads that are "usually long drives" with reps traveling 1.5 hours each way for unqualified appointments, and canvassers setting appointments where homeowners "either don't know you're coming or don't understand why you're there"

 — a sales ops and customer experience problem that Raptor's high-touch, accountable model directly counters in the market.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **Dedicated location/service-area page architecture.** Amos has a page for nearly every suburb in central Indiana targeting "[City] + roofing" queries. Raptor should build equivalent depth — specifically for Carmel, Fishers, Zionsville, Noblesville, and Greenwood — with city-specific content, project photos, and schema markup that Amos is not executing properly. Do it cleaner and faster.

2. **Named marketing leadership as a credibility signal.** 

Amos lists a Director of Marketing and a Marketing Manager by name on their BBB profile.

 This is a small but real trust signal in B2C home services. Cameron should ensure Raptor's BBB and Google Business profiles list marketing/leadership contacts and use that visibility to create content authority (op-eds, local press quotes, home improvement columns) that Amos is not generating.

3. **Field marketing team-lead structure.** The Team Lead, Field Marketing posting on ZipRecruiter signals Amos is scaling a structured canvassing operation with management hierarchy. Watch whether this translates into heavier presence at Lowes/Home Depot parking lot events, HOA outreach, or neighborhood drop campaigns in Raptor's core zip codes — and prepare a counter-program that emphasizes Raptor's referral-first, non-canvassing reputation as a premium differentiator.

## Bone Dry Roofing - Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard**
**Refreshed: Tuesday, May 20, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

Owner Gene Judd grew up the son of a roofing contractor in Illinois, graduated from Indiana University, and stayed in central Indiana to build the company.

 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 20 businesses in eight states, including 11 Midwest locations plus Bone Dry Roofing West, Florida, Commercial, Roof One, QRS, Ravlin's, RCV, and Gary's Roofing

 — making them a regional roll-up operator, not a pure local competitor. Their core identity is volume-driven "peace of mind" service backed by deep manufacturer relationships; 

they hold Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor and CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster Applicator status.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



As of their 2023 Residential Contractor of the Year profile, Bone Dry reported 500 employees company-wide, with a scope of 81% residential and 19% commercial.

 

LeadIQ pegged company-wide headcount at approximately 240 employees as of March 2026

 — indicating meaningful variance across data sources. **Confidence: medium** (estimates range from 240 to 500 depending on whether subsidiary headcount is consolidated). On revenue: 

ZoomInfo notes that the hiring of a new CFO and COO came "on the heels of Bone Dry Roofing's financial performance in 2023 that included revenue of over $183 million."

 

Of the $121M reported in 2022, approximately $36 million (30%) came from the Indianapolis office alone.

 **Revenue confidence: medium** — the Indianapolis location is likely a $40-50M+ operation on its own by 2025 based on trajectory.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active and broad. 

There are currently 78 open jobs at Bone Dry Roofing Inc., with 21 of those based in Indianapolis.

 Roles posted on ZipRecruiter and Indeed include: 

Assistant Production Manager

; 

Systems Analyst for business operations, noted as being in "growth mode"

; 

Division Manager (Roofing), responsible for overall management of sales and production

; and 

Home Solution Specialists (in-home sales reps) and Commercial Service Technicians.

 The Systems Analyst and Division Manager postings are the ones to watch — ops-level builds like that precede market expansion pushes. No standalone marketing coordinator or CMO-level hire is currently visible in Indiana, which tracks with their in-house CMO (Matt Tyner) being tenured.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, the Indianapolis location at 7735 Winton Dr has 75 reviews

 — versus 2,422 on Google. That is a 97% review-funneling gap, the clearest sign in this market of a team that has mastered Google review capture but has done nothing to cultivate Yelp. Their Facebook presence (

825 likes, 264 people talking about it

) is active but thin for a company of their scale. The UTM parameters in their Facebook profile links (`utm_campaign=profile-link&campaign_code=BDR-DIG-ORGS-ROOF-IN-PHO-FB-202402`) show they are tracking social-to-web traffic with some discipline. 

They carry an A+ BBB rating and have won multiple Angie's List Super Service Awards.

 

They have a partnership with Indy Humane

 that generates community goodwill mentions. BBB complaints page is live but complaint volume is not alarming based on available data. No notable Reddit presence identified for the Indy location.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Bone Dry operates `bonedry.com` with a dedicated subdirectory at `bonedry.com/indianapolis/` and location-specific service pages (e.g., `bonedry.com/indianapolis/roofing/`). 

Their tech stack includes WordPress, Adobe Premiere Pro, Webpack, and Module Federation

 — a competent but not cutting-edge setup. The Indianapolis page targets head terms like "roofing contractor Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Indianapolis" with repetitive on-page copy rather than topical authority content. No evidence of a robust blog targeting long-tail question queries ("how much does a roof cost in Carmel IN," etc.) — their content investment appears shallow relative to their domain age and backlink footprint. Their multi-location architecture gives them a domain authority advantage that a single-location operator cannot easily replicate; `bonedry.com` almost certainly carries a DA of 45+ based on press coverage, Owens Corning partner links, and the [2023 Roofing Contractor Magazine profile](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing). AEO posture is not differentiated — no visible FAQ schema, no structured "ask" content targeting voice or AI-surfaced queries.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry Roofing is almost certainly named in AI answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. The combination of their volume (2,422 Google reviews), national press coverage (Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Contractor of the Year), multi-state footprint, and aged domain makes them a high-probability citation for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Their BBB A+ status and F.C. Tucker partnership (

Bone Dry is a member of F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

) generate structured third-party mentions that LLMs index heavily. However, their lack of specific suburb-level content (Zionsville, Fishers, Noblesville pages are thin or absent) creates a gap — AI answers for hyper-local prompts like "roofing company Fishers Noblesville" are less certain. Raptor should be targeting exactly those prompts with purpose-built content.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Bone Dry beats Raptor:** Review volume is not close — 2,422 vs. 673 — and that gap alone dominates Local Pack rankings and AI citation frequency. They have a named CMO (Matt Tyner), an in-house training academy (Bone Dry University), a multi-channel sales system, company-provided vehicles for reps, and a national award that functions as evergreen PR. 

Their policy of keeping a production supervisor on-site for every project's duration

 is a process differentiator that is easy to market and hard to argue against. **Where Raptor beats Bone Dry:** A 5.0 star rating versus 4.8 is a genuine differentiator at the premium tier — no sophisticated buyer reads 2,422 reviews; they filter by rating first. Raptor's accountability positioning ("we don't outsource accountability") hits directly at the most common grievance in Bone Dry's employee reviews. **Most exploitable weakness:** 

Indeed reviews score Bone Dry's management accountability at 3.3 out of 5, with employees noting that "higher up managers are not held accountable for anything" and feel "disconnected."

 That internal dysfunction surfaces in customer experience — Raptor's owner-present, single-market focus is the direct counter-positioning.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

**1. On-site production supervisor as a standard deliverable.** 

Bone Dry's policy of a production supervisor present for the entire project, with no payment taken until the customer has "expressed total agreement and satisfaction," is a process they market explicitly.

 Raptor should formalize and name an equivalent standard in all sales materials and on the website — make it a named commitment, not just a verbal promise.

**2. The F.C. Tucker referral partnership.** 

Bone Dry is embedded in F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

 — an inbound referral channel from one of Indy's dominant real estate brands. Raptor should identify equivalent real estate brokerage, insurance agent, and property management partnership channels that Bone Dry is not already locked into. These are pre-qualified, high-intent homeowner referrals that bypass paid search entirely.

**3. Formalized veteran and first responder discount as a brand signal.** 

Bone Dry has partnered with Military.com and pledged support for the veteran community

 as a recruiting and PR tool. 

Their discount program covers military members, veterans, senior citizens, first responders, teachers, and healthcare professionals.

 Raptor should either match this with a cleaner, more premium-positioned version (fewer categories, stronger guarantee) or own a distinct community vertical Bone Dry has not claimed.

**Refreshed:** Tuesday, May 20, 2025 | **Subject:** [indyroofandrestoration.com](https://indyroofandrestoration.com)

---

## 1. Who They Are



Aaron Christy founded Indy Roof & Restoration in 2018.

 

The company is led by founder Aaron Christy and COO Adam Kaminski

, with 

Greg Russell serving as Operations Manager per BBB records.

 Their core identity is storm restoration and insurance advocacy — 

they lean heavily on working with insurance companies and positioning themselves as trusted by real estate agents and residential and commercial customers throughout central Indiana.

 Structurally they operate as a full exterior GC: 

roofs, gutters, siding, interior work, and anything else damaged during a storm.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale

**Confidence: medium.** Multiple data sources converge in the 25–50 employee range. 

Clodura.AI lists them at 11–50 employees total

, while 

SignalHire estimates approximately 30 employees.

 

Growjo estimates annual revenue of $10.9M with 47 employees

 — the most aggressive estimate in the dataset, though Growjo skews high. 

Prospeo pegs annual revenue closer to $2.4M

, which appears to undercount significantly given their review velocity and GC scope. A $5M–$10M ARR range is the most defensible read. 

Growjo did note they grew employee count by 38% in the prior year

 — a meaningful signal regardless of which revenue figure is correct.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Their 

careers page actively solicits "driven individuals" emphasizing personal and professional growth

, and 

commission-based Field Inspectors are a standing open role, with the primary function of roof and exterior inspections and guiding homeowners through the insurance process.

 

Indeed also shows an active Water & Mold Restoration Sales posting, requiring experience in water damage restoration or mitigation sales

 — a signal they are pushing deeper into the interior restoration/mitigation vertical. 

Clodura's org chart shows a dedicated Marketing Director (Nick Segar) and Sales Manager (Daniel Ralston)

, both titles suggesting they have invested in internal marketing infrastructure, not just outsourced SEO. No VP- or Director-level ops hire detected in the last 30 days on ZipRecruiter or Indeed specific to Indy Roof.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

The platform gap here is real and exploitable. 

Yelp has placed a Consumer Alert on their business page flagging abnormal activity or attempts to mislead consumers

 — a damaging signal that Yelp's algorithm has flagged suspected review manipulation. Against 2,202 Google reviews, 

Yelp shows only 28 reviews

 — a 79:1 ratio that is a textbook review-funneling pattern. 

Facebook shows 4,777 page likes and an 86% recommendation rate across 48 reviews

 — again a fraction of their Google volume. Their Facebook page is tied to the entity "INDY ROOF CO," which is a slightly different DBA and creates potential brand confusion. 

BBB-accredited since July 2019 with an A+ rating

, but the BBB complaint section contains at least one detailed narrative alleging a forged signature and cash payment irregularity from April 2025 — not yet resolved publicly at time of this brief. 

Community presence includes Brownsburg Little League Softball, Beech Grove High School Marching Band, Habitat for Humanity, and the Shelbyville Animal Shelter

, all of which generate local press and trust signals without paid placement.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture



A third-party 2026 Indianapolis roofing roundup (Stay Dry Roofing's own site) cites Indy Roof & Restoration as a strong regional company recognized for insurance advocacy and high review volume, calling them a top contender and honorable mention.

 That kind of third-party citation on a competitor's domain is a backlink signal worth watching — they are generating citation mentions even from rivals. Their website URL structure (service area pages for Carmel, Fishers, Greenwood, Brownsburg, Westfield, Zionsville per their 

careers page

) suggests a standard local SEO landing page strategy. 

ZoomInfo's tech stack shows Facebook Pixel, Facebook Web Custom Audiences, WordPress, and PHP

 — a fairly lean setup with no obvious schema-heavy CMS. No evidence of structured data investment or AEO-specific FAQ schema content surfaced. Their blog exists but is thin. The Red Rocket content subdomain (`indyroofandrestoration.redrocketcontent.com`) confirms they use Red Rocket as their SEO/content vendor, which is a local Indianapolis digital shop — not a national roofing-specialist agency.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Indy Roof & Restoration does appear in AI-generated local roundups. The Stay Dry Roofing roundup — which itself ranks in Google for Indy roofing queries — 

identifies them specifically for insurance advocacy and 24/7 emergency response, and recommends them for homeowners wanting intense insurance-claim support and mitigation services.

 That content will be scraped by LLMs and surface in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini responses to queries like "best storm damage roofer Indianapolis." However, their own domain does not appear to have AEO-optimized content (FAQ schema, structured Q&A, cited statistics) that would make them a primary source in generative answers. Their AI visibility is derivative — they show up because others write about them, not because their own content is structured for retrieval. That is a gap Raptor can exploit directly with properly structured AEO content targeting suburb-level queries (Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, Carmel).

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Sheer review volume — 2,202 vs. 673 — dominates the GBP proximity algorithm and creates an imposing social proof wall for undecided homeowners. Their insurance advocacy positioning and 24/7 emergency response branding gives them a clear lane during storm cycles. Community sponsorship visibility (Little League, high school band, Habitat) is a PR flywheel Raptor has not matched at that frequency.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 vs. 4.9 on Google — a meaningful delta at premium price points where buyers scrutinize. The Yelp Consumer Alert, the BBB complaint involving alleged forged signatures, and the 86% Facebook recommendation rate all create credible character vulnerabilities that a premium brand can exploit through contrast messaging. Raptor's "we don't outsource accountability" positioning is a direct counter-punch to a company that has documented sub-rep conduct issues.

**Most exploitable weakness:** The Yelp Consumer Alert for abnormal review activity combined with the 2025 BBB complaint about alleged forgery and cash demands gives Raptor a clean lane to run a "verified, accountable, no-surprises" campaign that doesn't need to name the competitor — the contrast speaks for itself.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Water & Mold Restoration Sales as a revenue extension.** Their active Indeed posting for this role is not accidental — interior mitigation is a high-margin adjacency that keeps them in the job longer per home. Cameron should evaluate whether Raptor has a referral partnership or upsell path into this category before Indy Roof locks up the relationships.

2. **The community sponsorship matrix.** 

Brownsburg Little League, Beech Grove Marching Band, Habitat for Humanity, Shelbyville Animal Shelter

 — these are hyper-local, low-cost, high-impression placements that generate organic social content, earned media, and Nextdoor word-of-mouth simultaneously. Raptor should map equivalent sponsorships in its primary zip codes before Indy Roof expands its footprint further north and west.

3. **Podcast and trade press positioning.** 

Aaron Christy appeared on a local podcast discussing his company's growth and the roofing industry

, and 

was quoted directly in the 2026 Roofing Contractor State of the Industry report

. That earned authority converts into AEO citations when LLMs pull industry sources. Cameron and Patrick should be pitching themselves to equivalent Indy-market podcasts and trade publications to build the same citation footprint — before Christy's voice becomes the default "Indianapolis roofer expert" in generative search results.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief — Cochran Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 2010, Cochran Exteriors has built its reputation as a central Indiana exterior remodeling contractor.

 

The company is co-owned by Ross Cochran and John Cochran

, with 

Brad Baugh serving as Brand President

 — a title that signals an Infinity Home Services-era executive layer above the founding family. 

Cochran Exteriors was acquired by Infinity Home Services in June 2022

, making it a platform company asset, not an independent operator — a fact they do not prominently advertise to consumers. 

Their service scope covers roofing, siding, windows, doors, and gutters across Indianapolis and central Indiana.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



PitchBook lists Cochran Exteriors at 43 total employees

, while 

ZoomInfo brackets them at 11–50 employees at their Indianapolis headquarters.

 **Confidence: medium.** On revenue, sources diverge: 

RocketReach estimates 2025 annual revenue at $6.8 million

, while 

CIENCE puts the range at $10–25 million.

 The spread reflects the opacity of a private subsidiary. Given the 1,187 Google review count, two physical office locations, and national Top 100 Roofing Contractor recognition, the $8–12M working estimate is most defensible. **Confidence: low.** Notably, 

Cochran Exteriors received an SBA PPP loan of $1–2 million from Regions Bank, supporting retention of 47 jobs

 — the strongest independent headcount signal available.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Two active hiring signals found on LinkedIn within recent months: 

Cochran posted for a Commercial Estimator in Indianapolis

, and 

also posted for a Residential Sales Consultant in Indianapolis.

 The Commercial Estimator post is the more strategically significant signal — it confirms they are pushing harder into the commercial segment, likely driven by Infinity Home Services' margin requirements. No marketing, ops leadership, or digital/AEO roles were identified in current postings, which is a notable gap given the scale of their review velocity.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Cochran Exteriors holds BBB Accreditation with an A+ rating

 and 

maintains two physical locations: 8461 Castlewood Dr, Indianapolis, and 48 N Emerson Ave, Suite 600, Greenwood.

 

They have been named one of the Top 100 Roofing Contractors in the nation

 — a credentialing claim they deploy across Yelp, Nextdoor, and their own site. On Yelp, they have only 54 reviews ([cochranexteriors-indianapolis-2](https://www.yelp.com/biz/cochran-exteriors-indianapolis-2)) against 1,187 on Google — a textbook review-funneling gap. The BBB complaint file is worth watching: 

at least one reviewer states "Avoid this company. They will weasel out of poor workmanship. Warranty isn't worth the paper it was written on."

 Separately, 

a BBB reviewer noted that a crew member asked them to leave a good review so he could get "stars" and a bonus

 — a structurally risky incentive model that inflates volume at the cost of authenticity. 

On Nextdoor, Cochran comes up positively recommended for roofing, windows, gutters, and siding, with customers praising the team's professionalism.

 

Their tech stack includes Google Ads Conversion Tracking and Microsoft Clarity

, confirming active paid media and on-site behavioral tracking.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Cochran's domain ([cochranexteriors.com](https://www.cochranexteriors.com)) is a 15-year-old root domain with consistent content investment. 

They maintain an active blog covering roofing, siding, and windows, positioning themselves as exterior remodeling educators.

 

They hold both Owens Corning Platinum and GAF Certified Contractor status

 — dual manufacturer certifications that generate authoritative backlinks and trust signals AI engines weight heavily. Their service area pages are geo-segmented (e.g., `/in/roofing`) and their Houzz profile lists neighborhood-specific landing pages (Castleton, Crows Nest, Rocky Ripple, Williams Creek, etc.) — a hyperlocal SEO strategy Raptor has room to counter. 

They also carry Angie's List Super Service Awards from 2012–2013 and NRCA membership

, which contribute to their backlink profile. No evidence of schema markup issues surfaced, and their use of Cloudflare and Bootstrap suggests a modern technical foundation.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Cochran Exteriors has meaningful AI citation exposure based on their profile: a 15-year-old domain, Top 100 Roofing Contractor designation, dual manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning Platinum + GAF), BBB A+ accreditation, and 1,187 Google reviews are exactly the structured trust signals that ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity pull when generating "best roofers Indianapolis" responses. Their blog content targets long-tail queries that AI engines scrape for sourcing. They are likely cited in generative results for broad Indianapolis roofing queries and storm damage/insurance claim contexts given how extensively their insurance claim assistance process is documented across review platforms. Raptor's 5.0 rating at 673 reviews is a stronger quality signal, but Cochran's volume and manufacturer credentials currently give them the AEO edge. Closing that gap requires schema-marked FAQ content, manufacturer credential pages, and press placements — none of which require ad spend.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (1,187 vs. 673), multi-location physical footprint, dual manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning Platinum + GAF), Top 100 national ranking, and a 15-year domain with hyperlocal SEO pages covering neighborhood-level queries Raptor has not yet captured.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 star rating vs. 4.7 (the difference matters at the premium price point), no corporate parent diluting the local accountability narrative, and zero credible evidence of incentivized review solicitation — which is a live liability for Cochran.

**Most exploitable weakness:** 

The documented practice of crews asking customers for reviews in exchange for "stars" and a bonus

 is a structural integrity problem that Raptor's owner-response model and authentic review velocity directly counters in any head-to-head sales conversation.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Neighborhood-level landing pages.** Cochran has built out pages targeting specific Indianapolis neighborhoods (Castleton, Rocky Ripple, Williams Creek, Wynnedale, etc.) with service-specific URL structures. These are low-cost AEO and local SEO assets. Raptor should build equivalent pages for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood with schema markup before Cochran's domain age advantage compounds further.

2. **Dual manufacturer certification as a content pillar.** 

Their Owens Corning Platinum and GAF Certified Contractor credentials

 are cited across every major directory profile and generate backlinks from manufacturer websites. If Raptor holds or can obtain comparable certifications, those credential pages need to be live, linked, and schema-marked — they are direct inputs into how generative AI ranks contractor recommendations.

3. **Commercial estimator expansion as a lead.** The active Commercial Estimator hire signals Cochran is moving budget and capacity toward commercial work. That creates a potential gap in their residential pipeline responsiveness — specifically in the suburban markets (Carmel, Fishers, Westfield) where Raptor competes on premium positioning. Cameron should monitor review cadence in those zip codes; a volume dip from Cochran in the next 60–90 days would confirm the commercial pivot is pulling attention away from residential.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief — White Oak Construction
**Updated:** Tuesday, May 20, 2025 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## 1. Who They Are



White Oak Construction Corporation has been BBB-accredited since August 1992, putting their founding at 1982 — over 43 years in business.

 

Leadership is James (Sam) Luppino, President, and David Wilson, Vice President.

 

They serve Indianapolis, Lafayette, and Evansville, Indiana, as well as Sellersburg, Kentucky

, and position themselves as a full home-improvement company (roofing, siding, windows, gutters, doors, and interior remodeling) rather than a pure-play roofing contractor — a meaningfully different competitive posture than Raptor.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



LinkedIn lists their company size as 51–200 employees, and their own LinkedIn profile claims a team of 150+ trained employees.

 **Confidence: medium** — LinkedIn self-reporting at this scale is often aspirational, and Indeed employee review counts suggest a smaller active headcount. 

With four physical locations (Indianapolis, Lafayette, Sellersburg, and Warsaw)

, they are operating as a regional multi-branch contractor. No public revenue figure exists; at ~150 employees across four branches in a multi-trade residential model, a $15M–$25M annual revenue estimate is reasonable. **Confidence: low** — no verified third-party figure available.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Indeed currently shows 5 open jobs at White Oak Construction.

 

Active postings include Event Services Associate ($16–17/hr) posted within the last 2 days, Survey Collection Specialist ($16–17/hr), and a Sales Representative role (from $100,000/year).

 

Additional listings visible on Indeed include Sales Representative roles in Sellersburg ($70K–$160K) and Lafayette (from $100K), plus Advertising Canvasser in Indianapolis ($16–17/hr).

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital-specific roles are visible. The heavy canvasser and door-to-door sales hiring signals that their primary lead-gen engine remains offline, high-touch, and field-dependent — a structurally expensive model in a post-COVID market.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

Google: 1,043 reviews at 4.2 stars (provided). Review velocity has dropped to roughly 1/week as of May 2025 — a meaningful deceleration for a company this size.



Yelp shows 75 reviews with 141 photos as of April 2026

 — no star rating surfaced in the snippet, but the presence is thin relative to their Google volume, a classic review-funneling pattern.



BBB shows an average of 3.43 out of 5 stars across 28 customer reviews

 — that is a 0.77-star gap below their Google rating, which is a significant credibility discrepancy. 

One January 2026 review describes a sales rep staying over two hours and quoting $92K for a roof, then offering to bring it to $65K on the spot

 — a high-pressure in-home sales tactic complaint that is damaging on a trust platform like BBB.



BBB complaints: 9 total in the last 3 years, with 1 complaint closed in the last 12 months.

 Angi rating is 4.7. No Facebook Ad Library data was retrievable in this refresh cycle — flag for the next pull.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

White Oak has invested meaningfully in on-site content. 

Their blog targets high-intent local queries with pages like "How to Compare Roofing Contractors in Indianapolis," covering service areas from Marion County to Brownsburg, Plainfield, Carmel, Greenwood, and Westfield.

 

They hold a GAF certified contractor listing

, which generates a credible backlink from a manufacturer domain. 

Their product differentiation language — "CAT4 wind-rated" systems with a "50-year warranty covering materials AND labor"

 — is schema-friendly and appears consistently across multiple service pages, indicating structured content deployment. They are ranking for or targeting queries like "roofing contractors Indianapolis," "roof replacement Indianapolis," and suburb-specific variants. Domain authority is not publicly confirmed this cycle, but their content strategy and multi-location citation footprint suggest a meaningful organic presence. Their key vulnerability: the content reads generic and could apply to any city with a find-replace — no hyper-local depth.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

No direct AI citation data was returned in this research cycle. Based on their content architecture — consistent service-area pages, FAQ schema patterns, GAF backlink, and longstanding domain — they have the structural ingredients to surface in AI-generated answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. However, their 4.2 Google rating and 3.43 BBB rating create a trust signal gap that generative engines increasingly weigh. Raptor's 5.0 rating at 673 verified reviews is a stronger trust-signal package for AEO, particularly for queries like "best roofer in Indianapolis" or suburb-specific prompts where AI models tend to anchor on rating quality over raw volume.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where White Oak beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (1,043 vs. 673), four-location geographic footprint, GAF certification creating manufacturer backlinks, and a 43-year tenure that weighs well in local trust signals. Their multi-trade model also generates repeat-customer touchpoints Raptor does not have.

**Where Raptor beats White Oak:** 5.0 vs. 4.2 on Google — a full 0.8-star gap that matters enormously in LSA and map-pack rankings. Raptor's 0.92 owner response rate is competitive; White Oak's BBB trail of high-pressure sales complaints (the $92K-to-$65K in-appointment flip) creates an exploitable brand vulnerability in a market where homeowners are comparing contractors on trust, not just price.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their documented in-home sales pressure tactics and 3.43 BBB rating create a direct contrast play — Raptor's transparent, premium positioning and perfect rating is the cleaner story in any head-to-head moment.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **GAF or manufacturer certification backlinks.** 

White Oak's GAF listing at [gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential/usa/in/indianapolis/white-oak-construction-corporation-1116433) generates a high-authority manufacturer backlink.

 Cameron should audit whether Raptor has equivalent manufacturer directory listings (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) and claim every eligible one — these are free, high-DA backlinks with zero content lift required.

2. **Service-area content depth at the suburb level.** White Oak runs dedicated location pages for Indianapolis, Carmel, Brownsburg, and others. Their execution is thin and templated, but the architecture is right. Raptor should build tighter, genuinely local suburb pages — referencing actual neighborhoods, HOA permit processes, and local weather patterns — that AI models and Google will prefer over find-and-replace copy.

3. **Monitor their canvassing-to-review pipeline.** 

Indeed employee reviews describe White Oak's canvasser-heavy model as generating "constant churn and turnover."

 If their field sales volume drops, their review velocity — already at ~1/week — will crater further. Raptor should track their 30/90-day review cadence monthly; if White Oak stalls below 4.0, an aggressive local PR push (press release, Nextdoor campaign, neighborhood sponsorship) during that window could permanently widen the star-rating gap in the local map pack.

## Competitive Intelligence Brief — Bone Dry Roofing (Loc 2 / Winton Dr, Indianapolis)
**Refreshed: May 19, 2026 | Dashboard Cycle: Tuesday**

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Bone Dry Roofing was founded by Gene Judd, who launched it as a true family affair out of a garage in Speedway, Indiana.

 

Founded in 1989, the company is headquartered in Indianapolis and has expanded to include offices across Ohio, Kentucky, Missouri, and Tennessee

 — making Loc 2 (7735 Winton Dr, Indianapolis, IN 46268) one node in a sprawling multi-state platform. 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 15 roofing locations plus acquired brands including G&W Roofing, Ravlin's Roofing, Roof One, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors.

 Their distinction in the Indy market is sheer brand ubiquity and institutional infrastructure — they are not a single-location operator but a regional roll-up competing locally.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



Per *Roofing Contractor* Magazine's 2023 profile, Bone Dry operates 20 locations nationally with 500 employees and an 81%/19% residential-to-commercial split.

 That is the enterprise figure. For Loc 2 specifically, the Indianapolis office historically accounted for a meaningful slice: 

in 2022, Bone Dry reported $121.6M in total revenue, with roughly $36 million — about 30% — attributable to its original Indianapolis operation.

 Enterprise-wide revenue has accelerated since: 

ZoomInfo notes the hiring of a new CFO and COO followed financial performance in 2023 that included revenue of over $183 million.

 **Confidence on enterprise revenue: high** (confirmed by trade press and ZoomInfo). **Confidence on Loc 2 isolated revenue: medium** — the $36M Indy figure is the most recent public data point and is now 3 years old.

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**

Bone Dry's ATS (hosted at [jobs.lever.co/bonedry](https://jobs.lever.co/bonedry)) shows active Indianapolis-specific openings across Commercial, Customer Service, Roofing, Sales, and Solar divisions right now. Drilling into what is tactically significant:

- 

Active listings target sales representatives specifically for the Southside of Indianapolis and/or the Greenwood area

 — they are pushing into Raptor's southern-suburb turf.
- 

An Insurance Claims Specialist and Insurance Specialist are being recruited to work with clients filing claims for roof damage

 — a dedicated insurance-lane sales function, which is a volume play.
- 

A Management in Training (MIT) program is actively recruiting

, indicating pipeline-building for future production and sales leadership.

**CONFIDENTIAL — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Ownership, Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**DATE:** May 14, 2025
**RE:** 90-Day Offensive Strategy — Taking Market Share from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION BRIEF**

We hold 2,195 reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor holds 671 at 5.0. On paper, they have a star-rating edge. In volume — the metric that drives LSA rank, consumer trust, and market perception — we dominate them by more than 3-to-1. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and the number of reviews.

 That asymmetry is our most powerful weapon and we are not using it aggressively enough. Here is how we change that this quarter.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Single-Channel Lead Dependency**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

The contractors getting crushed right now all have the same profile: they built their entire lead generation around one paid channel. When that channel gets more expensive and less effective, they have nowhere to go except spend more.

 

Roofing LSA costs now run $55–$90 per lead, with storm damage queries hitting $150 or more in active weather zones.

 **Raptor is renting leads from Google. We need to make that rent feel unbearable by owning the organic and earned channels they are ignoring.**

**Weakness 2: Thin Geographic Roots Outside Center Grove and Greenwood**

Raptor has deliberately concentrated its community identity in Greenwood and Center Grove. That is smart micro-positioning — but it is also a ceiling. It leaves Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Avon, Brownsburg, and Mooresville comparatively uncontested from their brand. Their own website lists these markets but offers no localized content, no neighborhood-specific proof, no community ties. **Their brand identity is geographically narrow. We can establish dominant local presence in six surrounding submarkets before they react.**

**Weakness 3: A 5.0 Rating Is a Trap — And Their Volume Gap Is Catastrophic**

671 reviews is a thin foundation for a "premium" brand claim in a metro of two million people. A 5.0 with 671 reviews statistically signals a brand that is either early-stage or one that aggressively manages negative reviews out of public view. 

91% of homeowners rely on online reviews before choosing a contractor.

 When a homeowner compares Raptor's 671 reviews to our 2,195, the psychological authority gap is irreversible at the point of decision. **We must make that comparison unavoidable in our ad creative and landing pages.** Additionally, Raptor's brand "accountability" messaging has no third-party verification layer — no GuildQuality profile with external data, no volume of cross-platform reviews. Our depth of proof across platforms is superior; we are simply not weaponizing it.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "2,000+ Reasons" — Volume Dominance Ad Blitz**

Launch a Google Ads and Meta campaign directly targeting Greenwood, Center Grove, Carmel, and Fishers zip codes with a single creative hook: **"2,000+ families in Central Indiana trusted us with their roof. See why."** The ad links to neighborhood-specific landing pages showing real job photos, real homeowner names, and review counts by zip code. This is not a comparison ad — it does not name Raptor. It simply makes our social proof so visible and localized that Raptor's numbers look thin by comparison. Run Performance Max alongside standard search to capture the full funnel. 

Maximize the Google Business Profile with weekly updates, real job photos, accurate service listings, and every review responded to within 24 hours. Businesses with active GBPs saw 28% more discovery search views within 90 days.



**Campaign 2: Nextdoor + Neighborhood Facebook Group Infiltration in Center Grove and Greenwood**

This is their home turf. We take it. Assign two dedicated field marketers to saturate Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor with genuine project posts — before/after photos, real customer names, hyperlocal testimonials. Simultaneously, run Nextdoor Neighborhood Ads in these exact zip codes. 

By targeting specific neighborhoods, especially those where you are already working, you create geographic relevance and social proof. Unlike shared leads from third-party providers, you are not competing with multiple other roofers for the same prospect.

 Every crew truck in those neighborhoods gets a door hanger dropped on adjacent homes. Cost per lead for this channel is a fraction of LSA. **We do not need to outspend Raptor in their backyard. We need to out-show them.**

**Campaign 3: AI Search and GBP Domination Play**

Raptor's website content is thin on educational depth. Ours needs to be the resource Google AI and ChatGPT cite when homeowners ask about Indianapolis roofing. Immediately commission 12 location-specific blog articles targeting: "best roofers in Carmel IN," "hail damage roof claim Greenwood IN," "how long does a roof replacement take in Indianapolis," and equivalent queries for every submarket Raptor claims but doesn't own. 

When ChatGPT or Google AI Mode recommends a contractor, it pulls from websites that answer real questions. "How much does a furnace replacement cost in Charlotte?" beats "We provide quality HVAC service" every single time.

 Pair this with a dedicated Google Business Profile posting schedule — one post every three days, every post geotagged, every post with a real job photo.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a hyper-targeted LSA and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on Raptor's branded adjacent keywords — "Raptor Roofing reviews," "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis," "Raptor Roofing vs" — and route that traffic to a landing page titled: "Comparing Indianapolis Roofers? Here's What 2,195 Reviews Look Like."**

The page shows no competitor names. It shows our review volume, our cross-platform presence, our years in market since 2018, our BBB A+ standing, and a side-by-side of what 671 reviews versus 2,195 reviews actually means in terms of completed jobs and homeowner confidence. 

There is a fixed number of LSA leads in every roofing market, influenced by demand, seasonality, and competition.

 Every lead we intercept from a homeowner researching Raptor is a lead that costs Raptor money — they paid to generate that consumer's awareness, and we convert it.

**Cameron should be uncomfortable not because we are attacking his brand. He should be uncomfortable because we are making his review gap the centerpiece of every homeowner's decision — and he cannot fix 671 versus 2,195 in 90 days.**

This is where we win.

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use only. Recommend immediate budget alignment meeting within 5 business days.*

## Three Moves for This Week

**1. Launch an "Insurance Coverage Audit" inspection offer before ARAC owns the post-hail education search lane in Johnson County.**

ARAC Roof It Forward dropped multiple Indy-targeted hail-damage and insurance-process articles in the last three weeks heading into peak storm season, and they're explicitly positioning themselves as the adjuster-meeting expert. Meanwhile, the "8-Year Rule" and Roof Payment Schedule endorsements are quietly converting RCV policies to ACV, leaving homeowners on the hook for 60-70% of replacement cost. ARAC is fighting for the post-storm searcher. The bigger, undefended lane is the pre-storm worried homeowner — and that lead is colder, cheaper, and converts on trust, which is exactly Raptor's strong suit at 5.0 stars across 673 reviews.

Build a free "Roof & Policy Audit" — a 30-minute on-site visit that includes drone photos, pre-loss condition documentation (which the homeowner keeps), and a one-page plain-English breakdown of their policy's settlement basis with the relevant endorsement language flagged. Do not sell on this visit. The leave-behind is the lead magnet — homeowners will text it to their neighbors, which is the referral mechanic that actually compounds in Greenwood. Build a single landing page this week with FAQ schema targeting "Greenwood roof insurance coverage," "Johnson County ACV vs RCV," and "is my roof covered Indiana" — these are zero-volume today and will be high-volume the morning after the first real hail event.

Success metric this week: page live by Friday, 15 audits booked by end of next week, and one homeowner-friendly social video shot explaining the 8-Year Rule. Track which audits convert to replacement jobs over the next 90 days — this is also a list-building play for the next storm.

**2. Stand up a same-hour text-response SLA and put the actual number in paid ad creative — directly attacking Trojan Roofing's 0.06 response rate and the labor-constrained 50%+ of competitors who can't pick up the phone.**

Trojan has 643 reviews and is functionally dormant on response (0.06 rate, zero new reviews in 7 and 30 days). Bone Dry's secondary location is at 0.88. The RoofersCoffeeShop report confirms more than half of contractors are short-staffed, which means homeowners who call competitors after 5pm are getting voicemail. Amos added 33 reviews last week and Indy Roof added 28 — they're winning the volume game. Raptor cannot out-volume them this quarter, but Raptor can out-respond every single one of them, and that is what homeowners actually feel.

Commit to a published "text back in 10 minutes, 7am-9pm, 7 days a week" SLA. Internally, route every inbound to a shared on-call line with backup coverage. Externally, the headline of every Google Ads and LSA creative this week becomes: "Text us. We answer in 10 minutes. 673 five-star reviews say we mean it." This is a direct-response angle that no Indy roofer in the top 10 is running because most of them can't actually deliver it. Test it as a callout in LSA messaging and a primary headline in Google Ads — homeowners post-storm are anxious and the company that responds first wins disproportionately.

Success metric: median inbound response time under 10 minutes for the next 14 days, tracked in the CRM. CTR on the new ad creative versus the existing control measured by Friday of next week. If CTR lifts 15%+ and the SLA holds, this becomes the year's primary positioning line across every channel.

**3. Lock in a referral pact with two Greenwood-area independent insurance agents this week, while SPG Roofing is busy promoting their Top 100 ranking instead of building street-level distribution.**

SPG moved from #128 to #92 on the Roofing Contractor Top 100 list and they will spend the next 60 days putting that badge on every truck, yard sign, and landing page. That is air war. The ground war they are not fighting is the local independent insurance agent — and an independent agent in Greenwood writes 20-40 homeowner policies a month, every single one of which is a future roof claim. Agents do not want to recommend storm chasers because their clients call them screaming when the warranty work disappears. A 5.0-star local contractor with a clean accountability story is exactly what they want to hand out.

Identify five independent agents (not captive State Farm/Allstate offices — those are restricted) operating in Greenwood, Bargersville, Whiteland, and Franklin. Walk in this week with coffee, the 673-review credential, the new Insurance Coverage Audit offer from action #1, and a simple ask: "When your clients have a roof question, send them to us. We won't sell them anything they don't need, we'll document the claim professionally, and we'll make you look good." Offer to co-brand the coverage audit leave-behind with their logo. No kickback — that's an insurance regulation issue and also degrades trust. The exchange is reputation for reputation.

Success metric: two signed-up agent partners by end of next week, three coverage audits booked through agent referral within 30 days. Long term, three to five active agent relationships in south Indy is a lead source SPG and Amos cannot easily replicate because it requires owner-led trust-building, not marketing spend — exactly the moat Raptor is built to widen.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing — Cameron Blakely, CMO Dashboard**
*Refreshed: Thursday, May 22, 2025*

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they serve both residential and commercial customers as a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor, and hold memberships in good standing with the BBB (A+), the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They now operate with locations in both Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, making them a multi-market operator — a meaningful scale distinction from most Indy competitors. Their core differentiator is a full-service exterior platform: roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, and commercial painting all under one roof, with a heavy lean into insurance claims navigation.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach puts annual revenue at $28.6 million (2025 estimate) with 57 employees.

 

Prospeo independently estimates approximately 51–100 employees.

 **Confidence: medium.** Revenue figures from third-party data aggregators carry noise, but the $12M–$29M range across multiple sources is plausible for a 50+ year old multi-trade operation with a 3,000+ review velocity. 

A PPP loan of $584,200 from Stock Yards Bank resulted in the reported retention of 40 jobs

, which provides a floor on their W-2 headcount. 

Known leadership includes a Director of Sales, a VP of Construction (Todd Danbom), and a Marketing Director (Charles Crowley).



---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



ZipRecruiter shows an open Team Lead, Field Marketing role in Indianapolis.

 

Their own careers page is actively recruiting Home Improvement Sales Consultants, trained to "out-sell the competition," running both company-provided leads and self-generated referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags an open Estimator & Project Manager role in Indianapolis.

 The Field Marketing Team Lead posting is the one to watch — it signals they are expanding or restructuring canvassing operations, which is their dominant top-of-funnel model. A marketing specialist role was also recently active per Glassdoor. No C-suite or digital marketing director-level hires detected in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**



Amos Roofing & Exteriors holds only 2.5 stars on Yelp

 against their 4.9 on Google — a significant platform disparity that is a textbook review-funneling signal. They are clearly driving customers to Google and not managing Yelp proactively. 

Facebook shows 1,383 likes with only 23 people "talking about this"

 — minimal organic engagement for a company of their scale, suggesting Facebook is largely dormant. No active Facebook Ad Library presence was confirmed. 

BBB-accredited since September 1993

 with an A+ rating and active recent reviews. 

On Angi, they carry a 4.5 overall rating

 — solid but not perfect. GuildQuality shows verified reviews including some negative feedback around siding quality and communication, concentrated in 2017–2018 but visible in search.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Amos Exteriors runs on WordPress with PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — a legacy tech stack that likely limits Core Web Vitals performance and structured data execution. They have built out a deep location/service page architecture (e.g., [amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) which generates decent long-tail coverage across Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood. They are ranking for core Indy roofing queries on the strength of domain age (54 years) and review volume. However, the jQuery 1.11.1 version is outdated by roughly a decade, which is a schema implementation and page speed liability. No evidence of a robust backlink strategy from local press or Indy-area publications. Their blog exists but content cadence appears irregular. The GAF Master Elite designation earns them a high-authority inbound link from [gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential/usa/in/indianapolis/amos-exteriors-inc-1113337) which Raptor should match or counter.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current AI engine behavior for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," and "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville": Amos Exteriors is likely to appear in AI-generated answers by virtue of their review volume (3,098 Google reviews), domain age, multi-location page structure, and GAF Master Elite certification — all of which are strong citation signals for LLMs pulling from structured web data. Their 54-year operating history and BBB A+ accreditation since 1993 further boost entity authority in knowledge graph indexing. Raptor, with 675 reviews and a 5.0 rating, is a thinner entity profile at this stage. The gap is not about quality — it is about entity depth and crawlable citation surface area. Raptor should be building AEO-optimized FAQ schema, press mentions, and third-party citation anchors (NRCA membership, GAF certification page, local news features) to close this AI visibility gap.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,098 vs. 675), domain age, multi-trade service breadth, Lafayette market expansion, and an in-house marketing department with named Director of Marketing and Marketing Manager on the BBB profile. Their insurance claims navigation operation is a well-oiled machine with dedicated reps named throughout reviews. **Where Raptor beats Amos:** Raptor holds a 5.0 vs. 4.9 — the cleanest rating in the Indy top 10 by volume — and runs a premium, accountable positioning that Amos cannot credibly claim given Glassdoor complaints about sales rep quality, canvassing no-shows, and a 2.5 Yelp rating. The most exploitable weakness: 

Amos canvassers are reportedly setting appointments where "the homeowner either doesn't know you're coming, or doesn't understand why you're there"

 — a trust and brand integrity gap Raptor can hammer directly in paid and social messaging.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **Location-specific service page architecture.** 

Amos explicitly builds out named suburb service areas including Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Geist, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, Franklin, and Anderson

 with dedicated URLs. Raptor should audit whether it has comparable depth — each suburb page is an independent AEO and local SEO asset.

2. **Multi-trade upsell model.** 

Amos installs GAF asphalt shingles, slate, cedar shake, and flat systems as a GAF Master Elite Contractor with System Plus Warranty coverage

, and upsells into siding, gutters, windows, and masonry on the same job. Monitor whether their average ticket size is growing through multi-trade attachment — this is the revenue-per-customer lever Raptor should have an opinion on.

3. **GuildQuality third-party review pipeline.** Amos pipes verified customer surveys through [GuildQuality](https://www.guildquality.com/profile/amos-exteriors-inc), which generates an independent review corpus that feeds AEO signals. Cameron should evaluate whether adding a GuildQuality or similar verified-survey layer gives Raptor an additional citation source that AI engines pull when surfacing contractor recommendations.

Of the $121M reported in 2022, approximately $36 million (30%) came from the Indianapolis office alone.

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

 Roles posted on ZipRecruiter and Indeed include:

 — versus 2,422 on Google. That is a 97% review-funneling gap, the clearest sign in this market of a team that has mastered Google review capture but has done nothing to cultivate Yelp. Their Facebook presence (
