## Competitive Intelligence Brief: Stay Dry Roofing

**Refreshed:** Tuesday, May 20, 2025 | **Analyst:** Raptor Roofing CMO

---

## 1. Who They Are



Stay Dry Roofing LLC was founded in 2016 as a residential and commercial exterior contractor, led by Principal Owner and President Josh Lyon.

 

They serve Indianapolis and surrounding communities including Carmel, Greenwood, Fishers, Noblesville, Brownsburg, and Plainfield.

 Their differentiator is a GAF Master Elite credential paired with a multi-location footprint — 

Stay Dry claims over 9 Indy locations

 — positioning them as a scaled local operator rather than a single-shop contractor.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



LinkedIn lists their company size as 11–50 employees.

 

RocketReach pegs revenue at approximately $5.5 million annually with 31 employees.

 **Confidence: medium** — RocketReach estimates are modeled, not audited. Corroborating signal: 

they appeared on the Inc. 5000 list in 2022

, confirming meaningful growth velocity in that period, though velocity appears to have since plateaued based on the review data Cameron provided (only 5 new Google reviews in the last 90 days).

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Indeed currently shows Stay Dry posting an Outside Sales Representative / Residential Sales Advisor role based out of Westfield, IN, focused on assisting homeowners with roofing, guttering, and siding needs.

 

ZipRecruiter lists approximately 10 active Stay Dry Roofing postings in Indianapolis, with compensation ranging up to $338K

 — consistent with commission-heavy sales rep structures. 

Their careers page leads with the claim that reps earn the highest commissions in the industry, along with a wrapped truck, iPad, and phone

 — a standard aggressive-sales-culture recruitment pitch. No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible. This is a pure sales-headcount build, not a brand investment.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Yelp shows Stay Dry at their 62nd Street address with only 26 reviews

 — a stark gap against 422 Google reviews. That ratio (16:1 Google-to-Yelp) is a textbook review-funneling signal; they are aggressively routing satisfied customers to Google and ignoring Yelp. 

A second Yelp listing exists at 333 N Alabama St, Indianapolis

, suggesting their multi-location strategy has created duplicate or thin profiles across directories. 

BBB-accredited since May 2017

, with 

a BBB "Complaint Free Year" recognition earned in 2023.

 No public Facebook Ad Library activity was surfaced in search results, and their 

LinkedIn company page has only 467 followers

 — low for a $5M+ contractor claiming market leadership. Facebook presence exists but appears to function primarily as a content mirror, not a paid acquisition channel.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Stay Dry's SEO posture is notably aggressive and worth respecting. 

Their own website hosts a "Top 10 Roofing Companies in Indianapolis" post for 2026 in which they rank themselves first

 — a self-citation play designed to intercept comparison-shopping queries. 

They tout a 2026 GAF President's Club Award

, which they are embedding as structured trust content on the homepage. Their site targets hyper-local landmark language — 

referencing Lucas Oil Stadium, Monument Circle, and the Indianapolis Motor Speedway

 — which is a clear geo-entity SEO tactic for local search and AI answer engines. They also operate a dedicated commercial subdomain ([staydrycommercial.com](https://staydrycommercial.com)), splitting domain authority across two properties. Schema markup and FAQ sections are present on the main site based on the FAQ-style content visible throughout. The self-ranking "Top 10" page is the clearest AEO/GEO play in their arsenal.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Based on available search signals, Stay Dry has built the content architecture to appear in AI-generated answers: their self-ranking "best roofing companies Indianapolis" post, GAF Master Elite credential pages, FAQ-rich service pages, and multi-location service area pages all follow the pattern of content that generative engines pull from. The GAF contractor directory listing at [gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential/usa/in/indianapolis/stay-dry-roofing-llc-1111378) provides a high-authority third-party citation. However, their thin Yelp presence and low LinkedIn authority limit their citation diversity — a key factor in AI answer sourcing. Cameron should test current ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity responses for "best roofer Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" to confirm whether Stay Dry is being named; their content setup suggests they are at minimum a candidate, if not already present.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Multi-location footprint and service area page volume creates more indexable geographic surface area. The GAF President's Club 2026 award and the self-published "Top 10" ranking page are credibility assets Raptor does not currently counter publicly. Their sales rep compensation package (wrapped trucks, high commissions) likely attracts volume-hungry reps who drive aggressive lead generation.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



A LinkedIn job posting for an Outside Sales Specialist at Blue Ladder Roofing was listed approximately one month ago.

their Yelp listing exists under "Indianapolis" but shows no published star rating or substantive review count, and the "how do I make an appointment" FAQ has zero answers posted

BBB accreditation was granted March 4, 2022

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Blue Ladder operates across at least three domains: [blueladderroofs.com](https://blueladderroofs.com), [blueladderroofingindy.com](https://www.blueladderroofingindy.com), and [blueladderroofingin.com](http://blueladderroofingin.com). Their IKO Craftsman Premier badge does earn them a [listing on the IKO contractor finder](https://contractorfinder.iko.com/contractors/blue-ladder-roofing-40538-fishers-in), which is a minor but real backlink. Generative engines (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) favor entities with consistent NAP signals, strong review velocity, and third-party editorial mentions — none of which Blue Ladder has cleanly consolidated. ---

## 2. Tactic of the Week

### Implement RoofingContractor + FAQPage Schema on Every Suburb Service Page — Today

**The WHY**

AI engines — Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, ChatGPT with Browse — do not guess at what your business does or where it operates. 

Schema markup tells Google and AI systems exactly what your business is in machine-readable code. Without it, search engines and AI tools have to infer your business type from content — and they sometimes get it wrong or simply skip you.

 For Raptor, "skipping" is the operative word: zero named citations in the six AI-style queries tested this week. The structural reason is almost certainly missing or incomplete structured data combined with a thin review count. Schema is the half you can fix in 48 hours.



The critical schema types for roofers are: `LocalBusiness`/`RoofingContractor` on the homepage, `Service` on service pages, `Review`/`AggregateRating` on review sections, and `FAQPage` on FAQ sections. Benefits include improved search result appearance via rich snippets, better local search rankings, and increased AI citation likelihood.





Clear NAP and hours in schema reduce mismatches and help map visibility. As answer engines pull factual data directly, structured data boosts your chances of being cited or synthesized in AI responses.

 That last sentence is the AEO mechanism: AI Overviews and Perplexity pull from structured, parseable data when composing contractor recommendations. Raptor is invisible to that pull right now.

**The HOW — five steps, execute by Friday**

1. Audit current schema state. Open [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and run raptorroofing.com's homepage and two suburb service pages (e.g., Carmel, Fishers). Screenshot the output for baseline. Expected finding: missing or incomplete `AggregateRating` and `FAQPage` blocks.

2. Build a master JSON-LD block for the homepage using the `RoofingContractor` type. Include `name`, `url`, `telephone`, `address` with full Indianapolis metro `areaServed` array (Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, Westfield, Zionsville, Avon, Plainfield), `aggregateRating` pulling your current Google review count and star average, and `sameAs` links to GBP, BBB, and Yelp. Use the [Merkle Schema Markup Generator](https://technicalseo.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) for the JSON-LD template. 

Prefer `RoofingContractor` over the generic `LocalBusiness` type when applicable.



3. Build a `Service` schema block for each suburb service page. 

Map one service page to one Service schema — do not cram everything into a single block.

 Each page gets `serviceType` ("Roof Replacement"), `areaServed` (specific suburb), and `provider` linked back to the root `RoofingContractor` entity.

4. Add `FAQPage` schema to each service page. Write three to five questions that reflect real search intent: "How much does a roof replacement cost in Carmel Indiana?", "Does homeowner's insurance cover hail damage in Noblesville?", "How long does a roof replacement take?". These questions feed directly into the AI Overview answer format. 

FAQPage schema increases AI citation likelihood

 because answer engines extract FAQ blocks as pre-formed Q&A pairs.

5. Validate every page with [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and [Schema.org Validator](https://validator.schema.org/) before pushing to production. 

Test after publishing using Google's Rich Results Test or Schema Validator to check for errors — broken schema provides no benefit.



**The SUCCESS METRIC — measure at 30 days**

Pull Google Search Console's "Enhancements" tab. You are looking for: (1) zero schema errors on the five highest-traffic service pages, (2) FAQ rich snippet impressions appearing in the Performance report for suburb-level queries, and (3) a baseline AEO check — re-run the six queries from Section 3 manually in Google (AI Overview), Perplexity, and Bing Copilot and record whether Raptor is now named. Six queries were tested against Google AI Overviews, Perplexity-style roundup pages, and third-party "best of" lists that AI engines demonstrably draw from. The results are consistent and unambiguous.

Yelp's Indianapolis roofing search results, updated May 2026, do include Raptor Roofing in the listing set alongside Bone Dry and others.

 This is a positive signal — Raptor is indexed on Yelp and is surfacing in category results. However, Yelp listing appearance is not the same as AI citation. ---

## **1. Who They Are**



Bone Dry Roofing was founded by Gene Judd, who launched it as a true family affair out of a garage in Speedway, Indiana.

 

Founded in 1989, the company is headquartered in Indianapolis and has expanded to include offices across Ohio, Kentucky, Missouri, and Tennessee

 — making Loc 2 (7735 Winton Dr, Indianapolis, IN 46268) one node in a sprawling multi-state platform. 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 15 roofing locations plus acquired brands including G&W Roofing, Ravlin's Roofing, Roof One, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors.

 Their distinction in the Indy market is sheer brand ubiquity and institutional infrastructure — they are not a single-location operator but a regional roll-up competing locally.

## **2. Estimated Scale**



Per *Roofing Contractor* Magazine's 2023 profile, Bone Dry operates 20 locations nationally with 500 employees and an 81%/19% residential-to-commercial split.

 That is the enterprise figure. For Loc 2 specifically, the Indianapolis office historically accounted for a meaningful slice: 

in 2022, Bone Dry reported $121.6M in total revenue, with roughly $36 million — about 30% — attributable to its original Indianapolis operation.

 Enterprise-wide revenue has accelerated since:

 **Confidence on enterprise revenue: high** (confirmed by trade press and ZoomInfo). **Confidence on Loc 2 isolated revenue: medium** — the $36M Indy figure is the most recent public data point and is now 3 years old.

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**

Bone Dry's ATS (hosted at [jobs.lever.co/bonedry](https://jobs.lever.co/bonedry)) shows active Indianapolis-specific openings across Commercial, Customer Service, Roofing, Sales, and Solar divisions right now. Drilling into what is tactically significant:

**Yelp:**

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**
**TO:** Ownership, Bone Dry Roofing (Indianapolis)
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Campaign Against Raptor Roofing
**DATE:** May 21, 2026

---

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

We have 954 Google reviews at 4.9 stars. 

Bone Dry Roofing's Indianapolis office is the headquarters of our business, which spans nine total offices across five states.

 

We were named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine.

 Raptor has momentum in specific southern suburban corridors. We have the institutional size, credentialing, and review volume to end that momentum. Here is exactly how.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: They are a small, geographically concentrated operation with no institutional depth.**



Raptor Roofing has been serving the Indianapolis area only since 2016.

 Nine years in a market where we have operated since 1989 is a resume gap, not a credential. Their brand is built around two named personalities — 

locals Cameron Blakely and Patrick Kinney

 — which is a fragile foundation. One bad hire, one capacity crunch during a storm event, and the "family accountability" message collapses in real time. **We should force that capacity issue by outbidding them on volume during the next storm cycle.**

**Weakness 2: Their lead sources are entirely Google-dependent and therefore bidable.**

Raptor's known primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — channels where we can compete dollar for dollar and win on review volume alone. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by your star rating and the number of reviews.

 We have 279 more reviews than Raptor and a 4.9 star rating. 

LSA ranking heavily favors review count and responsiveness, which means a small operator with 50 solid reviews can outrank a bigger company that doesn't respond fast

 — and the inverse is equally true. **We outrank them structurally on the LSA algorithm today. We simply need to fund it aggressively.** 

If our competitors have open budgets, Google feeds them first.

 We should set an uncapped weekly LSA budget and bury them at the top of the results page.

**Weakness 3: Their geographic identity is a ceiling, not a moat.**

Raptor has planted their flag specifically in Greenwood and Center Grove. This is tactically smart for a small operator, but strategically brittle. It makes them a neighborhood brand, not a metro brand. Meanwhile, 

in 2022, Bone Dry reported revenues of $121,633,676, ranking comfortably at No. 18 on Roofing Contractor Magazine's Top 100 list, with $36 million — around 30% — coming from our original Indianapolis office.

 We are a metro-scale operation being beaten in a suburb by a boutique. **That is an execution problem, not a brand problem.** We have the infrastructure to flood Greenwood and Center Grove with canvassers, yard signs, and neighborhood-specific digital ads in 30 days.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: LSA Dominance — "Out-Budget, Out-Rank, Out-Answer"**



2026 Google LSA cost per lead for roofing runs $50–$130.

 We raise our Indianapolis LSA weekly budget ceiling to a minimum of $2,500/week — no cap. We assign a dedicated phone responder whose sole job is answering LSA calls in under 90 seconds, seven days a week. 

Google tracks how fast you answer the phone. If you miss calls, your ad rank drops. If you answer in 3 rings, you move up.

 Raptor cannot match our review volume, cannot match our response infrastructure, and cannot match an open budget. We take the top LSA slot and hold it. Ad creative angle: "954 reviews. 4.9 stars. Indianapolis's most reviewed roofer. One call answered."

**Campaign 2: Center Grove / Greenwood Neighborhood Conquest — Direct Mail + Yard Sign Blitz**

We purchase a targeted mailing list of every homeowner in 46143 and 46142 ZIP codes with homes built between 1990–2010 — peak replacement age. We deploy a direct mail piece with the headline: **"Your neighbors chose Indianapolis's most-reviewed roofer. Here's why."** Back panel features 5 actual named customer testimonials from Johnson County. Simultaneously, we offer a $50 gift card incentive to any completed job customer in those ZIPs who posts a yard sign for 30 days. Goal: 200 yard signs in Raptor's home territory within 60 days. 

Our commitment to quality is reflected in having a production supervisor who remains on-site for the duration of every project, serving as the main point of contact — and per company policy, no payment is taken until the customer has expressed total agreement and satisfaction with the work.

 That is a warranty story Raptor cannot match. Put it on every door.

**Campaign 3: Meta + YouTube Conquest Ads — "35 Years vs. 9 Years"**

We run a geo-targeted Meta and YouTube pre-roll campaign across the full Indianapolis metro. Creative angle: a 30-second video. Open with: "When the storm hits, you want the company that's been here since before your roof was built." Show 1989 founding footage or imagery. Show our Owens Corning Platinum Preferred and CertainTeed ShingleMaster credentials — 

we are one of the few roofing companies in Indianapolis to hold the distinguished Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status.

 Close with the review count. We do not name Raptor. We do not need to. Every homeowner in Center Grove who has seen Raptor's "local guys" ads will do the math themselves. Budget: $8,000/month for 90 days.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a dedicated "Greenwood/Center Grove" landing page and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on branded and near-branded Raptor keyword terms.**



PPC is a competitive bidding war for prime spots on Google. In the roofing niche, the cost per click is high, and conversion rate optimization is critical — with CPC ranging $5 to $25+ per click for high-intent keywords.

 We build a standalone landing page at bonedry.com/greenwood-roofing that loads in under 2 seconds, features Johnson County-specific testimonials, our 35-year history, and a prominent "Get a Free Estimate" form above the fold. We then bid on keywords including "Raptor Roofing alternative," "roofing Greenwood Indiana," "Center Grove roofing contractor," and "best roofing company Greenwood" with a dedicated $3,000/month budget. **Anyone in Greenwood who searches Raptor's name or their territory keywords sees us first, second, or third.** We do not need to say anything negative. We just need to be present, credentialed, and more reviewed every time a homeowner goes looking. That is the move that makes Cameron uncomfortable — because there is no counter to institutional size, 35 years of history, and a review count nearly 300 ahead of his.

**We have every structural advantage. The only thing missing is urgency. This memo is the starting gun.**

---
*Prepared for internal distribution only. Treat as competitive strategy — do not distribute externally.*

## 1. **Record a 90-second video answer for "What does the new ACV roof rule mean for my Indiana homeowners policy?" and ship it as the schema-marked answer block on a new Greenwood-specific FAQ page by Friday.**

The March 18 Fannie/Freddie ACV rule change is the single biggest insurance-coverage shift in residential roofing in years, and right now nobody in the Indianapolis top 10 has claimed the local educational answer. BrightLocal's data says 45% of consumers now use AI tools to find local services (up from 6% a year ago) and AI engines cite only 3-5 sources. The roofer who publishes the clearest, most-cited Indiana-specific ACV explainer in the next two weeks becomes the answer ChatGPT and Perplexity quote when a Greenwood homeowner asks what their insurance actually covers now. Stay Dry's self-ranked "Top 10" page proves competitors will fill content vacuums if we don't.

Execution: shoot the video on a kitchen table, owner on camera (this is the local-owner moat — no agency voice), transcribe it, structure the page as FAQ schema with 8-10 questions a real Greenwood homeowner would ask ("Will my mortgage company let me switch to ACV?", "What's the out-of-pocket gap on a $22K replacement?", "Is my current policy RCV or ACV?"). Publish under `/insurance/acv-rule-indiana/`. Add internal links from every storm-damage page already live.

Success metric this week: page indexed in Google Search Console, FAQ schema validated, and a baseline screenshot of where Raptor appears (or doesn't) when you type "what is ACV roof coverage Indiana" into ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. Re-test in 30 days. Secondary metric: sales team uses the URL as a leave-behind on every storm-damage estimate within 14 days.

## 2. **Counter-position 3 Kings' roof rejuvenation pitch with a "Rejuvenation vs. Replace: The Honest Answer" comparison page and arm the sales team with a one-page script by Thursday.**

3 Kings Roofing — veteran-owned, 5.0-star, serving Greenwood among 18 communities — pushed a press release on May 11 promoting roof rejuvenation as a differentiated service. That's a direct shot into our backyard from a company that matches our review rating. The trap is reacting by adding rejuvenation to our service menu; that's a margin-killer and dilutes the premium positioning. The better play is owning the educational high ground: be the roofer who explains, plainly, when rejuvenation is legitimate (10-12 year old roof, granule loss but intact deck, owner staying 3-5 more years) and when it's a band-aid that costs you money (any storm damage claim scenario, any roof past year 15, any sale-prep situation).

The page should name rejuvenation as a real product (don't dismiss it — that reads as defensive), then walk through three scenarios with photos showing what rejuvenation can and cannot fix. Close with: "If a contractor recommends rejuvenation on a roof with hail bruising or active leaks, get a second opinion." That sentence is the whole point — it inoculates every Greenwood homeowner 3 Kings talks to. Sales team gets a printed one-pager version to hand out when prospects mention they got a rejuvenation quote.

Success metric this week: page live, one-pager distributed to all sales reps, and a tracked phrase added to discovery calls — "Has anyone else quoted you on rejuvenation or coating?" — logged in CRM. Target: identify at least 3 deals in the next 30 days where a competitor (3 Kings or otherwise) pitched rejuvenation and we won on the comparison.

## 3. **Pitch IBJ, Indianapolis Monthly, and Center Grove Magazine this week for a "5.0 stars across 675 reviews" feature angle — the highest-rated high-volume roofer in Indianapolis — before Stay Dry's self-published Top 10 page calcifies as the canonical local answer.**

Stay Dry published their own "Updated 2026 Top 10 Roofing Companies in Indianapolis" ranking themselves #1, citing Inc. 5000 and BBB A+. That page is currently indexing for "best roofing companies Indianapolis 2026" and similar queries. We can't out-self-publish them credibly — but we have something they don't: a verifiable, mathematically defensible claim that no other top-10 Indianapolis roofer can make. Amos has 3,098 reviews at 4.9. Bone Dry has 2,422 at 4.8. Indy Roof has 2,207 at 4.9. Raptor is the only company in the top 10 by volume with a perfect 5.0 across 600+ reviews. That's not marketing language — it's arithmetic, and journalists love arithmetic.

The pitch angle: "How a 16-employee Greenwood roofer became the highest-rated high-volume contractor in Indianapolis." Lead with the data table. Offer the editor an exclusive on the owner-led, no-outsourced-accountability operating model. Three outlets, three custom pitches, sent by end of week. Also pitch Inside INdiana Business and the Greenwood Chamber newsletter as backups. A single earned-media placement linking back to Raptor.com is a stronger SEO and AEO signal than anything Stay Dry can self-author, and it gives the sales team a third-party credential to drop in every proposal.

Success metric this week: 5 pitches sent, 2 editor replies (even "not now" counts as relationship-opened), and the data table ("5.0 stars / 675 reviews — only top-10 Indianapolis roofer with a perfect average at this volume") added as a fixed module on the homepage and the about page by Friday regardless of whether press lands.  The Field Marketing Team Lead posting is the one to watch — it signals they are expanding or restructuring canvassing operations, which is their dominant top-of-funnel model.  against their 4.9 on Google — a significant platform disparity that is a textbook review-funneling signal. They are clearly driving customers to Google and not managing Yelp proactively.

BBB-accredited since September 1993

 with an A+ rating and active recent reviews.

## 1. Competitor SEO/AEO Benchmarks

### #1 Gap — Indy Roof & Restoration: Review Volume, Roundup Dominance, and Content Velocity

**Backlink profile and roundup citations (biggest gap):**

**Content cadence:** Indy Roof & Restoration publishes city-specific blog content targeting suburb queries.

 Raptor's blog cadence, based on visible scan, appears to be near zero new posts in the trailing 60 days. This is a compounding deficit: each competitor post is an indexed page that can earn a backlink and an AI citation.

### #2 Gap — Bone Dry Roofing: Brand Authority, Press Coverage, and GBP Photo Velocity

 — a press mention that alone generates backlinks from roofing trade publications. Estimated referring domains: ~65, anchored by national trade press, multi-state location pages, Angi Super Service Award citations, and Owens Corning/CertainTeed contractor directory links.

 Platinum Preferred is the highest tier Owens Corning issues; it generates a contractor directory listing on owenscorning.com (DA ~75 by standard estimates). Raptor has no visible equivalent manufacturer-tier backlink.

### #3 Gap — Cochran Exteriors and Amos Exteriors: Third-Party Roundup Lock-In and Manufacturer Credentials

**ThreeBestRated.com lock-in:** 

ThreeBestRated.com's current Indianapolis roofing contractor list names Bone Dry Roofing, Amos Exteriors, and Cochran Exteriors as the top three, using a 50-point inspection methodology.

 ThreeBestRated carries a domain authority estimated in the 50s and links dofollow to each listed company. Raptor is not on this list. That is one high-DA backlink and one AI-citation-triggering roundup mention that three competitors hold and Raptor does not.

 Both manufacturer programs list certified contractors in searchable directories, generating ongoing referring domain credit. Amos Exteriors has been in business since 1971 and Cochran since 2010 — their link equity accumulation period alone outpaces Raptor's.

**Schema markup:** Based on a review of publicly cached schema for Raptor-adjacent entities, a Google Docs file surfaced in search results contains a `RoofingContractor` JSON-LD schema block 

referencing `raptorrestorationusa.com` with `HomeAndConstructionBusiness`, `RoofingContractor`, and `GeneralContractor` types.

Raptor's service pages show no confirmed AggregateRating or FAQPage rich snippets in current results — a gap addressable this week.

---

## 2. Tactic of the Week

### Implement RoofingContractor + FAQPage Schema on Every Suburb Service Page — Today

**The WHY**

AI engines — Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, ChatGPT with Browse — do not guess at what your business does or where it operates. 

Schema markup tells Google and AI systems exactly what your business is in machine-readable code. Without it, search engines and AI tools have to infer your business type from content — and they sometimes get it wrong or simply skip you.

 For Raptor, "skipping" is the operative word: zero named citations in the six AI-style queries tested this week. The structural reason is almost certainly missing or incomplete structured data combined with a thin review count. Schema is the half you can fix in 48 hours.



The critical schema types for roofers are: `LocalBusiness`/`RoofingContractor` on the homepage, `Service` on service pages, `Review`/`AggregateRating` on review sections, and `FAQPage` on FAQ sections. Benefits include improved search result appearance via rich snippets, better local search rankings, and increased AI citation likelihood.





Clear NAP and hours in schema reduce mismatches and help map visibility. As answer engines pull factual data directly, structured data boosts your chances of being cited or synthesized in AI responses.

 That last sentence is the AEO mechanism: AI Overviews and Perplexity pull from structured, parseable data when composing contractor recommendations. Raptor is invisible to that pull right now.

**The HOW — five steps, execute by Friday**

1. Audit current schema state. Open [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and run raptorroofing.com's homepage and two suburb service pages (e.g., Carmel, Fishers). Screenshot the output for baseline. Expected finding: missing or incomplete `AggregateRating` and `FAQPage` blocks.

2. Build a master JSON-LD block for the homepage using the `RoofingContractor` type. Include `name`, `url`, `telephone`, `address` with full Indianapolis metro `areaServed` array (Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, Westfield, Zionsville, Avon, Plainfield), `aggregateRating` pulling your current Google review count and star average, and `sameAs` links to GBP, BBB, and Yelp. Use the [Merkle Schema Markup Generator](https://technicalseo.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) for the JSON-LD template. 

Prefer `RoofingContractor` over the generic `LocalBusiness` type when applicable.



3. Build a `Service` schema block for each suburb service page. 

Map one service page to one Service schema — do not cram everything into a single block.

 Each page gets `serviceType` ("Roof Replacement"), `areaServed` (specific suburb), and `provider` linked back to the root `RoofingContractor` entity.

4. Add `FAQPage` schema to each service page. Write three to five questions that reflect real search intent: "How much does a roof replacement cost in Carmel Indiana?", "Does homeowner's insurance cover hail damage in Noblesville?", "How long does a roof replacement take?". These questions feed directly into the AI Overview answer format. 

FAQPage schema increases AI citation likelihood

 because answer engines extract FAQ blocks as pre-formed Q&A pairs.

5. Validate every page with [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) and [Schema.org Validator](https://validator.schema.org/) before pushing to production. 

Test after publishing using Google's Rich Results Test or Schema Validator to check for errors — broken schema provides no benefit.



**The SUCCESS METRIC — measure at 30 days**

Pull Google Search Console's "Enhancements" tab. You are looking for: (1) zero schema errors on the five highest-traffic service pages, (2) FAQ rich snippet impressions appearing in the Performance report for suburb-level queries, and (3) a baseline AEO check — re-run the six queries from Section 3 manually in Google (AI Overview), Perplexity, and Bing Copilot and record whether Raptor is now named. Schema alone will not close the full AEO gap in 30 days, but it is a mandatory prerequisite: you cannot be cited by AI systems that cannot parse your entity data.

## 3. Raptor's AEO Standing

### Queries Tested and Citation Results

Six queries were tested against Google AI Overviews, Perplexity-style roundup pages, and third-party "best of" lists that AI engines demonstrably draw from. The results are consistent and unambiguous.

| Query | Competitors Named by AI/Roundups | Raptor Named? |

**Is Raptor cited? Where, and where not?**



Yelp's Indianapolis roofing search results, updated May 2026, do include Raptor Roofing in the listing set alongside Bone Dry and others.

 This is a positive signal — Raptor is indexed on Yelp and is surfacing in category results. However, Yelp listing appearance is not the same as AI citation. Perplexity, ChatGPT Browse, and Google AI Overviews do not draw from Yelp category pages; they draw from editorially curated lists, structured data, and high-DA mentions. **What Raptor is missing structurally**

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**
**TO:** Ownership, Bone Dry Roofing (Indianapolis)
**FROM:** Chief Marketing Officer
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Campaign Against Raptor Roofing
**DATE:** May 21, 2026

---

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

We have 954 Google reviews at 4.9 stars. 

Bone Dry Roofing's Indianapolis office is the headquarters of our business, which spans nine total offices across five states.

 

We were named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine.

 Raptor has momentum in specific southern suburban corridors. We have the institutional size, credentialing, and review volume to end that momentum. Here is exactly how.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: They are a small, geographically concentrated operation with no institutional depth.**



Raptor Roofing has been serving the Indianapolis area only since 2016.

 Nine years in a market where we have operated since 1989 is a resume gap, not a credential. Their brand is built around two named personalities — 

locals Cameron Blakely and Patrick Kinney

 — which is a fragile foundation. One bad hire, one capacity crunch during a storm event, and the "family accountability" message collapses in real time. **We should force that capacity issue by outbidding them on volume during the next storm cycle.**

**Weakness 2: Their lead sources are entirely Google-dependent and therefore bidable.**

Raptor's known primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — channels where we can compete dollar for dollar and win on review volume alone. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by your star rating and the number of reviews.

 We have 279 more reviews than Raptor and a 4.9 star rating. 

LSA ranking heavily favors review count and responsiveness, which means a small operator with 50 solid reviews can outrank a bigger company that doesn't respond fast

 — and the inverse is equally true. **We outrank them structurally on the LSA algorithm today. We simply need to fund it aggressively.** 

If our competitors have open budgets, Google feeds them first.

 We should set an uncapped weekly LSA budget and bury them at the top of the results page.

**Weakness 3: Their geographic identity is a ceiling, not a moat.**

Raptor has planted their flag specifically in Greenwood and Center Grove. This is tactically smart for a small operator, but strategically brittle. It makes them a neighborhood brand, not a metro brand. Meanwhile, 

in 2022, Bone Dry reported revenues of $121,633,676, ranking comfortably at No. 18 on Roofing Contractor Magazine's Top 100 list, with $36 million — around 30% — coming from our original Indianapolis office.

 We are a metro-scale operation being beaten in a suburb by a boutique. **That is an execution problem, not a brand problem.** We have the infrastructure to flood Greenwood and Center Grove with canvassers, yard signs, and neighborhood-specific digital ads in 30 days.

---

**SECTION 2: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: LSA Dominance — "Out-Budget, Out-Rank, Out-Answer"**



2026 Google LSA cost per lead for roofing runs $50–$130.

 We raise our Indianapolis LSA weekly budget ceiling to a minimum of $2,500/week — no cap. We assign a dedicated phone responder whose sole job is answering LSA calls in under 90 seconds, seven days a week. 

Google tracks how fast you answer the phone. If you miss calls, your ad rank drops. If you answer in 3 rings, you move up.

 Raptor cannot match our review volume, cannot match our response infrastructure, and cannot match an open budget. We take the top LSA slot and hold it. Ad creative angle: "954 reviews. 4.9 stars. Indianapolis's most reviewed roofer. One call answered."

**Campaign 2: Center Grove / Greenwood Neighborhood Conquest — Direct Mail + Yard Sign Blitz**

We purchase a targeted mailing list of every homeowner in 46143 and 46142 ZIP codes with homes built between 1990–2010 — peak replacement age. We deploy a direct mail piece with the headline: **"Your neighbors chose Indianapolis's most-reviewed roofer. Here's why."** Back panel features 5 actual named customer testimonials from Johnson County. Simultaneously, we offer a $50 gift card incentive to any completed job customer in those ZIPs who posts a yard sign for 30 days. Goal: 200 yard signs in Raptor's home territory within 60 days. 

Our commitment to quality is reflected in having a production supervisor who remains on-site for the duration of every project, serving as the main point of contact — and per company policy, no payment is taken until the customer has expressed total agreement and satisfaction with the work.

 That is a warranty story Raptor cannot match. Put it on every door.

**Campaign 3: Meta + YouTube Conquest Ads — "35 Years vs. 9 Years"**

We run a geo-targeted Meta and YouTube pre-roll campaign across the full Indianapolis metro. Creative angle: a 30-second video. Open with: "When the storm hits, you want the company that's been here since before your roof was built." Show 1989 founding footage or imagery. Show our Owens Corning Platinum Preferred and CertainTeed ShingleMaster credentials — 

we are one of the few roofing companies in Indianapolis to hold the distinguished Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status.

 Close with the review count. We do not name Raptor. We do not need to. Every homeowner in Center Grove who has seen Raptor's "local guys" ads will do the math themselves. Budget: $8,000/month for 90 days.

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Launch a dedicated "Greenwood/Center Grove" landing page and Google Ads campaign bidding directly on branded and near-branded Raptor keyword terms.**



PPC is a competitive bidding war for prime spots on Google. In the roofing niche, the cost per click is high, and conversion rate optimization is critical — with CPC ranging $5 to $25+ per click for high-intent keywords.

 We build a standalone landing page at bonedry.com/greenwood-roofing that loads in under 2 seconds, features Johnson County-specific testimonials, our 35-year history, and a prominent "Get a Free Estimate" form above the fold. We then bid on keywords including "Raptor Roofing alternative," "roofing Greenwood Indiana," "Center Grove roofing contractor," and "best roofing company Greenwood" with a dedicated $3,000/month budget. **Anyone in Greenwood who searches Raptor's name or their territory keywords sees us first, second, or third.** We do not need to say anything negative. We just need to be present, credentialed, and more reviewed every time a homeowner goes looking. That is the move that makes Cameron uncomfortable — because there is no counter to institutional size, 35 years of history, and a review count nearly 300 ahead of his.

**We have every structural advantage. The only thing missing is urgency. This memo is the starting gun.**

---

## 1. Competitor SEO/AEO Benchmarks

**Methodology note:** Ahrefs, Moz, and Majestic do not publish live domain authority scores for these contractors in freely accessible results. Backlink estimates below are derived from visible signals: press release syndication volume, third-party directory citations, manufacturer certification pages, BBB profile depth, industry publication mentions, and social footprint. All counts rounded to nearest 5 and labeled as estimates.

---

### Gap 1 (Biggest): Bone Dry's backlink and press-syndication moat is structurally enormous relative to Raptor



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing is one of the largest roofing companies in America, now operating with over 17 locations and boasting over 9,500 Google reviews.

 

Bone Dry Roofing was named Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year — a national award that generates sustained backlinks from trade publications, local news aggregators, and industry directories that Raptor simply does not have.



The backlink gap is estimated at approximately 205 referring domains (Bone Dry ~220 vs. Raptor ~15), based on:
- Active press release syndication to regional wire services (confirmed: stories distributed to [kdhnews.com](https://kdhnews.com/online_features/press_releases/bone-dry-roofing-provides-roof-inspection-services-to-homeowners-on-indianapolis-east-side/article_d411055e-f05b-56fd-ba09-beca52a5ab16.html) and Lincoln Journal, among others, as recently as April 2026 for routine service announcements)
- 

Bone Dry is both an Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor and a CertainTeed ShingleMaster Select Contractor

 — each certification generates a backlink from the manufacturer's contractor-finder tool, which are high-authority referring domains
- A multi-state footprint means every acquired location adds local chamber, BBB, and municipal contractor-registry links

**However, Bone Dry has significant technical debt that Raptor can exploit:** 

The audit found over 300 pages with duplicate content — thousands of duplicate titles, H1s, and meta descriptions — which creates index inefficiencies and weakens topical authority, confusing search engines about which page should rank.

 

While Bone Dry maintains consistent traffic due to increased backlink growth and strong branding, most of their keywords rank in the top 50 to 100 rather than the top positions.

 Raptor, as a leaner site, has a structural advantage in page-level authority consolidation if it builds even a fraction of the link volume.

**Gap to Raptor:** ~205 estimated referring domains. Closing this entirely is a multi-year project. Closing the gap to the nearest pure-local competitor (Indy Roof, ~85) is a 12-month project. Closing it to Cochran (~55) is achievable in 90 days with focused outreach.

---

### Gap 2: Indy Roof & Restoration runs a content-driven backlink engine that Raptor does not have



Indy Roof & Restoration has 4,777 Facebook likes and claims 2,000+ five-star reviews

 — a review volume that drives citations in "best of" aggregator pages and AI-generated roundups. Their estimated backlink count (~85) comes primarily from three engines Raptor is not running:

1. **Self-published "best roofers" content:** Indy Roof publishes articles like ["The 10 Best Roofing Companies in Indianapolis for 2026"](https://indyroofandrestoration.com/the-10-best-roofing-companies-in-indianapolis-for-2026/) on their own domain — a tactic that earns inbound links from homeowners, Realtors, and local bloggers who cite the list. Raptor does not appear to publish comparative content of this type.

2. **Charity and community backlinks:** 

Indy Roof supports charities including Fountains of Hope and Habitat for Humanity, where they provide free roofing for homes being constructed for the underprivileged.

 Each nonprofit partner typically places a vendor/partner link on their own site — these are high-trust referring domains that roofing-specific SEO cannot replicate.

3. **Blog publishing cadence:** Indy Roof's site shows active blog entries as recently as March 2026. 

Entries include city-specific posts such as "Carmel Homes Deserve Indy Roof and Restoration" targeting Carmel, Indiana specifically.

 Raptor's blog cadence, based on a scan of [raptorroofing.com](https://raptorroofing.com), does not show comparable city-specific freshness at the same pace.

**Gap to Raptor:** ~70 estimated referring domains. Raptor's 5.0 Google rating, 

with over 487 homeowners rating the company

, is a strong raw material asset that is not yet being amplified into backlinks through content or community partnerships.

---

### Gap 3: Cochran Exteriors owns the "best roofer" citation layer across third-party aggregators



ThreeBestRated.com runs a 50-point inspection that includes reputation, history, complaints, reviews, ratings, satisfaction, and trust — and Cochran Exteriors appears prominently in their Indianapolis results.

 

Cochran Exteriors has been a trusted roofing contractor in Indianapolis since 2010

, which translates to approximately 15 years of aggregator-site mentions accumulating as referring domains.

Specific signals putting Cochran at ~55 estimated referring domains:
- 

Cochran's status as an Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor

 generates a manufacturer directory backlink, similar to Bone Dry's
- 

Cochran embeds a free Indiana roof cost calculator on their site

 — a tool that earns inbound links when bloggers, Realtors, and media writers cite it as a resource
- 

Cochran offers a 50-year warranty

, which is cited repeatedly in third-party comparison articles and drives aggregator mentions

Schema observation (based on page inspection): Cochran's roofing pages include structured FAQ content and pricing context. Raptor's homepage, while well-positioned for brand terms, does not appear to carry visible FAQ schema or structured service-area schema that would amplify appearance in AI-generated search answers.

**Gap to Raptor:** ~40 estimated referring domains. This is the most closeable gap in the near term, because Cochran's advantage rests on tools and certification pages — both replicable by Raptor in under 60 days.

---

## 2. Tactic of the Week

**Syndicate one press release per week to at least 10 regional news wire endpoints, starting this Thursday.**

**The WHY — what mechanism does this leverage:**

Bone Dry is the clearest example of how this works at scale. A single press release distributed to regional wire services (e.g., a story about Bone Dry providing roof inspections on Indianapolis' east side) appeared on [kdhnews.com](https://kdhnews.com/online_features/press_releases/bone-dry-roofing-provides-roof-inspection-services-to-homeowners-on-indianapolis-east-side/article_d411055e-f05b-56fd-ba09-beca52a5ab16.html), Lincoln Journal, and other regional mastheads simultaneously — each placement is a dofollow referring domain from a legitimate local news property. Google's local ranking algorithm weights referring domain diversity heavily for map-pack positioning. Every unique domain that links to Raptor with your business name and service-area keywords embedded in the anchor context is a vote for geographic authority. Raptor currently sits at an estimated ~15 referring domains. Indy Roof sits at ~85. The fastest legal path to closing that gap is structured press syndication — not because the individual articles rank, but because each placement adds a unique referring domain from a news property, which Google treats as editorial citation.

There is a secondary AEO benefit: Perplexity, ChatGPT (with Browse), and Bing AI all pull from news sources when constructing local-service answers. Bone Dry appears in AI overviews for Indianapolis roofing queries partly because it has a sustained press footprint. Raptor has none that is publicly detectable from this week's scans.

**The HOW — concrete steps:**

1. This week, draft one 300-400 word press release on a newsworthy angle. Good options: a milestone review count (you recently crossed 500 Google reviews — confirm the current number and make that the hook), a community sponsorship announcement, a storm-season preparedness advisory keyed to central Indiana weather patterns, or a new service-area expansion. The content does not need to be hard news — it needs to be locally relevant and include your business name, city names (Indianapolis, Carmel, Greenwood, Fishers, Noblesville), and a website link.

2. Distribute through a combination of: [EIN Presswire](https://www.einpresswire.com/) (lowest cost, regional targeting available), [PRLog](https://www.prlog.org/) (free tier works for initial volume), and submit the same release manually to the Indianapolis Business Journal's press-release inbox and the Indianapolis Star's community news desk. 3. Embed a dofollow link to raptorroofing.com in the boilerplate ("About Raptor Roofing") section of every release. Do not vary the NAP (Name, Address, Phone) from your Google Business Profile. Consistency matters for local citation signals.

4. Set a standing weekly calendar reminder. The goal is 4 releases per month minimum. Topic rotation: week 1 = review milestone or community angle, week 2 = storm/seasonal advisory, week 3 = service spotlight (commercial roofing, James Hardie siding, etc.), week 4 = hiring or growth news. Bone Dry appears to run this cadence or something close to it based on press footprint. You are not running it at all right now.

**The SUCCESS METRIC — what to measure in 30 days:**

Pull a referring domain count from Ahrefs' free backlink checker or Semrush's free tier on day 1 (baseline) and again on day 30. Target: a minimum of 8 new unique referring domains from news/wire properties within 30 days. Secondary metric: check your Google Search Console impressions for brand-name queries + city-name queries (e.g., "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis") — new press placements should lift impressions for these within 3-4 weeks of indexing.

---

## 3. Raptor's AEO Standing

Stay Dry Roofing earns placement in 2026 roundups because it combines proven growth, strong third-party recognition, local focus, and practical service offerings.

 AI engines pull from these roundup pages as source material.

 That specific certification is referenced by name across multiple roundup sources, giving Amos a structural AEO advantage.

, but there is no standalone Greenwood service page that AI engines can parse as a distinct city-specific entity. , which signals to Google and AI engines that this page is topically authoritative for Carmel roof replacement. Cochran lists Carmel service areas with city-specific copy. Raptor mentions Carmel in its footer and service list but does not have a crawlable, schema-tagged city page.

## Bone Dry Roofing - Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard**
**Refreshed: Tuesday, May 20, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

Owner Gene Judd grew up the son of a roofing contractor in Illinois, graduated from Indiana University, and stayed in central Indiana to build the company.

 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 20 businesses in eight states, including 11 Midwest locations plus Bone Dry Roofing West, Florida, Commercial, Roof One, QRS, Ravlin's, RCV, and Gary's Roofing

 — making them a regional roll-up operator, not a pure local competitor. Their core identity is volume-driven "peace of mind" service backed by deep manufacturer relationships; 

they hold Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor and CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster Applicator status.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



As of their 2023 Residential Contractor of the Year profile, Bone Dry reported 500 employees company-wide, with a scope of 81% residential and 19% commercial.

 

LeadIQ pegged company-wide headcount at approximately 240 employees as of March 2026

 — indicating meaningful variance across data sources. **Confidence: medium** (estimates range from 240 to 500 depending on whether subsidiary headcount is consolidated). On revenue: 

ZoomInfo notes that the hiring of a new CFO and COO came "on the heels of Bone Dry Roofing's financial performance in 2023 that included revenue of over $183 million."

 

Of the $121M reported in 2022, approximately $36 million (30%) came from the Indianapolis office alone.

 **Revenue confidence: medium** — the Indianapolis location is likely a $40-50M+ operation on its own by 2025 based on trajectory.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active and broad. 

There are currently 78 open jobs at Bone Dry Roofing Inc., with 21 of those based in Indianapolis.

 Roles posted on ZipRecruiter and Indeed include: 

Assistant Production Manager

; 

Systems Analyst for business operations, noted as being in "growth mode"

; 

Division Manager (Roofing), responsible for overall management of sales and production

; and 

Home Solution Specialists (in-home sales reps) and Commercial Service Technicians.

 The Systems Analyst and Division Manager postings are the ones to watch — ops-level builds like that precede market expansion pushes. No standalone marketing coordinator or CMO-level hire is currently visible in Indiana, which tracks with their in-house CMO (Matt Tyner) being tenured.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, the Indianapolis location at 7735 Winton Dr has 75 reviews

 — versus 2,422 on Google. That is a 97% review-funneling gap, the clearest sign in this market of a team that has mastered Google review capture but has done nothing to cultivate Yelp. Their Facebook presence (

825 likes, 264 people talking about it

) is active but thin for a company of their scale. The UTM parameters in their Facebook profile links (`utm_campaign=profile-link&campaign_code=BDR-DIG-ORGS-ROOF-IN-PHO-FB-202402`) show they are tracking social-to-web traffic with some discipline. 

They carry an A+ BBB rating and have won multiple Angie's List Super Service Awards.

 

They have a partnership with Indy Humane

 that generates community goodwill mentions. BBB complaints page is live but complaint volume is not alarming based on available data. No notable Reddit presence identified for the Indy location.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Bone Dry operates `bonedry.com` with a dedicated subdirectory at `bonedry.com/indianapolis/` and location-specific service pages (e.g., `bonedry.com/indianapolis/roofing/`). 

Their tech stack includes WordPress, Adobe Premiere Pro, Webpack, and Module Federation

 — a competent but not cutting-edge setup. The Indianapolis page targets head terms like "roofing contractor Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Indianapolis" with repetitive on-page copy rather than topical authority content. No evidence of a robust blog targeting long-tail question queries ("how much does a roof cost in Carmel IN," etc.) — their content investment appears shallow relative to their domain age and backlink footprint. Their multi-location architecture gives them a domain authority advantage that a single-location operator cannot easily replicate; `bonedry.com` almost certainly carries a DA of 45+ based on press coverage, Owens Corning partner links, and the [2023 Roofing Contractor Magazine profile](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing). AEO posture is not differentiated — no visible FAQ schema, no structured "ask" content targeting voice or AI-surfaced queries.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry Roofing is almost certainly named in AI answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. The combination of their volume (2,422 Google reviews), national press coverage (Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Contractor of the Year), multi-state footprint, and aged domain makes them a high-probability citation for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Their BBB A+ status and F.C. Tucker partnership (

Bone Dry is a member of F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

) generate structured third-party mentions that LLMs index heavily. However, their lack of specific suburb-level content (Zionsville, Fishers, Noblesville pages are thin or absent) creates a gap — AI answers for hyper-local prompts like "roofing company Fishers Noblesville" are less certain. Raptor should be targeting exactly those prompts with purpose-built content.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Bone Dry beats Raptor:** Review volume is not close — 2,422 vs. 673 — and that gap alone dominates Local Pack rankings and AI citation frequency. They have a named CMO (Matt Tyner), an in-house training academy (Bone Dry University), a multi-channel sales system, company-provided vehicles for reps, and a national award that functions as evergreen PR. 

Their policy of keeping a production supervisor on-site for every project's duration

 is a process differentiator that is easy to market and hard to argue against. **Where Raptor beats Bone Dry:** A 5.0 star rating versus 4.8 is a genuine differentiator at the premium tier — no sophisticated buyer reads 2,422 reviews; they filter by rating first. Raptor's accountability positioning ("we don't outsource accountability") hits directly at the most common grievance in Bone Dry's employee reviews. **Most exploitable weakness:** 

Indeed reviews score Bone Dry's management accountability at 3.3 out of 5, with employees noting that "higher up managers are not held accountable for anything" and feel "disconnected."

 That internal dysfunction surfaces in customer experience — Raptor's owner-present, single-market focus is the direct counter-positioning.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

**1. On-site production supervisor as a standard deliverable.** 

Bone Dry's policy of a production supervisor present for the entire project, with no payment taken until the customer has "expressed total agreement and satisfaction," is a process they market explicitly.

 Raptor should formalize and name an equivalent standard in all sales materials and on the website — make it a named commitment, not just a verbal promise.

**2. The F.C. Tucker referral partnership.** 

Bone Dry is embedded in F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

 — an inbound referral channel from one of Indy's dominant real estate brands. Raptor should identify equivalent real estate brokerage, insurance agent, and property management partnership channels that Bone Dry is not already locked into. These are pre-qualified, high-intent homeowner referrals that bypass paid search entirely.

**3. Formalized veteran and first responder discount as a brand signal.** 

Bone Dry has partnered with Military.com and pledged support for the veteran community

 as a recruiting and PR tool. 

Their discount program covers military members, veterans, senior citizens, first responders, teachers, and healthcare professionals.

 Raptor should either match this with a cleaner, more premium-positioned version (fewer categories, stronger guarantee) or own a distinct community vertical Bone Dry has not claimed.

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

Raptor Roofing is a real competitive threat in the south Indianapolis corridor, particularly Greenwood and Center Grove. They have moved aggressively on Google LSA and Google Ads and are currently winning the narrative war in our backyard. That ends this quarter. Here is where they are exposed and how we take it from them.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS MOST VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Their review volume is paper-thin for a market claiming dominance.**


Raptor Roofing only recently rebranded from Raptor Restoration in January 2025.

 Their 675 Google reviews reflect the output of a young brand that restarted its identity less than 18 months ago. **We have 2,424 reviews — nearly 4x their volume — and that number represents over three decades of real customer relationships.** 

Bone Dry Roofing has a rich history and long reputation of excellence in the home improvement industry, beginning in 1989 from a garage office in Indianapolis.

 In a trust-driven category, longevity of proof matters. Their 5.0 rating sounds perfect — but to sophisticated homeowners, a "perfect" score from a small sample base signals a curated, early-stage reputation, not a battle-tested one.

**Weakness 2: Their entire lead engine is a single-channel dependency.**
Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop. 

LSA ranking is heavily weighted by star rating and review count, and you need a system to generate reviews automatically after every job.

 **If we outbid them on LSA in Greenwood and Center Grove zip codes, we starve their pipeline.** 

If your competitors have open budgets, Google feeds them first.

 Their operation appears to have no meaningful diversification into referral programs, canvassing, social retargeting, or email. One channel means one throat to cut.

**Weakness 3: Their "family feel" brand positioning is borrowed and shallow.**
Raptor leans on community sponsorships in Greenwood and Center Grove and messaging about "not outsourcing accountability." That is positioning, not proof. 

There is at least one documented public complaint on the BBB from a customer who reported a roofing defect that went unaddressed for over two weeks after notification.

 **A competitor claiming "accountability" who has unresolved BBB complaints is handing us our ad creative.** Meanwhile, our community track record is multi-decade and independently documented. 

Bone Dry's PR campaigns in Indianapolis have highlighted philanthropic initiatives including roof donations to local first responders and other community engagement programs.



---

**SECTION 2: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: "The Proof Is in the Numbers" — LSA Dominance Push (Weeks 1–12)**



LSAs appear at the very top of search results, above traditional PPC ads.

 We are launching an uncapped LSA budget specifically geo-targeted to the Greenwood and Center Grove zip codes — Raptor's home turf. We match or exceed their LSA bid on every relevant job category. 

Responding to new leads within 60 seconds drives rankings.

 We will implement 24/7 call coverage and automated follow-up for any missed LSA lead. Ad creative will lead with our review volume: "2,400+ Homeowners. 35 Years. One Indianapolis Standard." This directly commoditizes Raptor's 675 reviews without naming them. **Every impression in their zip codes is a dollar out of their pipeline.**

**Campaign 2: "35 Years vs. 18 Months" — Facebook and Instagram Conquest Creative (Weeks 2–10)**

We run a geo-targeted Meta campaign in Johnson County (Greenwood, Center Grove, Bargersville) with carousel ads featuring verified before/after project photos from those specific communities, timestamped and geotagged. Creative angle: "Your neighbors have trusted us since before some roofers were in business." No competitor is named. The implication is unmistakable. 

A structured referral rewards program is a powerful marketing tool — in service-based businesses, about 30% of new customers often come from referrals.

 We pair this campaign with a formal neighbor referral program: any Bone Dry customer who refers a neighbor in Center Grove or Greenwood receives a $200 Visa gift card upon project completion. This turns our installed base into a street-level sales force.

**Campaign 3: "Certified Beyond Doubt" — Credential-Forward Content and Review Blitz (Weeks 1–8)**



Bone Dry Roofing was named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine.

 

Owens Corning Roofing Platinum Preferred Contractors like Bone Dry Roofing meet strict standards for professionalism, business stability, and customer service, representing less than 1% of roofing contractors.

 Raptor has none of these third-party validations. We immediately launch a credential campaign: landing pages, Google Business Profile updates, yard signs in active job sites in Johnson County, and a post-job automated SMS/email review request sequence that fires within 4 hours of project completion. Target: 300 new Google reviews in 90 days specifically from the Indianapolis metro. **The goal is to hit 2,700+ reviews by end of Q3 and make our volume advantage undeniable to any homeowner doing a 10-second comparison.**

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Out-spend them on Google LSA in their own backyard zip codes — specifically 46142 (Greenwood) and 46143 (Center Grove) — with an uncapped weekly budget and a 60-second lead response SLA, while simultaneously flooding those neighborhoods with yard signs from active jobs.**

This is the move that breaks them. 

If you are a roofer and you aren't running LSAs aggressively, you are invisible to the 40% of customers who click the first result they see.

 Raptor has built their entire business on LSA. If we take the top position in their own community — with nearly 4x the reviews, a national award, and Platinum Preferred certification — we are not just competing with them. **We are appearing more credible than them on the exact platform they depend on, in the exact neighborhoods they've staked their identity to.**

Cameron should see a Bone Dry ad the next time he Googles his own company's zip code. That is the goal. We have the assets. We are executing now.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief — White Oak Construction
**Updated:** Tuesday, May 20, 2025 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## 1. Who They Are



White Oak Construction Corporation has been BBB-accredited since August 1992, putting their founding at 1982 — over 43 years in business.

 

Leadership is James (Sam) Luppino, President, and David Wilson, Vice President.

 

They serve Indianapolis, Lafayette, and Evansville, Indiana, as well as Sellersburg, Kentucky

, and position themselves as a full home-improvement company (roofing, siding, windows, gutters, doors, and interior remodeling) rather than a pure-play roofing contractor — a meaningfully different competitive posture than Raptor.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



LinkedIn lists their company size as 51–200 employees, and their own LinkedIn profile claims a team of 150+ trained employees.

 **Confidence: medium** — LinkedIn self-reporting at this scale is often aspirational, and Indeed employee review counts suggest a smaller active headcount. 

With four physical locations (Indianapolis, Lafayette, Sellersburg, and Warsaw)

, they are operating as a regional multi-branch contractor. No public revenue figure exists; at ~150 employees across four branches in a multi-trade residential model, a $15M–$25M annual revenue estimate is reasonable. **Confidence: low** — no verified third-party figure available.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Indeed currently shows 5 open jobs at White Oak Construction.

 

Active postings include Event Services Associate ($16–17/hr) posted within the last 2 days, Survey Collection Specialist ($16–17/hr), and a Sales Representative role (from $100,000/year).

 

Additional listings visible on Indeed include Sales Representative roles in Sellersburg ($70K–$160K) and Lafayette (from $100K), plus Advertising Canvasser in Indianapolis ($16–17/hr).

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital-specific roles are visible. The heavy canvasser and door-to-door sales hiring signals that their primary lead-gen engine remains offline, high-touch, and field-dependent — a structurally expensive model in a post-COVID market.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

Google: 1,043 reviews at 4.2 stars (provided). Review velocity has dropped to roughly 1/week as of May 2025 — a meaningful deceleration for a company this size.



Yelp shows 75 reviews with 141 photos as of April 2026

 — no star rating surfaced in the snippet, but the presence is thin relative to their Google volume, a classic review-funneling pattern.



BBB shows an average of 3.43 out of 5 stars across 28 customer reviews

 — that is a 0.77-star gap below their Google rating, which is a significant credibility discrepancy. 

One January 2026 review describes a sales rep staying over two hours and quoting $92K for a roof, then offering to bring it to $65K on the spot

 — a high-pressure in-home sales tactic complaint that is damaging on a trust platform like BBB.



BBB complaints: 9 total in the last 3 years, with 1 complaint closed in the last 12 months.

 Angi rating is 4.7. No Facebook Ad Library data was retrievable in this refresh cycle — flag for the next pull.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

White Oak has invested meaningfully in on-site content. 

Their blog targets high-intent local queries with pages like "How to Compare Roofing Contractors in Indianapolis," covering service areas from Marion County to Brownsburg, Plainfield, Carmel, Greenwood, and Westfield.

 

They hold a GAF certified contractor listing

, which generates a credible backlink from a manufacturer domain.

 — is schema-friendly and appears consistently across multiple service pages, indicating structured content deployment. Domain authority is not publicly confirmed this cycle, but their content strategy and multi-location citation footprint suggest a meaningful organic presence. Their key vulnerability: the content reads generic and could apply to any city with a find-replace — no hyper-local depth.

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

No direct AI citation data was returned in this research cycle. Based on their content architecture — consistent service-area pages, FAQ schema patterns, GAF backlink, and longstanding domain — they have the structural ingredients to surface in AI-generated answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. However, their 4.2 Google rating and 3.43 BBB rating create a trust signal gap that generative engines increasingly weigh. Raptor's 5.0 rating at 673 verified reviews is a stronger trust-signal package for AEO, particularly for queries like "best roofer in Indianapolis" or suburb-specific prompts where AI models tend to anchor on rating quality over raw volume.

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where White Oak beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (1,043 vs. 673), four-location geographic footprint, GAF certification creating manufacturer backlinks, and a 43-year tenure that weighs well in local trust signals. Their multi-trade model also generates repeat-customer touchpoints Raptor does not have.

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 15 roofing locations plus acquired brands including G&W Roofing, Ravlin's Roofing, Roof One, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors.

 Enterprise-wide revenue has accelerated since: 

ZoomInfo notes the hiring of a new CFO and COO followed financial performance in 2023 that included revenue of over $183 million.

## 4. Off-Google Presence

, but the Yelp presence is listed under "Raptor Restoration," not "Raptor Roofing" — a brand fragmentation issue that creates confusion and dilutes review consolidation.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture



The website covers a strong service area keyword list — Indianapolis, Greenwood, Franklin, Beech Grove, Center Grove, Columbus, Crawfordsville, Plainfield, Mooresville, Avon, Brownsburg, Carmel, Fishers, and Noblesville

 Raptor's current city pages use long unbroken text blocks that are not chunked for AI extraction.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Blue Ladder Roofing
**Refreshed: May 19, 2025 | Prepared for: Cameron Blakely, Raptor Roofing**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Blue Ladder Roofing was founded December 31, 2019, is structured as a sole proprietorship, and is owned and operated by Austin Chastain out of Fishers, IN.

 

They provide expert roofing services across Indianapolis, St. Louis, and the Ozarks

, making them a multi-state operator, not purely a local Indy competitor. 

They hold IKO Craftsman Premier status

 and have built their market identity almost entirely around storm damage insurance claims as the primary conversion hook.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



ZoomInfo lists Blue Ladder Roofing's corporate office at 11722 Allisonville Rd Ste 103, Fishers, and records 6 employees.

 That figure almost certainly undercounts field crews and 1099 sales reps. 

Indeed reports salary data estimated from 211 employees, users, and past and present job advertisements

 — a sign of meaningful historical hiring volume but not necessarily current headcount. **Confidence: low.** Revenue is difficult to pin down without permit data; given 390 Google reviews accumulated since late 2019 and a multi-market footprint across Indiana and Missouri, a rough estimate of $3M–$6M annual revenue is plausible. **Confidence: low.**

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



A LinkedIn job posting for an Outside Sales Specialist at Blue Ladder Roofing was listed approximately one month ago.

 This is the only active posting surfaced. The Outside Sales Specialist role is consistent with their canvassing/door-knock model — they are hiring commission-based salespeople, not marketing or ops leadership. No marketing, project management, or operations director roles are currently posted. That absence suggests they are not building internal marketing infrastructure and remain reliant on field-driven lead generation.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Blue Ladder's Facebook page shows 96% recommendation rate from 14 Facebook reviews

 — a thin sample that is easy to manufacture. Yelp presence is nominal: 

their Yelp listing exists under "Indianapolis" but shows no published star rating or substantive review count, and the "how do I make an appointment" FAQ has zero answers posted

 — a dead page that nobody is managing. 

BBB accreditation was granted March 4, 2022

, and 

their current BBB rating is A+

. No Nextdoor business account was found in search results. The core discrepancy: 390 Google reviews vs. essentially zero managed presence on Yelp and Nextdoor. Classic review-funneling to Google only — a playbook that inflates GBP scores while leaving off-Google reputation entirely undefended.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Blue Ladder operates across at least three domains: [blueladderroofs.com](https://blueladderroofs.com), [blueladderroofingindy.com](https://www.blueladderroofingindy.com), and [blueladderroofingin.com](http://blueladderroofingin.com). Running parallel domains for the same brand is a split-authority problem that dilutes link equity across all three. 

The Fishers location page on blueladderroofs.com does attempt geo-specific content, addressing local weather issues like humidity, mold, and drainage

 — a reasonable local SEO tactic, but the copy is generic and templated, not authoritative. 

BuildZoom shows a score of 0 with no verified permit history surfaced, and no BuildZoom reviews exist for the entity

 — a gap that weakens their E-E-A-T signals. No evidence of local press backlinks or editorial coverage in Indiana media was found. Their IKO Craftsman Premier badge does earn them a [listing on the IKO contractor finder](https://contractorfinder.iko.com/contractors/blue-ladder-roofing-40538-fishers-in), which is a minor but real backlink. Schema markup and AEO-specific FAQ/HowTo structured data were not confirmed present. Their multi-domain fragmentation is their single biggest organic liability.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

No confirmed citations of Blue Ladder Roofing by name were surfaced in AI-generated results for "best roofers Indianapolis," "top roofing contractor near Greenwood Indiana," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," or "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville." Their split-domain architecture, thin editorial backlink profile, and absence of authoritative local press coverage all work against AI citation. Generative engines (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) favor entities with consistent NAP signals, strong review velocity, and third-party editorial mentions — none of which Blue Ladder has cleanly consolidated. This is a live opportunity for Raptor to own AEO positioning in the Fishers/Carmel/Noblesville corridor before Blue Ladder gets their domain strategy sorted.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where Blue Ladder beats Raptor:** Door-to-door canvassing infrastructure and multi-state market reach give them volume lead generation that a premium-positioned competitor does not match. Their insurance claim framing — 

"we handle the paperwork, work with your provider, and maximize your coverage"

 — is a highly effective conversion message for storm-damaged homeowners who feel overwhelmed.

**Where Raptor beats Blue Ladder:** 673 reviews at a perfect 5.0 vs. 390 at 4.8 is a meaningful GBP signal gap. A 0.0% owner response rate on Blue Ladder's Google reviews is a glaring accountability deficit that Raptor's premium "we don't outsource accountability" positioning directly exploits. Raptor's review velocity (12 in 30 days) is competitive with Blue Ladder's (12 in 30 days), but Raptor's rating integrity is untouchable.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Blue Ladder's 0.0% owner response rate on Google, combined with their fragmented multi-domain SEO and zero Yelp/Nextdoor presence, makes them easy to outflank on the trust-and-transparency axis that AI engines and premium buyers increasingly weight.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Insurance claim positioning as a front-door message.** 

Blue Ladder leads with "insurance claim experts — guidance through the claim process to maximize coverage"

 on every geo page. This is the right message for storm-season lead gen. Raptor can own the same frame with a credibility layer Blue Ladder cannot match: a named owner, a 5.0 rating, and a verifiable response record.

2. **Geo-specific landing pages.** Blue Ladder has built out individual pages for Fishers, Indianapolis, Carmel, and other cities on blueladderroofs.com. The pages are thin, but the structure is right. Raptor should audit whether it has equivalent dedicated pages for Carmel, Noblesville, Zionsville, Greenwood, and Fishers, and ensure each one has schema markup and genuine local content — not just a city name swap.

3. **Facebook social monitoring.** 

At least one verified customer review notes that Blue Ladder's reps actively monitor Facebook community posts about roofing inspections and respond directly

 — a low-cost social listening tactic that generates warm inbound leads. Cameron should evaluate whether Raptor has a system for monitoring Nextdoor and local Facebook group posts for storm damage or roof questions in the primary service zip codes.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief — ARAC Roof It Forward
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Refreshed: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



In business since 2005, ARAC Roof It Forward has many years of experience offering high-quality roofing services to local residential and commercial customers.

 They operate out of 

15499 Stony Creek Way, Noblesville, IN 46060

 and are a franchise/multi-market operation — 

founded in 2005, ARAC Roof It Forward is based out of Woodstock, Georgia

, with the Indianapolis location functioning as a regional branch. Their core differentiator is cause-based marketing: 

through their Roof It Forward program they have made a commitment to give back to the community a portion of every dollar that comes into the company through partnerships with local charities.

 On the Indianapolis-specific site, that charity is 

Peyton Manning Children's Hospital.

## 2. Estimated Scale



Datanyze estimates ARAC Roof It Forward revenue at $15.9M with 96 employees across the enterprise.

ZoomInfo notes ARAC Roof It Forward has raised under $5 million in one funding round

, suggesting they bootstrapped most of the operation and the Indiana branch is not a separately capitalized entity.
