## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Two active signals worth flagging. First, 

ARAC Roof It Forward is looking for an experienced Canvassing Manager to join their team, responsible for managing a team of canvassers and ensuring they meet their goals.

 A canvassing manager hire is a volume-play, storm-chase move — they are building a door-knocking army, not a referral engine. Second, 

ZoomInfo flags that ARAC Roof It Forward has more open roles in Sales than at any point in the past 12 months,

 with 

technologies listed including Salesforce and Google Reviews.

 as of June 2025. 

Glassdoor shows 24 open positions

 across the organization. No marketing, ops leadership, or CMO-level hires detected — their growth lever is clearly field sales headcount, not brand.

## 4. Off-Google Presence

The off-Google picture is fractured. 

Yelp lists them at 15503 Stony Creek Way, Noblesville

 — a slight address discrepancy vs. the official 15499. No visible Yelp star rating was returned in search results, suggesting thin or suppressed Yelp presence relative to their 310-review Google profile. 

They are BBB accredited since March 6, 2015

 and 

carry an A+ BBB rating.

one 2025 customer hired them after a tree fall, the roof wasn't replaced until July, and as of October the roof was sagging, buckling, and sheathing was damaged.

 A second BBB complaint documents 

a customer in June 2025 where the service drop worsened significantly after install, dropping to under 6 feet in some areas.

 

Their Indiana Facebook page has only 650 likes with 1 person talking about them

 — effectively a dormant channel. 

They maintain a Nextdoor listing as a full-service contractor

 but engagement is not visible. **Key discrepancy: 4.7 Google, active BBB complaints in 2025 = review funneling almost certain.**

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

ARAC runs a notably aggressive geo-page SEO strategy. Their domain [roofitforward.com](https://www.roofitforward.com) hosts dedicated landing pages for Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, Zionsville, Brownsburg, Plainfield, Anderson, and Greenfield —

 They also operate a second Indiana-specific domain, [roofitforwardindiana.com](https://www.roofitforwardindiana.com), creating potential duplicate-content risk but also two shots at ranking.

, which earns backlinks from the Owens Corning contractor directory — a legitimate DA-boosting link. Their site copy is repetitive and thin on blog/thought-leadership content; no evidence of schema markup investment or AEO-targeted FAQ structures was found. 

Their free video inspection landing page framing ("we bring the roof down to you") is a conversion hook

 that could rank for intent-rich queries — Raptor should audit whether that page is outranking equivalent Raptor content.

, a platform LLMs frequently pull contractor citations from; and (3) their Owens Corning Platinum Preferred status is a certification signal that appears in structured directories. Raptor's 673 reviews at 5.0 stars with an active cadence is a stronger AEO signal if properly structured with FAQ schema and location-specific content.

a portion of every dollar goes to fund a local beneficiary, and this is not a one-time deal but a percentage of revenue from every completed job.

**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Erie Home, founded in 1982 and headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, is a leading direct-to-consumer residential re-roofing platform operating across North America.

 

Pat Trompeter is the company's founder (now Chairman of the Board), with Jenilee Common serving as CEO and Randy Hamilton as President.

 Their differentiator is a fully vertically integrated model — 

Erie handles the end-to-end process from lead generation through final installation, positioning themselves on the peace-of-mind pitch rather than local craftsmanship.

 Critically, 

as of September 8, 2025, Erie Home was acquired by Leaf Home

, folding it into the largest DTC residential home services platform in North America — a post-acquisition integration dynamic that should be front of mind for Raptor.

## 2. Estimated Scale



Erie Home ranked #4 on Roofing Contractor's 2025 Top 100 list with reported annual revenue of $609 million in 2024.

 **Confidence: High** (cited in trade press with named list ranking.) 

The company operates more than 90 locations across 37 states.

 For headcount, 

Indeed estimates salary data from 10,700+ employees, users, and past/present job advertisements

 — suggesting a workforce north of 3,000–5,000 FTEs nationally. **Confidence: Medium** (no hard FTE figure publicly confirmed post-acquisition). The Indianapolis location is one branch of a national machine; local decision-making authority is limited.

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



Erie Home's active Indeed posting for Indianapolis lists roofing subcontractors, noting the company has been ranked in the Top 10 on the Qualified Remodeler Top 500 list for consecutive years.

 

ZipRecruiter shows multiple "Hiring Immediately for Roofing Subcontractors" listings — Erie is actively seeking crews for consistent, year-round work.

 

Nationally, Erie is recruiting Sales Representatives with commission structures averaging $2,500 per sale, citing $600M+ in annual revenue as a recruitment hook.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or branch management postings were identified for Indianapolis specifically in the last 30 days. The subcontractor-heavy hiring posture confirms Erie does not self-perform installs locally — a meaningful accountability gap Raptor can exploit.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

Erie's Indianapolis Google profile sits at 277 reviews / 4.6 stars with **zero reviews in the last 90 days and no owner responses on record** — a dead profile for a company this size. This is not organic momentum; it reads as a centrally managed, now-neglected local GBP. 

Erie claims an A+ BBB rating nationally

, but the BBB profile is managed from Toledo — there is no Indianapolis-specific BBB entity. 

Consumer Affairs reviews nationally include complaints about leaking roofs post-installation and improper ridge vent installation

 — the kind of execution failures consistent with a subcontractor-dependent model. 

LinkedIn marketing copy touts "outstanding ratings across all major review sites including Google, BBB, GuildQuality, TrustPilot, Birdeye, Indeed and Glassdoor"

 — but the Indianapolis Google stagnation tells a different story. No active Facebook Ad Library presence was confirmed for the Indianapolis market specifically at time of this brief.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

[eriehome.com](https://eriehome.com) is a nationally scaled domain with substantial authority derived from press coverage of the Leaf Home acquisition, Roofing Contractor Top 100 citations, and PR wire syndication. The Indianapolis location page ([eriehome.com/locations/roofing/indianapolis-in/](https://eriehome.com/locations/roofing/indianapolis-in/)) is templated and thin. 

It targets Indianapolis, Carmel, Greenwood, and Lawrence in copy

 but reads like a scaled location page, not locally authored content. 

The site's HTML is 154.96 KB — more than 4x the average — which can negatively impact load times and user experience.

 No evidence of a local Indianapolis blog content strategy or backlinks from Indy-specific media (IBJ, IndyStar, Indy Chamber). Their AEO posture nationally is strong due to brand volume, but locally they are invisible in terms of schema-rich, city-specific content that would drive AI citation.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Erie Home, due to sheer national revenue scale ($609M, Top 5 nationally) and the high-profile Leaf Home acquisition press coverage, is likely cited in generic "largest roofing companies" AI answers. However, for hyper-local queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," or "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville," Erie's thin, templated location pages provide weak AEO signals. AI engines favor locally specific, structured, review-rich content — Raptor's 673 reviews at 5.0 stars, combined with locally authored content targeting those exact suburb queries, represents a direct opportunity to outrank Erie in generative engine responses for Central Indiana. Erie's post-acquisition integration noise is also likely suppressing any new AEO content investment at the local level right now.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Erie beats Raptor:** National brand recognition, a lifetime warranty product, third-party financing at scale, and a $609M revenue machine that can spend on paid media without flinching. Their workaterie.com recruitment engine and Sales MIT program means they can flood local markets with commission-driven reps quickly.

**Where Raptor beats Erie:** Raptor holds a 5.0 star rating at 673 reviews vs Erie's 4.6 at 277 with zero recent review velocity — a dead signal in Google's local algorithm. Erie's subcontractor installation model is its most exploitable weakness: 

Erie is a "one call close" company where reps must convince homeowners to pay 3–4x what they expected for a product they did not ask about

 — the exact opposite of Raptor's accountability positioning. The most exploitable weakness: **zero owner responses on the Indianapolis GBP in any recorded window** — Cameron can weaponize this contrast in sales conversations and review strategy immediately.

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Subcontractor disclosure as a sales tool.** Erie's own Indianapolis job reviews note the install model's friction. Cameron should build a direct comparison into sales scripts and proposal decks: Raptor uses its own crews, Erie uses subcontractors. Make it a documented close, not just a verbal point.

2. **Lifetime warranty language.** 

Erie's CEO pitch is "we will be with you for the rest of the life of the roof and the next one."

 That is a powerful retention and close narrative. Evaluate whether Raptor's warranty language is as visceral and forward-looking in collateral.

3. **Monitor the Leaf Home integration for local service degradation.** 

The September 2025 Leaf Home acquisition combined two DTC leaders into one entity

 — integrations of this scale historically cause local customer service gaps, slower lead response, and review stagnation (which is already showing in Indy). Set a Google Alerts cadence for "Erie Home Indianapolis" and "Leaf Home Indianapolis" and be ready to surge Raptor's local paid media when Erie's GBP rating starts slipping.

## Bone Dry Roofing - Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard**
**Refreshed: Tuesday, May 20, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

Owner Gene Judd grew up the son of a roofing contractor in Illinois, graduated from Indiana University, and stayed in central Indiana to build the company.

 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 20 businesses in eight states, including 11 Midwest locations plus Bone Dry Roofing West, Florida, Commercial, Roof One, QRS, Ravlin's, RCV, and Gary's Roofing

 — making them a regional roll-up operator, not a pure local competitor. Their core identity is volume-driven "peace of mind" service backed by deep manufacturer relationships; 

they hold Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor and CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster Applicator status.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



As of their 2023 Residential Contractor of the Year profile, Bone Dry reported 500 employees company-wide, with a scope of 81% residential and 19% commercial.

 

LeadIQ pegged company-wide headcount at approximately 240 employees as of March 2026

 — indicating meaningful variance across data sources. **Confidence: medium** (estimates range from 240 to 500 depending on whether subsidiary headcount is consolidated). On revenue: 

ZoomInfo notes that the hiring of a new CFO and COO came "on the heels of Bone Dry Roofing's financial performance in 2023 that included revenue of over $183 million."

 

Of the $121M reported in 2022, approximately $36 million (30%) came from the Indianapolis office alone.

 **Revenue confidence: medium** — the Indianapolis location is likely a $40-50M+ operation on its own by 2025 based on trajectory.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active and broad. 

There are currently 78 open jobs at Bone Dry Roofing Inc., with 21 of those based in Indianapolis.

 Roles posted on ZipRecruiter and Indeed include: 

Assistant Production Manager

; 

Systems Analyst for business operations, noted as being in "growth mode"

; 

Division Manager (Roofing), responsible for overall management of sales and production

; and 

Home Solution Specialists (in-home sales reps) and Commercial Service Technicians.

 The Systems Analyst and Division Manager postings are the ones to watch — ops-level builds like that precede market expansion pushes. No standalone marketing coordinator or CMO-level hire is currently visible in Indiana, which tracks with their in-house CMO (Matt Tyner) being tenured.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, the Indianapolis location at 7735 Winton Dr has 75 reviews

 — versus 2,422 on Google. That is a 97% review-funneling gap, the clearest sign in this market of a team that has mastered Google review capture but has done nothing to cultivate Yelp. Their Facebook presence (

825 likes, 264 people talking about it

) is active but thin for a company of their scale. The UTM parameters in their Facebook profile links (`utm_campaign=profile-link&campaign_code=BDR-DIG-ORGS-ROOF-IN-PHO-FB-202402`) show they are tracking social-to-web traffic with some discipline. 

They carry an A+ BBB rating and have won multiple Angie's List Super Service Awards.

 

They have a partnership with Indy Humane

 that generates community goodwill mentions. BBB complaints page is live but complaint volume is not alarming based on available data. No notable Reddit presence identified for the Indy location.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Bone Dry operates `bonedry.com` with a dedicated subdirectory at `bonedry.com/indianapolis/` and location-specific service pages (e.g., `bonedry.com/indianapolis/roofing/`). 

Their tech stack includes WordPress, Adobe Premiere Pro, Webpack, and Module Federation

 — a competent but not cutting-edge setup. The Indianapolis page targets head terms like "roofing contractor Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Indianapolis" with repetitive on-page copy rather than topical authority content. No evidence of a robust blog targeting long-tail question queries ("how much does a roof cost in Carmel IN," etc.) — their content investment appears shallow relative to their domain age and backlink footprint. Their multi-location architecture gives them a domain authority advantage that a single-location operator cannot easily replicate; `bonedry.com` almost certainly carries a DA of 45+ based on press coverage, Owens Corning partner links, and the [2023 Roofing Contractor Magazine profile](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing). AEO posture is not differentiated — no visible FAQ schema, no structured "ask" content targeting voice or AI-surfaced queries.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry Roofing is almost certainly named in AI answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. The combination of their volume (2,422 Google reviews), national press coverage (Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Contractor of the Year), multi-state footprint, and aged domain makes them a high-probability citation for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Their BBB A+ status and F.C. Tucker partnership (

Bone Dry is a member of F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

) generate structured third-party mentions that LLMs index heavily. However, their lack of specific suburb-level content (Zionsville, Fishers, Noblesville pages are thin or absent) creates a gap — AI answers for hyper-local prompts like "roofing company Fishers Noblesville" are less certain. Raptor should be targeting exactly those prompts with purpose-built content.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Bone Dry beats Raptor:** Review volume is not close — 2,422 vs. 673 — and that gap alone dominates Local Pack rankings and AI citation frequency. They have a named CMO (Matt Tyner), an in-house training academy (Bone Dry University), a multi-channel sales system, company-provided vehicles for reps, and a national award that functions as evergreen PR. 

Their policy of keeping a production supervisor on-site for every project's duration

 is a process differentiator that is easy to market and hard to argue against. **Where Raptor beats Bone Dry:** A 5.0 star rating versus 4.8 is a genuine differentiator at the premium tier — no sophisticated buyer reads 2,422 reviews; they filter by rating first. Raptor's accountability positioning ("we don't outsource accountability") hits directly at the most common grievance in Bone Dry's employee reviews. **Most exploitable weakness:** 

Indeed reviews score Bone Dry's management accountability at 3.3 out of 5, with employees noting that "higher up managers are not held accountable for anything" and feel "disconnected."

 That internal dysfunction surfaces in customer experience — Raptor's owner-present, single-market focus is the direct counter-positioning.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

**1. On-site production supervisor as a standard deliverable.** 

Bone Dry's policy of a production supervisor present for the entire project, with no payment taken until the customer has "expressed total agreement and satisfaction," is a process they market explicitly.

 Raptor should formalize and name an equivalent standard in all sales materials and on the website — make it a named commitment, not just a verbal promise.

**2. The F.C. Tucker referral partnership.** 

Bone Dry is embedded in F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

 — an inbound referral channel from one of Indy's dominant real estate brands. Raptor should identify equivalent real estate brokerage, insurance agent, and property management partnership channels that Bone Dry is not already locked into. These are pre-qualified, high-intent homeowner referrals that bypass paid search entirely.

**3. Formalized veteran and first responder discount as a brand signal.** 

Bone Dry has partnered with Military.com and pledged support for the veteran community

 as a recruiting and PR tool. 

Their discount program covers military members, veterans, senior citizens, first responders, teachers, and healthcare professionals.

 Raptor should either match this with a cleaner, more premium-positioned version (fewer categories, stronger guarantee) or own a distinct community vertical Bone Dry has not claimed.

 In a trust-driven category, longevity of proof matters. Their 5.0 rating sounds perfect — but to sophisticated homeowners, a "perfect" score from a small sample base signals a curated, early-stage reputation, not a battle-tested one.

**Weakness 2: Their entire lead engine is a single-channel dependency.**
Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads — full stop.

Raptor leans on community sponsorships in Greenwood and Center Grove and messaging about "not outsourcing accountability." That is positioning, not proof.

**Out-spend them on Google LSA in their own backyard zip codes — specifically 46142 (Greenwood) and 46143 (Center Grove) — with an uncapped weekly budget and a 60-second lead response SLA, while simultaneously flooding those neighborhoods with yard signs from active jobs.**

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing — Cameron Blakely, CMO Dashboard**
*Refreshed: Thursday, May 22, 2025*

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they serve both residential and commercial customers as a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor, and hold memberships in good standing with the BBB (A+), the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They now operate with locations in both Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, making them a multi-market operator — a meaningful scale distinction from most Indy competitors. Their core differentiator is a full-service exterior platform: roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, and commercial painting all under one roof, with a heavy lean into insurance claims navigation.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach puts annual revenue at $28.6 million (2025 estimate) with 57 employees.

 

Prospeo independently estimates approximately 51–100 employees.

 **Confidence: medium.** Revenue figures from third-party data aggregators carry noise, but the $12M–$29M range across multiple sources is plausible for a 50+ year old multi-trade operation with a 3,000+ review velocity. 

A PPP loan of $584,200 from Stock Yards Bank resulted in the reported retention of 40 jobs

, which provides a floor on their W-2 headcount. 

Known leadership includes a Director of Sales, a VP of Construction (Todd Danbom), and a Marketing Director (Charles Crowley).



---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



ZipRecruiter shows an open Team Lead, Field Marketing role in Indianapolis.

 

Their own careers page is actively recruiting Home Improvement Sales Consultants, trained to "out-sell the competition," running both company-provided leads and self-generated referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags an open Estimator & Project Manager role in Indianapolis.

 The Field Marketing Team Lead posting is the one to watch — it signals they are expanding or restructuring canvassing operations, which is their dominant top-of-funnel model. A marketing specialist role was also recently active per Glassdoor. No C-suite or digital marketing director-level hires detected in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**



Amos Roofing & Exteriors holds only 2.5 stars on Yelp

 against their 4.9 on Google — a significant platform disparity that is a textbook review-funneling signal. They are clearly driving customers to Google and not managing Yelp proactively. 

Facebook shows 1,383 likes with only 23 people "talking about this"

 — minimal organic engagement for a company of their scale, suggesting Facebook is largely dormant. No active Facebook Ad Library presence was confirmed. 

BBB-accredited since September 1993

 with an A+ rating and active recent reviews. 

On Angi, they carry a 4.5 overall rating

 — solid but not perfect. GuildQuality shows verified reviews including some negative feedback around siding quality and communication, concentrated in 2017–2018 but visible in search.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Amos Exteriors runs on WordPress with PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — a legacy tech stack that likely limits Core Web Vitals performance and structured data execution. They have built out a deep location/service page architecture (e.g., [amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) which generates decent long-tail coverage across Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood. They are ranking for core Indy roofing queries on the strength of domain age (54 years) and review volume. However, the jQuery 1.11.1 version is outdated by roughly a decade, which is a schema implementation and page speed liability. No evidence of a robust backlink strategy from local press or Indy-area publications. Their blog exists but content cadence appears irregular. The GAF Master Elite designation earns them a high-authority inbound link from [gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential/usa/in/indianapolis/amos-exteriors-inc-1113337) which Raptor should match or counter.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current AI engine behavior for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," and "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville": Amos Exteriors is likely to appear in AI-generated answers by virtue of their review volume (3,098 Google reviews), domain age, multi-location page structure, and GAF Master Elite certification — all of which are strong citation signals for LLMs pulling from structured web data. Their 54-year operating history and BBB A+ accreditation since 1993 further boost entity authority in knowledge graph indexing. Raptor, with 675 reviews and a 5.0 rating, is a thinner entity profile at this stage. The gap is not about quality — it is about entity depth and crawlable citation surface area. Raptor should be building AEO-optimized FAQ schema, press mentions, and third-party citation anchors (NRCA membership, GAF certification page, local news features) to close this AI visibility gap.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,098 vs. 675), domain age, multi-trade service breadth, Lafayette market expansion, and an in-house marketing department with named Director of Marketing and Marketing Manager on the BBB profile. Their insurance claims navigation operation is a well-oiled machine with dedicated reps named throughout reviews. **Where Raptor beats Amos:** Raptor holds a 5.0 vs. 4.9 — the cleanest rating in the Indy top 10 by volume — and runs a premium, accountable positioning that Amos cannot credibly claim given Glassdoor complaints about sales rep quality, canvassing no-shows, and a 2.5 Yelp rating. The most exploitable weakness: 

Amos canvassers are reportedly setting appointments where "the homeowner either doesn't know you're coming, or doesn't understand why you're there"

 — a trust and brand integrity gap Raptor can hammer directly in paid and social messaging.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **Location-specific service page architecture.** 

Amos explicitly builds out named suburb service areas including Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Geist, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, Franklin, and Anderson

 with dedicated URLs. Raptor should audit whether it has comparable depth — each suburb page is an independent AEO and local SEO asset.

2. **Multi-trade upsell model.** 

Amos installs GAF asphalt shingles, slate, cedar shake, and flat systems as a GAF Master Elite Contractor with System Plus Warranty coverage

, and upsells into siding, gutters, windows, and masonry on the same job. Monitor whether their average ticket size is growing through multi-trade attachment — this is the revenue-per-customer lever Raptor should have an opinion on.

3. **GuildQuality third-party review pipeline.** Amos pipes verified customer surveys through [GuildQuality](https://www.guildquality.com/profile/amos-exteriors-inc), which generates an independent review corpus that feeds AEO signals. Cameron should evaluate whether adding a GuildQuality or similar verified-survey layer gives Raptor an additional citation source that AI engines pull when surfacing contractor recommendations.

## Bone Dry Roofing - Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard**
**Refreshed: Tuesday, May 20, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

Owner Gene Judd grew up the son of a roofing contractor in Illinois, graduated from Indiana University, and stayed in central Indiana to build the company.

 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans 20 businesses in eight states, including 11 Midwest locations plus Bone Dry Roofing West, Florida, Commercial, Roof One, QRS, Ravlin's, RCV, and Gary's Roofing

 — making them a regional roll-up operator, not a pure local competitor. Their core identity is volume-driven "peace of mind" service backed by deep manufacturer relationships; 

they hold Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor and CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster Applicator status.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



As of their 2023 Residential Contractor of the Year profile, Bone Dry reported 500 employees company-wide, with a scope of 81% residential and 19% commercial.

 

LeadIQ pegged company-wide headcount at approximately 240 employees as of March 2026

 — indicating meaningful variance across data sources. **Confidence: medium** (estimates range from 240 to 500 depending on whether subsidiary headcount is consolidated). On revenue: 

ZoomInfo notes that the hiring of a new CFO and COO came "on the heels of Bone Dry Roofing's financial performance in 2023 that included revenue of over $183 million."

 

Of the $121M reported in 2022, approximately $36 million (30%) came from the Indianapolis office alone.

 **Revenue confidence: medium** — the Indianapolis location is likely a $40-50M+ operation on its own by 2025 based on trajectory.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active and broad. 

There are currently 78 open jobs at Bone Dry Roofing Inc., with 21 of those based in Indianapolis.

 Roles posted on ZipRecruiter and Indeed include: 

Assistant Production Manager

; 

Systems Analyst for business operations, noted as being in "growth mode"

; 

Division Manager (Roofing), responsible for overall management of sales and production

; and 

Home Solution Specialists (in-home sales reps) and Commercial Service Technicians.

 The Systems Analyst and Division Manager postings are the ones to watch — ops-level builds like that precede market expansion pushes. No standalone marketing coordinator or CMO-level hire is currently visible in Indiana, which tracks with their in-house CMO (Matt Tyner) being tenured.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, the Indianapolis location at 7735 Winton Dr has 75 reviews

 — versus 2,422 on Google. That is a 97% review-funneling gap, the clearest sign in this market of a team that has mastered Google review capture but has done nothing to cultivate Yelp. Their Facebook presence (

825 likes, 264 people talking about it

) is active but thin for a company of their scale. The UTM parameters in their Facebook profile links (`utm_campaign=profile-link&campaign_code=BDR-DIG-ORGS-ROOF-IN-PHO-FB-202402`) show they are tracking social-to-web traffic with some discipline. 

They carry an A+ BBB rating and have won multiple Angie's List Super Service Awards.

 

They have a partnership with Indy Humane

 that generates community goodwill mentions. BBB complaints page is live but complaint volume is not alarming based on available data. No notable Reddit presence identified for the Indy location.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Bone Dry operates `bonedry.com` with a dedicated subdirectory at `bonedry.com/indianapolis/` and location-specific service pages (e.g., `bonedry.com/indianapolis/roofing/`). 

Their tech stack includes WordPress, Adobe Premiere Pro, Webpack, and Module Federation

 — a competent but not cutting-edge setup. The Indianapolis page targets head terms like "roofing contractor Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Indianapolis" with repetitive on-page copy rather than topical authority content. No evidence of a robust blog targeting long-tail question queries ("how much does a roof cost in Carmel IN," etc.) — their content investment appears shallow relative to their domain age and backlink footprint. Their multi-location architecture gives them a domain authority advantage that a single-location operator cannot easily replicate; `bonedry.com` almost certainly carries a DA of 45+ based on press coverage, Owens Corning partner links, and the [2023 Roofing Contractor Magazine profile](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing). AEO posture is not differentiated — no visible FAQ schema, no structured "ask" content targeting voice or AI-surfaced queries.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry Roofing is almost certainly named in AI answers for broad Indianapolis roofing queries. The combination of their volume (2,422 Google reviews), national press coverage (Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Contractor of the Year), multi-state footprint, and aged domain makes them a high-probability citation for prompts like "best roofers Indianapolis" or "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Their BBB A+ status and F.C. Tucker partnership (

Bone Dry is a member of F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

) generate structured third-party mentions that LLMs index heavily. However, their lack of specific suburb-level content (Zionsville, Fishers, Noblesville pages are thin or absent) creates a gap — AI answers for hyper-local prompts like "roofing company Fishers Noblesville" are less certain. Raptor should be targeting exactly those prompts with purpose-built content.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Bone Dry beats Raptor:** Review volume is not close — 2,422 vs. 673 — and that gap alone dominates Local Pack rankings and AI citation frequency. They have a named CMO (Matt Tyner), an in-house training academy (Bone Dry University), a multi-channel sales system, company-provided vehicles for reps, and a national award that functions as evergreen PR. 

Their policy of keeping a production supervisor on-site for every project's duration

 is a process differentiator that is easy to market and hard to argue against. **Where Raptor beats Bone Dry:** A 5.0 star rating versus 4.8 is a genuine differentiator at the premium tier — no sophisticated buyer reads 2,422 reviews; they filter by rating first. Raptor's accountability positioning ("we don't outsource accountability") hits directly at the most common grievance in Bone Dry's employee reviews. **Most exploitable weakness:** 

Indeed reviews score Bone Dry's management accountability at 3.3 out of 5, with employees noting that "higher up managers are not held accountable for anything" and feel "disconnected."

 That internal dysfunction surfaces in customer experience — Raptor's owner-present, single-market focus is the direct counter-positioning.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

**1. On-site production supervisor as a standard deliverable.** 

Bone Dry's policy of a production supervisor present for the entire project, with no payment taken until the customer has "expressed total agreement and satisfaction," is a process they market explicitly.

 Raptor should formalize and name an equivalent standard in all sales materials and on the website — make it a named commitment, not just a verbal promise.

**2. The F.C. Tucker referral partnership.** 

Bone Dry is embedded in F.C. Tucker's Home Services network

 — an inbound referral channel from one of Indy's dominant real estate brands. Raptor should identify equivalent real estate brokerage, insurance agent, and property management partnership channels that Bone Dry is not already locked into. These are pre-qualified, high-intent homeowner referrals that bypass paid search entirely.

**3. Formalized veteran and first responder discount as a brand signal.** 

Bone Dry has partnered with Military.com and pledged support for the veteran community

 as a recruiting and PR tool. 

Their discount program covers military members, veterans, senior citizens, first responders, teachers, and healthcare professionals.

 Raptor should either match this with a cleaner, more premium-positioned version (fewer categories, stronger guarantee) or own a distinct community vertical Bone Dry has not claimed.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Indy Roof & Restoration
**Refreshed:** Tuesday, May 20, 2025 | **Subject:** [indyroofandrestoration.com](https://indyroofandrestoration.com)

---

## 1. Who They Are



Aaron Christy founded Indy Roof & Restoration in 2018.

 

The company is led by founder Aaron Christy and COO Adam Kaminski

, with 

Greg Russell serving as Operations Manager per BBB records.

 Their core identity is storm restoration and insurance advocacy — 

they lean heavily on working with insurance companies and positioning themselves as trusted by real estate agents and residential and commercial customers throughout central Indiana.

 Structurally they operate as a full exterior GC: 

roofs, gutters, siding, interior work, and anything else damaged during a storm.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale

**Confidence: medium.** Multiple data sources converge in the 25–50 employee range. 

Clodura.AI lists them at 11–50 employees total

, while 

SignalHire estimates approximately 30 employees.

 

Growjo estimates annual revenue of $10.9M with 47 employees

 — the most aggressive estimate in the dataset, though Growjo skews high. 

Prospeo pegs annual revenue closer to $2.4M

, which appears to undercount significantly given their review velocity and GC scope. A $5M–$10M ARR range is the most defensible read. 

Growjo did note they grew employee count by 38% in the prior year

 — a meaningful signal regardless of which revenue figure is correct.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Their 

careers page actively solicits "driven individuals" emphasizing personal and professional growth

, and 

commission-based Field Inspectors are a standing open role, with the primary function of roof and exterior inspections and guiding homeowners through the insurance process.

 

Indeed also shows an active Water & Mold Restoration Sales posting, requiring experience in water damage restoration or mitigation sales

 — a signal they are pushing deeper into the interior restoration/mitigation vertical. 

Clodura's org chart shows a dedicated Marketing Director (Nick Segar) and Sales Manager (Daniel Ralston)

, both titles suggesting they have invested in internal marketing infrastructure, not just outsourced SEO. No VP- or Director-level ops hire detected in the last 30 days on ZipRecruiter or Indeed specific to Indy Roof.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence

The platform gap here is real and exploitable. 

Yelp has placed a Consumer Alert on their business page flagging abnormal activity or attempts to mislead consumers

 — a damaging signal that Yelp's algorithm has flagged suspected review manipulation. Against 2,202 Google reviews, 

Yelp shows only 28 reviews

 — a 79:1 ratio that is a textbook review-funneling pattern. 

Facebook shows 4,777 page likes and an 86% recommendation rate across 48 reviews

 — again a fraction of their Google volume. Their Facebook page is tied to the entity "INDY ROOF CO," which is a slightly different DBA and creates potential brand confusion. 

BBB-accredited since July 2019 with an A+ rating

, but the BBB complaint section contains at least one detailed narrative alleging a forged signature and cash payment irregularity from April 2025 — not yet resolved publicly at time of this brief. 

Community presence includes Brownsburg Little League Softball, Beech Grove High School Marching Band, Habitat for Humanity, and the Shelbyville Animal Shelter

, all of which generate local press and trust signals without paid placement.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture



A third-party 2026 Indianapolis roofing roundup (Stay Dry Roofing's own site) cites Indy Roof & Restoration as a strong regional company recognized for insurance advocacy and high review volume, calling them a top contender and honorable mention.

 That kind of third-party citation on a competitor's domain is a backlink signal worth watching — they are generating citation mentions even from rivals. Their website URL structure (service area pages for Carmel, Fishers, Greenwood, Brownsburg, Westfield, Zionsville per their 

careers page

) suggests a standard local SEO landing page strategy. 

ZoomInfo's tech stack shows Facebook Pixel, Facebook Web Custom Audiences, WordPress, and PHP

 — a fairly lean setup with no obvious schema-heavy CMS. No evidence of structured data investment or AEO-specific FAQ schema content surfaced. Their blog exists but is thin. The Red Rocket content subdomain (`indyroofandrestoration.redrocketcontent.com`) confirms they use Red Rocket as their SEO/content vendor, which is a local Indianapolis digital shop — not a national roofing-specialist agency.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Indy Roof & Restoration does appear in AI-generated local roundups. The Stay Dry Roofing roundup — which itself ranks in Google for Indy roofing queries — 

identifies them specifically for insurance advocacy and 24/7 emergency response, and recommends them for homeowners wanting intense insurance-claim support and mitigation services.

 That content will be scraped by LLMs and surface in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini responses to queries like "best storm damage roofer Indianapolis." However, their own domain does not appear to have AEO-optimized content (FAQ schema, structured Q&A, cited statistics) that would make them a primary source in generative answers. Their AI visibility is derivative — they show up because others write about them, not because their own content is structured for retrieval. That is a gap Raptor can exploit directly with properly structured AEO content targeting suburb-level queries (Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, Carmel).

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Sheer review volume — 2,202 vs. 673 — dominates the GBP proximity algorithm and creates an imposing social proof wall for undecided homeowners. Their insurance advocacy positioning and 24/7 emergency response branding gives them a clear lane during storm cycles. Community sponsorship visibility (Little League, high school band, Habitat) is a PR flywheel Raptor has not matched at that frequency.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 vs. 4.9 on Google — a meaningful delta at premium price points where buyers scrutinize. The Yelp Consumer Alert, the BBB complaint involving alleged forged signatures, and the 86% Facebook recommendation rate all create credible character vulnerabilities that a premium brand can exploit through contrast messaging. Raptor's "we don't outsource accountability" positioning is a direct counter-punch to a company that has documented sub-rep conduct issues.

**Most exploitable weakness:** The Yelp Consumer Alert for abnormal review activity combined with the 2025 BBB complaint about alleged forgery and cash demands gives Raptor a clean lane to run a "verified, accountable, no-surprises" campaign that doesn't need to name the competitor — the contrast speaks for itself.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Water & Mold Restoration Sales as a revenue extension.** Their active Indeed posting for this role is not accidental — interior mitigation is a high-margin adjacency that keeps them in the job longer per home. Cameron should evaluate whether Raptor has a referral partnership or upsell path into this category before Indy Roof locks up the relationships.

2. **The community sponsorship matrix.** 

Brownsburg Little League, Beech Grove Marching Band, Habitat for Humanity, Shelbyville Animal Shelter

 — these are hyper-local, low-cost, high-impression placements that generate organic social content, earned media, and Nextdoor word-of-mouth simultaneously. Raptor should map equivalent sponsorships in its primary zip codes before Indy Roof expands its footprint further north and west.

3. **Podcast and trade press positioning.** 

Aaron Christy appeared on a local podcast discussing his company's growth and the roofing industry

, and 

was quoted directly in the 2026 Roofing Contractor State of the Industry report

. That earned authority converts into AEO citations when LLMs pull industry sources. Cameron and Patrick should be pitching themselves to equivalent Indy-market podcasts and trade publications to build the same citation footprint — before Christy's voice becomes the default "Indianapolis roofer expert" in generative search results.

## 1. Who They Are

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Erie beats Raptor:** National brand recognition, a lifetime warranty product, third-party financing at scale, and a $609M revenue machine that can spend on paid media without flinching. Their workaterie.com recruitment engine and Sales MIT program means they can flood local markets with commission-driven reps quickly.

 Salary data from Indeed suggests the company draws from roughly 5,400 employee records across all markets.  — that integration can feed review automation and booking schema, which is a legitimate AEO signal. roofing websites that focus on a specific service and service area generate a tighter vector embedding than general contractors servicing the entire country.

 AmeriPro's location pages are thin and templated, reducing their semantic relevance in geo-specific AI prompts like "best roofer in Carmel Indiana" or "roof replacement Fishers." ## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where AmeriPro beats Raptor:** National brand halo and manufacturer credentials (GAF Master Elite President's Club, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred) carry weight in insurance-claim conversations; homeowners who've seen their yard signs across the neighborhood have pre-built familiarity.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief — Cochran Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 2010, Cochran Exteriors has built its reputation as a central Indiana exterior remodeling contractor.

 

The company is co-owned by Ross Cochran and John Cochran

, with 

Brad Baugh serving as Brand President

 — a title that signals an Infinity Home Services-era executive layer above the founding family. 

Cochran Exteriors was acquired by Infinity Home Services in June 2022

, making it a platform company asset, not an independent operator — a fact they do not prominently advertise to consumers. 

Their service scope covers roofing, siding, windows, doors, and gutters across Indianapolis and central Indiana.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



PitchBook lists Cochran Exteriors at 43 total employees

, while 

ZoomInfo brackets them at 11–50 employees at their Indianapolis headquarters.

 **Confidence: medium.** On revenue, sources diverge: 

RocketReach estimates 2025 annual revenue at $6.8 million

, while 

CIENCE puts the range at $10–25 million.

 The spread reflects the opacity of a private subsidiary. Given the 1,187 Google review count, two physical office locations, and national Top 100 Roofing Contractor recognition, the $8–12M working estimate is most defensible. **Confidence: low.** Notably, 

Cochran Exteriors received an SBA PPP loan of $1–2 million from Regions Bank, supporting retention of 47 jobs

 — the strongest independent headcount signal available.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Two active hiring signals found on LinkedIn within recent months: 

Cochran posted for a Commercial Estimator in Indianapolis

, and 

also posted for a Residential Sales Consultant in Indianapolis.

 The Commercial Estimator post is the more strategically significant signal — it confirms they are pushing harder into the commercial segment, likely driven by Infinity Home Services' margin requirements. No marketing, ops leadership, or digital/AEO roles were identified in current postings, which is a notable gap given the scale of their review velocity.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Cochran Exteriors holds BBB Accreditation with an A+ rating

 and 

maintains two physical locations: 8461 Castlewood Dr, Indianapolis, and 48 N Emerson Ave, Suite 600, Greenwood.

 

They have been named one of the Top 100 Roofing Contractors in the nation

 — a credentialing claim they deploy across Yelp, Nextdoor, and their own site. On Yelp, they have only 54 reviews ([cochranexteriors-indianapolis-2](https://www.yelp.com/biz/cochran-exteriors-indianapolis-2)) against 1,187 on Google — a textbook review-funneling gap. The BBB complaint file is worth watching: 

at least one reviewer states "Avoid this company. They will weasel out of poor workmanship. Warranty isn't worth the paper it was written on."

 Separately, 

a BBB reviewer noted that a crew member asked them to leave a good review so he could get "stars" and a bonus

 — a structurally risky incentive model that inflates volume at the cost of authenticity. 

On Nextdoor, Cochran comes up positively recommended for roofing, windows, gutters, and siding, with customers praising the team's professionalism.

 

Their tech stack includes Google Ads Conversion Tracking and Microsoft Clarity

, confirming active paid media and on-site behavioral tracking.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Cochran's domain ([cochranexteriors.com](https://www.cochranexteriors.com)) is a 15-year-old root domain with consistent content investment. 

They maintain an active blog covering roofing, siding, and windows, positioning themselves as exterior remodeling educators.

 

They hold both Owens Corning Platinum and GAF Certified Contractor status

 — dual manufacturer certifications that generate authoritative backlinks and trust signals AI engines weight heavily. Their service area pages are geo-segmented (e.g., `/in/roofing`) and their Houzz profile lists neighborhood-specific landing pages (Castleton, Crows Nest, Rocky Ripple, Williams Creek, etc.) — a hyperlocal SEO strategy Raptor has room to counter. 

They also carry Angie's List Super Service Awards from 2012–2013 and NRCA membership

, which contribute to their backlink profile. No evidence of schema markup issues surfaced, and their use of Cloudflare and Bootstrap suggests a modern technical foundation.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Cochran Exteriors has meaningful AI citation exposure based on their profile: a 15-year-old domain, Top 100 Roofing Contractor designation, dual manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning Platinum + GAF), BBB A+ accreditation, and 1,187 Google reviews are exactly the structured trust signals that ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity pull when generating "best roofers Indianapolis" responses. Their blog content targets long-tail queries that AI engines scrape for sourcing. They are likely cited in generative results for broad Indianapolis roofing queries and storm damage/insurance claim contexts given how extensively their insurance claim assistance process is documented across review platforms. Raptor's 5.0 rating at 673 reviews is a stronger quality signal, but Cochran's volume and manufacturer credentials currently give them the AEO edge. Closing that gap requires schema-marked FAQ content, manufacturer credential pages, and press placements — none of which require ad spend.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (1,187 vs. 673), multi-location physical footprint, dual manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning Platinum + GAF), Top 100 national ranking, and a 15-year domain with hyperlocal SEO pages covering neighborhood-level queries Raptor has not yet captured.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 star rating vs. 4.7 (the difference matters at the premium price point), no corporate parent diluting the local accountability narrative, and zero credible evidence of incentivized review solicitation — which is a live liability for Cochran.

**Most exploitable weakness:** 

The documented practice of crews asking customers for reviews in exchange for "stars" and a bonus

 is a structural integrity problem that Raptor's owner-response model and authentic review velocity directly counters in any head-to-head sales conversation.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Neighborhood-level landing pages.** Cochran has built out pages targeting specific Indianapolis neighborhoods (Castleton, Rocky Ripple, Williams Creek, Wynnedale, etc.) with service-specific URL structures. These are low-cost AEO and local SEO assets. Raptor should build equivalent pages for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood with schema markup before Cochran's domain age advantage compounds further.

2. **Dual manufacturer certification as a content pillar.** 

Their Owens Corning Platinum and GAF Certified Contractor credentials

 are cited across every major directory profile and generate backlinks from manufacturer websites. If Raptor holds or can obtain comparable certifications, those credential pages need to be live, linked, and schema-marked — they are direct inputs into how generative AI ranks contractor recommendations.

3. **Commercial estimator expansion as a lead.** The active Commercial Estimator hire signals Cochran is moving budget and capacity toward commercial work. That creates a potential gap in their residential pipeline responsiveness — specifically in the suburban markets (Carmel, Fishers, Westfield) where Raptor competes on premium positioning. Cameron should monitor review cadence in those zip codes; a volume dip from Cochran in the next 60–90 days would confirm the commercial pivot is pulling attention away from residential.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief — Cochran Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Updated: May 19, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 2010, Cochran Exteriors has built its reputation as a central Indiana exterior remodeling contractor.

 

The company is co-owned by Ross Cochran and John Cochran

, with 

Brad Baugh serving as Brand President

 — a title that signals an Infinity Home Services-era executive layer above the founding family. 

Cochran Exteriors was acquired by Infinity Home Services in June 2022

, making it a platform company asset, not an independent operator — a fact they do not prominently advertise to consumers. 

Their service scope covers roofing, siding, windows, doors, and gutters across Indianapolis and central Indiana.



---

## 2. Estimated Scale



PitchBook lists Cochran Exteriors at 43 total employees

, while 

ZoomInfo brackets them at 11–50 employees at their Indianapolis headquarters.

 **Confidence: medium.** On revenue, sources diverge: 

RocketReach estimates 2025 annual revenue at $6.8 million

, while 

CIENCE puts the range at $10–25 million.

 The spread reflects the opacity of a private subsidiary. Given the 1,187 Google review count, two physical office locations, and national Top 100 Roofing Contractor recognition, the $8–12M working estimate is most defensible. **Confidence: low.** Notably, 

Cochran Exteriors received an SBA PPP loan of $1–2 million from Regions Bank, supporting retention of 47 jobs

 — the strongest independent headcount signal available.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Two active hiring signals found on LinkedIn within recent months: 

Cochran posted for a Commercial Estimator in Indianapolis

, and 

also posted for a Residential Sales Consultant in Indianapolis.

 The Commercial Estimator post is the more strategically significant signal — it confirms they are pushing harder into the commercial segment, likely driven by Infinity Home Services' margin requirements. No marketing, ops leadership, or digital/AEO roles were identified in current postings, which is a notable gap given the scale of their review velocity.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Cochran Exteriors holds BBB Accreditation with an A+ rating

 and 

maintains two physical locations: 8461 Castlewood Dr, Indianapolis, and 48 N Emerson Ave, Suite 600, Greenwood.

 

They have been named one of the Top 100 Roofing Contractors in the nation

 — a credentialing claim they deploy across Yelp, Nextdoor, and their own site. On Yelp, they have only 54 reviews ([cochranexteriors-indianapolis-2](https://www.yelp.com/biz/cochran-exteriors-indianapolis-2)) against 1,187 on Google — a textbook review-funneling gap. The BBB complaint file is worth watching: 

at least one reviewer states "Avoid this company. They will weasel out of poor workmanship. Warranty isn't worth the paper it was written on."

 Separately, 

a BBB reviewer noted that a crew member asked them to leave a good review so he could get "stars" and a bonus

 — a structurally risky incentive model that inflates volume at the cost of authenticity. 

On Nextdoor, Cochran comes up positively recommended for roofing, windows, gutters, and siding, with customers praising the team's professionalism.

 

Their tech stack includes Google Ads Conversion Tracking and Microsoft Clarity

, confirming active paid media and on-site behavioral tracking.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Cochran's domain ([cochranexteriors.com](https://www.cochranexteriors.com)) is a 15-year-old root domain with consistent content investment. 

They maintain an active blog covering roofing, siding, and windows, positioning themselves as exterior remodeling educators.

 

They hold both Owens Corning Platinum and GAF Certified Contractor status

 — dual manufacturer certifications that generate authoritative backlinks and trust signals AI engines weight heavily. Their service area pages are geo-segmented (e.g., `/in/roofing`) and their Houzz profile lists neighborhood-specific landing pages (Castleton, Crows Nest, Rocky Ripple, Williams Creek, etc.) — a hyperlocal SEO strategy Raptor has room to counter. 

They also carry Angie's List Super Service Awards from 2012–2013 and NRCA membership

, which contribute to their backlink profile. No evidence of schema markup issues surfaced, and their use of Cloudflare and Bootstrap suggests a modern technical foundation.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Cochran Exteriors has meaningful AI citation exposure based on their profile: a 15-year-old domain, Top 100 Roofing Contractor designation, dual manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning Platinum + GAF), BBB A+ accreditation, and 1,187 Google reviews are exactly the structured trust signals that ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity pull when generating "best roofers Indianapolis" responses. Their blog content targets long-tail queries that AI engines scrape for sourcing. They are likely cited in generative results for broad Indianapolis roofing queries and storm damage/insurance claim contexts given how extensively their insurance claim assistance process is documented across review platforms. Raptor's 5.0 rating at 673 reviews is a stronger quality signal, but Cochran's volume and manufacturer credentials currently give them the AEO edge. Closing that gap requires schema-marked FAQ content, manufacturer credential pages, and press placements — none of which require ad spend.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (1,187 vs. 673), multi-location physical footprint, dual manufacturer certifications (Owens Corning Platinum + GAF), Top 100 national ranking, and a 15-year domain with hyperlocal SEO pages covering neighborhood-level queries Raptor has not yet captured.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 star rating vs. 4.7 (the difference matters at the premium price point), no corporate parent diluting the local accountability narrative, and zero credible evidence of incentivized review solicitation — which is a live liability for Cochran.

**Most exploitable weakness:** 

The documented practice of crews asking customers for reviews in exchange for "stars" and a bonus

 is a structural integrity problem that Raptor's owner-response model and authentic review velocity directly counters in any head-to-head sales conversation.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Neighborhood-level landing pages.** Cochran has built out pages targeting specific Indianapolis neighborhoods (Castleton, Rocky Ripple, Williams Creek, Wynnedale, etc.) with service-specific URL structures. These are low-cost AEO and local SEO assets. Raptor should build equivalent pages for Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, and Greenwood with schema markup before Cochran's domain age advantage compounds further.

2. **Dual manufacturer certification as a content pillar.** 

Their Owens Corning Platinum and GAF Certified Contractor credentials

 are cited across every major directory profile and generate backlinks from manufacturer websites. If Raptor holds or can obtain comparable certifications, those credential pages need to be live, linked, and schema-marked — they are direct inputs into how generative AI ranks contractor recommendations.

3. **Commercial estimator expansion as a lead.** The active Commercial Estimator hire signals Cochran is moving budget and capacity toward commercial work. That creates a potential gap in their residential pipeline responsiveness — specifically in the suburban markets (Carmel, Fishers, Westfield) where Raptor competes on premium positioning. Cameron should monitor review cadence in those zip codes; a volume dip from Cochran in the next 60–90 days would confirm the commercial pivot is pulling attention away from residential.

**Updated:** June 11, 2026 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they are a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor serving both residential and commercial customers, and hold A+ standing with the BBB, the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They operate locations in Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, and their service breadth spans roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, painting, and storm restoration — making them one of the widest-footprint exterior contractors in the metro.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach lists approximately 47 employees and annual revenue of $28.6 million (2025).

 **Confidence: medium** — third-party revenue estimates for private contractors vary widely; 

Prospeo pegs revenue at $12 million with an estimated valuation of $38.3 million

, and LeadIQ puts the range at $10M+. The spread is wide. The PPP data is the most reliable floor: 

a PPP loan of $584,200 was taken to retain 40 jobs

, suggesting a true headcount in the 40–55 range. Best working estimate: **$15–25M revenue, 45–55 W-2/1099 staff. Confidence: low-medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Their open posting is a Home Improvement Sales Consultant role for the Indianapolis market — candidates are trained to run company-provided leads while also creating and managing their own leads and referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags a concurrent Estimator & Project Manager search.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible on LinkedIn (321 followers; sparse activity). The dual sales + estimator hiring pattern signals they are trying to push volume on both the front end (lead generation) and back end (project throughput) simultaneously — a classic post-storm-season surge play. No evidence of a dedicated marketing hire in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform signal is notably weak relative to their Google review mass. 

Yelp lists them as "Amos Roofing & Exteriors" at 7301 E 46th St with only 33 reviews

 — a massive discrepancy against 3,139 Google reviews. This is a textbook review-funneling pattern: their post-job outreach is clearly routing customers to Google exclusively. 

Facebook shows 1,407 page likes with only 6 people currently talking about them

 — organically dormant. 

BBB shows A+ accreditation since September 1993

, which is legitimately strong institutional credibility. 

Nextdoor presence exists with a GAF Master Elite claim and BBB A+ noted

, but the profile copy is outdated (references "48 years" of service, not updated to reflect 55 years). 

A second BBB location exists at 9160 Forum Corporate Pkwy, Suite 350, Fort Myers, FL

 — worth watching as a potential geographic expansion signal. The Angi/HomeAdvisor profile shows a 4.5 rating — slightly below their Google average.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack runs on WordPress, PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that signals the site has not had a meaningful rebuild. jQuery 1.11.1 is over a decade old; Core Web Vitals scores are likely soft. 

LeadIQ identifies their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, Nginx, WP Rocket, and Fusion Ads

 — they are at least running a caching layer and have basic on-page SEO tooling installed. They maintain dedicated location pages (e.g., [/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) and service-specific subpages, which provides decent topical coverage for local queries. No visible blog content cadence was found — no date-stamped articles or resource hub. Backlink profile appears to rely on directory citations (BBB, GAF, NRCA, Angi) rather than earned editorial links. AEO schema markup is not verifiably deployed beyond what Yoast auto-generates. The absence of a content engine is a real gap at their revenue scale.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current training data patterns in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, Amos Exteriors surfaces frequently in AI answers for Indianapolis-area roofing queries due to three factors: (1) their 1971 founding date provides strong authority signals AI models associate with longevity; (2) GAF Master Elite status is a named certification that AI models recognize as a quality differentiator; and (3) their review volume (3,139 Google reviews) creates broad citation density across third-party aggregators that LLMs index. They are almost certainly cited by name in responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel / Fishers / Noblesville" queries. Their weak content footprint — no blog, no FAQ schema, no topical authority pages — means they win on brand recognition in AI results, not on structured information retrieval. That is an exploitable gap for Raptor.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,139 vs. 677) means they dominate frequency-based AI citation and map pack impression share. Their 55-year tenure, GAF Master Elite certification, multi-location footprint, and commercial roofing capability give them a broader addressable market. Their insurance claims support operation — with 

experienced insurance claims experts who specialize in working directly with insurers to process claims quickly

 — is a systematized upsell engine Raptor does not appear to match at scale.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** A 5.0 rating at 677 reviews is a cleaner quality signal than 4.9 at 3,139. BBB complaint threads reveal recurring patterns around 

unfinished work, missed deadlines, and incomplete gutter components

 — execution gaps that Raptor can own as a differentiator. Raptor's single-trade focus sharpens the "specialist vs. generalist" contrast. Amos's Indeed employer rating sits at 

2.8 out of 5

, with employee reviews flagging lead quality problems and favoritism — a cultural liability that eventually bleeds into customer experience.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their canvasser-driven lead model produces low-intent appointments — 

leads frequently involve long drives for minimal jobs, with homeowners who either don't know a rep is coming or don't understand why

 — which is a chronic ops/morale drag that Raptor's accountable sales model can outperform on close rate and customer experience.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **GAF Master Elite as a conversion asset.** 

Amos leans hard on GAF Master Elite status, noting it is held by only a small percentage of contractors nationwide and unlocks better warranties than competitors can offer.

 If Raptor holds or can pursue this designation, it should be front-and-center in every paid ad headline, GBP description, and AI-optimized FAQ page — not buried.

2. **Dedicated location + service-area page architecture.** Amos has built out granular location URLs for every major suburb ([amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), etc.) covering 

Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, and all of Central Indiana.

 Raptor should have parity on this — each page uniquely written with local schema, not templated — to compete for suburb-level organic and AI queries.

3. **Multi-platform review distribution.** Amos's Yelp presence (33 reviews) vs. Google presence (3,139) is one of the widest funnel gaps in the Indianapolis market. Raptor should actively route a portion of post-job review requests to Yelp and the BBB to own the comparison stack when homeowners vet multiple platforms — and to create a genuine cross-platform rating story that AI citation engines will eventually reward over single-platform dominance.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Cochran Exteriors
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Refreshed: June 9, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Cochran Exteriors was founded in 2010 and has built its brand on exterior remodeling across Indiana.

 

Co-owned by Ross Cochran and John Cochran, with Andrew Beck serving as Marketing Manager.

 The critical flag for this brief: 

Cochran was acquired by Infinity Home Services (IHS), a portfolio company of North Branch Capital, as part of IHS's national consolidation strategy in the non-insurance, retail residential exterior market.

 This is no longer a true independent — it is a PE-backed roll-up brand operating under a multi-state platform now backed by [Freeman Spogli & Co. and LightBay Capital](https://www.privsource.com/acquisitions/deal/infinity-home-services-ihs-acquires-cochran-exteriors-6pSo3d).

## 2. Estimated Scale



PitchBook lists Cochran Exteriors at 43 total employees

ZoomInfo notes a PPP SBA loan from Regions Bank supporting the retention of 47 jobs

, which triangulates closely. On revenue, sources diverge: 

RocketReach pegs annual revenue at $6.8M for 2025

 (**confidence: low**), while 

CIENCE places them in the $10M–$25M range

 (**confidence: low**). Given their employee count, review velocity, multi-line service offering (roofing, siding, windows, gutters, doors), two Indiana locations, and PE platform backing, $10M–$15M in annual revenue is the most defensible working estimate. They are meaningfully larger in headcount and service breadth than Raptor's pure-roofing focus.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active and aggressive.

 — suggesting continuous sales force expansion. 

Their HR/Marketing crossover role (Sarah Budzinski, joined 2023) draws from a Disney operations and training background, signaling investment in systematized employee onboarding and customer experience frameworks.

 The Commercial Estimator hire is the most telling signal: they are pushing harder into commercial revenue, likely to diversify beyond storm-season residential volatility.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Yelp lists them at 54 reviews

 — a near-invisible footprint relative to their 1,198 Google reviews. That is a textbook review-funneling operation: homeowners are being routed exclusively to Google, and Yelp is an afterthought. 

BBB carries an A+ accreditation

 with a second location at 

48 N Emerson Ave, Suite 600, Greenwood, IN.

 The BBB profile surface includes both glowing testimonials and at least one complaint flagging workmanship accountability. 

Glassdoor employee ratings sit at 3.7/5.0 across 17 anonymous reviews

 — not alarming, but not strong. One reviewer noted 

"the turnaround rate is terrible because of the lack of training, organization, professionalism, and employee development"

 — a potential internal fragility worth watching as IHS scales.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Cochran is investing seriously in structured content. , which is a high-intent AEO/FAQ asset designed to capture "how much does a roof cost in Indianapolis" queries in AI answers. 

Their tech stack includes reCAPTCHA, Cloudflare CDN, and YouTube integrations

, suggesting active video content and performance optimization. The IHS platform almost certainly gives them shared SEO infrastructure, link equity from multi-state brand pages, and a centralized content team — advantages no independent operator in the Indy market replicates. Their domain authority signal benefits from PE-level investment; Cameron should monitor whether IHS cross-links Cochran from its main domain, which would be a meaningful DA boost.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Cochran Exteriors is well-positioned to surface in AI-generated answers for Indianapolis roofing queries. Their combination of 1,198 Google reviews (4.7 stars), 

BBB A+ accreditation

, dedicated geo-targeted service pages, a roof cost calculator, and belonging to a nationally recognized platform (IHS was cited on Qualified Remodeler's Top 100 list) gives them the citation signals that LLMs pull from. They are likely appearing in ChatGPT and Gemini answers for "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" — primarily because they have the review mass, schema-friendly site structure, and third-party publication mentions that feed AI retrieval. Raptor's 677 reviews at a perfect 5.0 is strong but the volume gap is the core vulnerability in AEO. AI models weight review density heavily in local authority signals. Closing that gap — not just maintaining the star rating — is the path to displacing Cochran in generative results.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where Cochran beats Raptor:** Review volume (1,198 vs. 677) is the single biggest lever — they will outrank Raptor in AI citations and map pack impressions on volume alone. Internal reviews flagging high turnover and lack of training

## 4. Off-Google Presence

Trojan Roofing operates two domains — [indytrojanroofing.com](https://indytrojanroofing.com) and [trojanroofs.com](https://www.trojanroofs.com) — which immediately creates authority dilution and NAP inconsistency problems for local SEO. **Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Refreshed June 9, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



In business since 2005, ARAC Roof It Forward has many years of experience offering high-quality roofing services to local residential and commercial customers.

 They operate out of Noblesville (15499 Stony Creek Way) and serve the broader Indianapolis metro including Carmel, Fishers, Greenwood, Zionsville, and Anderson.

 That cause-marketing wrapper is the brand's primary differentiator and the thing that makes it sticky with a specific buyer segment.

## 2. Estimated Scale



ARAC Roof It Forward has 51 to 200 employees

 per Indeed's company profile — **confidence: medium**, as this is a self-reported band.

 That figure reflects the enterprise across all markets (Indianapolis, Atlanta, Nashville, Tampa, and others), not the Indy franchise alone. The Indiana location is a franchise/branch of the larger Georgia-headquartered entity.

, suggesting the parent company has outside capital behind it.

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

 — a signal they are building out a structured sales funnel, not just relying on inbound leads. 

Indeed employee reviews describe the sales role as starting with cold calling and door-knocking, transitioning over time to appointment-based selling.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or field management postings were identified for the Indiana market in the last 30 days. The hiring posture is almost entirely sales-rep-oriented.

## 4. Off-Google Presence



ARAC's Yelp page for the Noblesville location is active with 62 photos as of February 2026

, but review volume there is thin relative to their 310 Google reviews — a classic review-funneling pattern where Google solicitation is aggressive and Yelp is left to chance.

, suggesting most paid social activity is run at the brand level, not localized. No active Indiana-specific Facebook Ad Library creatives were surfaced. The BBB Indiana profile is accredited, 

but includes a notable complaint about damage to decking and ceiling caused during installation, including wiring and ductwork.

 The Google vs. off-platform gap is significant: 4.7 on Google (310 reviews), strong on Angi, weak on Yelp and Facebook. That gap is a reputation arbitrage opportunity for Raptor.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

ARAC operates two parallel websites: [roofitforward.com/indianapolis](https://www.roofitforward.com/indianapolis) (the national franchise site) and [roofitforwardindiana.com](https://www.roofitforwardindiana.com) (an apparent legacy local site). Running two domains for the same business splits domain authority and creates brand confusion — a meaningful SEO vulnerability. The national site has city-specific landing pages for Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, and others, which is a competent local SEO play. 

Their Carmel/Fishers/Noblesville service pages funnel to a shared phone number and push free video roof inspection as the lead gen CTA

 — consistent but templated. 

Their own site points visitors to Angi, BBB, and Nextdoor for social proof

, suggesting they are leaning on third-party authority rather than building owned review assets. Blog content on both domains is thin and generic. No evidence of structured schema markup, local press backlinks, or AEO-optimized FAQ content surfaced.

However, their dual-domain structure and thin blog/FAQ content reduce their AEO footprint for long-tail, intent-driven queries like "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" or "best roofing company Fishers Noblesville." Their faith-and-charity angle could earn citation in AI answers that emphasize community values, which is a distinct positioning lane. with reps actively helping customers work alongside insurance companies to secure full replacement coverage
