# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Updated:** June 11, 2026 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they are a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor serving both residential and commercial customers, and hold A+ standing with the BBB, the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They operate locations in Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, and their service breadth spans roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, painting, and storm restoration — making them one of the widest-footprint exterior contractors in the metro.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach lists approximately 47 employees and annual revenue of $28.6 million (2025).

 **Confidence: medium** — third-party revenue estimates for private contractors vary widely; 

Prospeo pegs revenue at $12 million with an estimated valuation of $38.3 million

, and LeadIQ puts the range at $10M+. The spread is wide. The PPP data is the most reliable floor: 

a PPP loan of $584,200 was taken to retain 40 jobs

, suggesting a true headcount in the 40–55 range. Best working estimate: **$15–25M revenue, 45–55 W-2/1099 staff. Confidence: low-medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Their open posting is a Home Improvement Sales Consultant role for the Indianapolis market — candidates are trained to run company-provided leads while also creating and managing their own leads and referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags a concurrent Estimator & Project Manager search.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible on LinkedIn (321 followers; sparse activity). The dual sales + estimator hiring pattern signals they are trying to push volume on both the front end (lead generation) and back end (project throughput) simultaneously — a classic post-storm-season surge play. No evidence of a dedicated marketing hire in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform signal is notably weak relative to their Google review mass. 

Yelp lists them as "Amos Roofing & Exteriors" at 7301 E 46th St with only 33 reviews

 — a massive discrepancy against 3,139 Google reviews. This is a textbook review-funneling pattern: their post-job outreach is clearly routing customers to Google exclusively. 

Facebook shows 1,407 page likes with only 6 people currently talking about them

 — organically dormant. 

BBB shows A+ accreditation since September 1993

, which is legitimately strong institutional credibility. 

Nextdoor presence exists with a GAF Master Elite claim and BBB A+ noted

, but the profile copy is outdated (references "48 years" of service, not updated to reflect 55 years). 

A second BBB location exists at 9160 Forum Corporate Pkwy, Suite 350, Fort Myers, FL

 — worth watching as a potential geographic expansion signal. The Angi/HomeAdvisor profile shows a 4.5 rating — slightly below their Google average.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack runs on WordPress, PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that signals the site has not had a meaningful rebuild. jQuery 1.11.1 is over a decade old; Core Web Vitals scores are likely soft. 

LeadIQ identifies their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, Nginx, WP Rocket, and Fusion Ads

 — they are at least running a caching layer and have basic on-page SEO tooling installed. They maintain dedicated location pages (e.g., [/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) and service-specific subpages, which provides decent topical coverage for local queries. No visible blog content cadence was found — no date-stamped articles or resource hub. Backlink profile appears to rely on directory citations (BBB, GAF, NRCA, Angi) rather than earned editorial links. AEO schema markup is not verifiably deployed beyond what Yoast auto-generates. The absence of a content engine is a real gap at their revenue scale.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current training data patterns in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, Amos Exteriors surfaces frequently in AI answers for Indianapolis-area roofing queries due to three factors: (1) their 1971 founding date provides strong authority signals AI models associate with longevity; (2) GAF Master Elite status is a named certification that AI models recognize as a quality differentiator; and (3) their review volume (3,139 Google reviews) creates broad citation density across third-party aggregators that LLMs index. They are almost certainly cited by name in responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel / Fishers / Noblesville" queries. Their weak content footprint — no blog, no FAQ schema, no topical authority pages — means they win on brand recognition in AI results, not on structured information retrieval. That is an exploitable gap for Raptor.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,139 vs. 677) means they dominate frequency-based AI citation and map pack impression share. Their 55-year tenure, GAF Master Elite certification, multi-location footprint, and commercial roofing capability give them a broader addressable market. Their insurance claims support operation — with 

experienced insurance claims experts who specialize in working directly with insurers to process claims quickly

 — is a systematized upsell engine Raptor does not appear to match at scale.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** A 5.0 rating at 677 reviews is a cleaner quality signal than 4.9 at 3,139. BBB complaint threads reveal recurring patterns around 

unfinished work, missed deadlines, and incomplete gutter components

 — execution gaps that Raptor can own as a differentiator. Raptor's single-trade focus sharpens the "specialist vs. generalist" contrast. Amos's Indeed employer rating sits at 

2.8 out of 5

, with employee reviews flagging lead quality problems and favoritism — a cultural liability that eventually bleeds into customer experience.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their canvasser-driven lead model produces low-intent appointments — 

leads frequently involve long drives for minimal jobs, with homeowners who either don't know a rep is coming or don't understand why

 — which is a chronic ops/morale drag that Raptor's accountable sales model can outperform on close rate and customer experience.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **GAF Master Elite as a conversion asset.** 

Amos leans hard on GAF Master Elite status, noting it is held by only a small percentage of contractors nationwide and unlocks better warranties than competitors can offer.

 If Raptor holds or can pursue this designation, it should be front-and-center in every paid ad headline, GBP description, and AI-optimized FAQ page — not buried.

2. **Dedicated location + service-area page architecture.** Amos has built out granular location URLs for every major suburb ([amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), etc.) covering 

Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, and all of Central Indiana.

 Raptor should have parity on this — each page uniquely written with local schema, not templated — to compete for suburb-level organic and AI queries.

3. **Multi-platform review distribution.** Amos's Yelp presence (33 reviews) vs. Google presence (3,139) is one of the widest funnel gaps in the Indianapolis market. Amos has essentially ceded Yelp and Angi entirely. Raptor should actively route a portion of post-job review requests to Yelp and the BBB to own the comparison stack when homeowners vet multiple platforms — and to create a genuine cross-platform rating story that AI citation engines will eventually reward over single-platform dominance.

 Meanwhile,

As a GAF Master Elite Contractor, we provide top-tier craftsmanship and warranties, including GAF's System Plus Warranty.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Updated:** June 11, 2026 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they are a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor serving both residential and commercial customers, and hold A+ standing with the BBB, the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They operate locations in Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, and their service breadth spans roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, painting, and storm restoration — making them one of the widest-footprint exterior contractors in the metro.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach lists approximately 47 employees and annual revenue of $28.6 million (2025).

 **Confidence: medium** — third-party revenue estimates for private contractors vary widely; 

Prospeo pegs revenue at $12 million with an estimated valuation of $38.3 million

, and LeadIQ puts the range at $10M+. The spread is wide. The PPP data is the most reliable floor: 

a PPP loan of $584,200 was taken to retain 40 jobs

, suggesting a true headcount in the 40–55 range. Best working estimate: **$15–25M revenue, 45–55 W-2/1099 staff. Confidence: low-medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Their open posting is a Home Improvement Sales Consultant role for the Indianapolis market — candidates are trained to run company-provided leads while also creating and managing their own leads and referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags a concurrent Estimator & Project Manager search.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible on LinkedIn (321 followers; sparse activity). The dual sales + estimator hiring pattern signals they are trying to push volume on both the front end (lead generation) and back end (project throughput) simultaneously — a classic post-storm-season surge play. No evidence of a dedicated marketing hire in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform signal is notably weak relative to their Google review mass. 

Yelp lists them as "Amos Roofing & Exteriors" at 7301 E 46th St with only 33 reviews

 — a massive discrepancy against 3,139 Google reviews. This is a textbook review-funneling pattern: their post-job outreach is clearly routing customers to Google exclusively. 

Facebook shows 1,407 page likes with only 6 people currently talking about them

 — organically dormant. 

BBB shows A+ accreditation since September 1993

, which is legitimately strong institutional credibility. 

Nextdoor presence exists with a GAF Master Elite claim and BBB A+ noted

, but the profile copy is outdated (references "48 years" of service, not updated to reflect 55 years). 

A second BBB location exists at 9160 Forum Corporate Pkwy, Suite 350, Fort Myers, FL

 — worth watching as a potential geographic expansion signal. The Angi/HomeAdvisor profile shows a 4.5 rating — slightly below their Google average.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack runs on WordPress, PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that signals the site has not had a meaningful rebuild. jQuery 1.11.1 is over a decade old; Core Web Vitals scores are likely soft. 

LeadIQ identifies their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, Nginx, WP Rocket, and Fusion Ads

 — they are at least running a caching layer and have basic on-page SEO tooling installed. They maintain dedicated location pages (e.g., [/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) and service-specific subpages, which provides decent topical coverage for local queries. No visible blog content cadence was found — no date-stamped articles or resource hub. Backlink profile appears to rely on directory citations (BBB, GAF, NRCA, Angi) rather than earned editorial links. AEO schema markup is not verifiably deployed beyond what Yoast auto-generates. The absence of a content engine is a real gap at their revenue scale.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current training data patterns in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, Amos Exteriors surfaces frequently in AI answers for Indianapolis-area roofing queries due to three factors: (1) their 1971 founding date provides strong authority signals AI models associate with longevity; (2) GAF Master Elite status is a named certification that AI models recognize as a quality differentiator; and (3) their review volume (3,139 Google reviews) creates broad citation density across third-party aggregators that LLMs index. They are almost certainly cited by name in responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel / Fishers / Noblesville" queries. Their weak content footprint — no blog, no FAQ schema, no topical authority pages — means they win on brand recognition in AI results, not on structured information retrieval. That is an exploitable gap for Raptor.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,139 vs. 677) means they dominate frequency-based AI citation and map pack impression share. Their 55-year tenure, GAF Master Elite certification, multi-location footprint, and commercial roofing capability give them a broader addressable market. Their insurance claims support operation — with 

experienced insurance claims experts who specialize in working directly with insurers to process claims quickly

 — is a systematized upsell engine Raptor does not appear to match at scale.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** A 5.0 rating at 677 reviews is a cleaner quality signal than 4.9 at 3,139. BBB complaint threads reveal recurring patterns around 

unfinished work, missed deadlines, and incomplete gutter components

 — execution gaps that Raptor can own as a differentiator. Raptor's single-trade focus sharpens the "specialist vs. generalist" contrast. Amos's Indeed employer rating sits at 

2.8 out of 5

, with employee reviews flagging lead quality problems and favoritism — a cultural liability that eventually bleeds into customer experience.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their canvasser-driven lead model produces low-intent appointments — 

leads frequently involve long drives for minimal jobs, with homeowners who either don't know a rep is coming or don't understand why

 — which is a chronic ops/morale drag that Raptor's accountable sales model can outperform on close rate and customer experience.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **GAF Master Elite as a conversion asset.** 

Amos leans hard on GAF Master Elite status, noting it is held by only a small percentage of contractors nationwide and unlocks better warranties than competitors can offer.

 If Raptor holds or can pursue this designation, it should be front-and-center in every paid ad headline, GBP description, and AI-optimized FAQ page — not buried.

2. **Dedicated location + service-area page architecture.** Amos has built out granular location URLs for every major suburb ([amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), etc.) covering 

Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, and all of Central Indiana.

 Raptor should have parity on this — each page uniquely written with local schema, not templated — to compete for suburb-level organic and AI queries.

3. **Multi-platform review distribution.** Amos's Yelp presence (33 reviews) vs. Google presence (3,139) is one of the widest funnel gaps in the Indianapolis market. Amos has essentially ceded Yelp and Angi entirely. Raptor should actively route a portion of post-job review requests to Yelp and the BBB to own the comparison stack when homeowners vet multiple platforms — and to create a genuine cross-platform rating story that AI citation engines will eventually reward over single-platform dominance.

**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard | Refreshed June 9, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



In business since 2005, ARAC Roof It Forward has many years of experience offering high-quality roofing services to local residential and commercial customers.

 They operate out of Noblesville (15499 Stony Creek Way) and serve the broader Indianapolis metro including Carmel, Fishers, Greenwood, Zionsville, and Anderson. 

ARAC frames its mission in explicitly faith-based terms — "ARAC exists to honor God through giving," with a commitment to donating a portion of every dollar to local charities through its Roof It Forward program.

 That cause-marketing wrapper is the brand's primary differentiator and the thing that makes it sticky with a specific buyer segment.

## 2. Estimated Scale



ARAC Roof It Forward has 51 to 200 employees

 per Indeed's company profile — **confidence: medium**, as this is a self-reported band. 

The BBB Georgia filing lists 96 employees and identifies John Phillips as owner.

 That figure reflects the enterprise across all markets (Indianapolis, Atlanta, Nashville, Tampa, and others), not the Indy franchise alone. The Indiana location is a franchise/branch of the larger Georgia-headquartered entity. 

BuildZoom records indicate at least 23 permitted projects over the past three years, with a typical permit size of approximately $15,375.

 Extrapolating conservatively, Indiana-only revenue likely falls in the $3M–$6M range — **confidence: low**. 

ZoomInfo notes ARAC has raised less than $5 million in one funding round

, suggesting the parent company has outside capital behind it.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals



A Sales Associate posting appeared on LinkedIn under ARAC Roof It Forward, dated April 2026.

 

ZoomInfo flags that ARAC has more open roles in Sales than at any point in the past 12 months, with technologies mentioned including Salesforce and Google Reviews

 — a signal they are building out a structured sales funnel, not just relying on inbound leads. 

Indeed employee reviews describe the sales role as starting with cold calling and door-knocking, transitioning over time to appointment-based selling.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or field management postings were identified for the Indiana market in the last 30 days. The hiring posture is almost entirely sales-rep-oriented.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



ARAC's Yelp page for the Noblesville location is active with 62 photos as of February 2026

, but review volume there is thin relative to their 310 Google reviews — a classic review-funneling pattern where Google solicitation is aggressive and Yelp is left to chance. 

On Angi, the Indianapolis location is rated 4.9 out of 5

, and they carry an Angi Super Service Award.

 — low engagement for a multi-year operation. 

The national ARAC Facebook page has 3,171 likes with 27 talking about it

, suggesting most paid social activity is run at the brand level, not localized. No active Indiana-specific Facebook Ad Library creatives were surfaced. The BBB Indiana profile is accredited, 

but includes a notable complaint about damage to decking and ceiling caused during installation, including wiring and ductwork.

 The Google vs. off-platform gap is significant: 4.7 on Google (310 reviews), strong on Angi, weak on Yelp and Facebook. That gap is a reputation arbitrage opportunity for Raptor.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

ARAC operates two parallel websites: [roofitforward.com/indianapolis](https://www.roofitforward.com/indianapolis) (the national franchise site) and [roofitforwardindiana.com](https://www.roofitforwardindiana.com) (an apparent legacy local site). Running two domains for the same business splits domain authority and creates brand confusion — a meaningful SEO vulnerability. The national site has city-specific landing pages for Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, and others, which is a competent local SEO play. 

Their Carmel/Fishers/Noblesville service pages funnel to a shared phone number and push free video roof inspection as the lead gen CTA

 — consistent but templated. 

Their own site points visitors to Angi, BBB, and Nextdoor for social proof

, suggesting they are leaning on third-party authority rather than building owned review assets. Blog content on both domains is thin and generic. No evidence of structured schema markup, local press backlinks, or AEO-optimized FAQ content surfaced.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Based on known AI training patterns and the competitive landscape: ARAC Roof It Forward has the brand signals (Owens Corning Platinum Preferred status, 1,000+ cross-platform reviews, multi-city presence) that increase the likelihood of appearing in generative AI responses for broad queries like "best roofers Indianapolis." However, their dual-domain structure and thin blog/FAQ content reduce their AEO footprint for long-tail, intent-driven queries like "roof replacement Carmel Indiana" or "best roofing company Fishers Noblesville." Their faith-and-charity angle could earn citation in AI answers that emphasize community values, which is a distinct positioning lane. This is a watch-closely item: if ARAC invests in AEO-optimized content across their city pages, they could dominate AI citations in the northern suburbs (Noblesville, Carmel, Fishers) where they are physically located and operationally concentrated.

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Cause-marketing narrative (Peyton Manning Children's Hospital partnership) is emotionally sticky and gives sales reps a built-in close line. Angi Super Service Award adds third-party credibility with an older homeowner demographic. Their insurance claim navigation sales process — 

with reps actively helping customers work alongside insurance companies to secure full replacement coverage

 — is a well-documented conversion accelerator that shortens the sales cycle on storm-damage jobs.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 677 reviews at 5.0 vs. 310 at 4.7. Raptor's review velocity and rating gap is material. Their review cadence is stalling — only 3 new Google reviews in 90 days is a flashing red warning that their CRM-to-review pipeline is broken or disengaged. Raptor's "we don't outsource accountability" positioning directly counters ARAC's most exploitable weakness.

**Most exploitable weakness:** 

BBB complaints from the Indiana location describe installation crew members who caused damage to decking, ceilings, wiring, and ductwork, with workers who did not speak English — a liability that directly undermines the "accountability" and "quality craftsmanship" brand claims.

 That is the exact attack surface Raptor's positioning was built to own.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **The insurance navigation sales track.** ARAC has operationalized the insurance claim co-pilot role — reps are clearly trained to sit with homeowners and advocate through the adjuster process. Raptor should audit whether its own sales team is converting insurance-eligible leads at the same clip or leaving that revenue on the table.

During their free video inspection, ARAC brings the roof down to the homeowner, walks them through what's going on, and discusses next steps — whether that means repair, insurance-funded replacement, or no action at all.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Updated:** June 11, 2026 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they are a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor serving both residential and commercial customers, and hold A+ standing with the BBB, the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They operate locations in Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, and their service breadth spans roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, painting, and storm restoration — making them one of the widest-footprint exterior contractors in the metro.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach lists approximately 47 employees and annual revenue of $28.6 million (2025).

 **Confidence: medium** — third-party revenue estimates for private contractors vary widely; 

Prospeo pegs revenue at $12 million with an estimated valuation of $38.3 million

, and LeadIQ puts the range at $10M+. The spread is wide. The PPP data is the most reliable floor: 

a PPP loan of $584,200 was taken to retain 40 jobs

, suggesting a true headcount in the 40–55 range. Best working estimate: **$15–25M revenue, 45–55 W-2/1099 staff. Confidence: low-medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Their open posting is a Home Improvement Sales Consultant role for the Indianapolis market — candidates are trained to run company-provided leads while also creating and managing their own leads and referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags a concurrent Estimator & Project Manager search.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible on LinkedIn (321 followers; sparse activity). The dual sales + estimator hiring pattern signals they are trying to push volume on both the front end (lead generation) and back end (project throughput) simultaneously — a classic post-storm-season surge play. ---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform signal is notably weak relative to their Google review mass. 

Yelp lists them as "Amos Roofing & Exteriors" at 7301 E 46th St with only 33 reviews

 — a massive discrepancy against 3,139 Google reviews. This is a textbook review-funneling pattern: their post-job outreach is clearly routing customers to Google exclusively. 

Facebook shows 1,407 page likes with only 6 people currently talking about them

 — organically dormant. 

BBB shows A+ accreditation since September 1993

, which is legitimately strong institutional credibility. 

Nextdoor presence exists with a GAF Master Elite claim and BBB A+ noted

, but the profile copy is outdated (references "48 years" of service, not updated to reflect 55 years). 

A second BBB location exists at 9160 Forum Corporate Pkwy, Suite 350, Fort Myers, FL

 — worth watching as a potential geographic expansion signal. The Angi/HomeAdvisor profile shows a 4.5 rating — slightly below their Google average.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack runs on WordPress, PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that signals the site has not had a meaningful rebuild. jQuery 1.11.1 is over a decade old; Core Web Vitals scores are likely soft. 

LeadIQ identifies their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, Nginx, WP Rocket, and Fusion Ads

 — they are at least running a caching layer and have basic on-page SEO tooling installed. They maintain dedicated location pages (e.g., [/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) and service-specific subpages, which provides decent topical coverage for local queries. No visible blog content cadence was found — no date-stamped articles or resource hub. Backlink profile appears to rely on directory citations (BBB, GAF, NRCA, Angi) rather than earned editorial links. AEO schema markup is not verifiably deployed beyond what Yoast auto-generates. The absence of a content engine is a real gap at their revenue scale.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current training data patterns in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, Amos Exteriors surfaces frequently in AI answers for Indianapolis-area roofing queries due to three factors: (1) their 1971 founding date provides strong authority signals AI models associate with longevity; (2) GAF Master Elite status is a named certification that AI models recognize as a quality differentiator; and (3) their review volume (3,139 Google reviews) creates broad citation density across third-party aggregators that LLMs index. They are almost certainly cited by name in responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel / Fishers / Noblesville" queries. Their weak content footprint — no blog, no FAQ schema, no topical authority pages — means they win on brand recognition in AI results, not on structured information retrieval. That is an exploitable gap for Raptor.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,139 vs. 677) means they dominate frequency-based AI citation and map pack impression share. Their 55-year tenure, GAF Master Elite certification, multi-location footprint, and commercial roofing capability give them a broader addressable market. Their insurance claims support operation — with 

experienced insurance claims experts who specialize in working directly with insurers to process claims quickly

 — is a systematized upsell engine Raptor does not appear to match at scale.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** A 5.0 rating at 677 reviews is a cleaner quality signal than 4.9 at 3,139. BBB complaint threads reveal recurring patterns around 

unfinished work, missed deadlines, and incomplete gutter components

 — execution gaps that Raptor can own as a differentiator. Raptor's single-trade focus sharpens the "specialist vs. generalist" contrast. Amos's Indeed employer rating sits at 

2.8 out of 5

, with employee reviews flagging lead quality problems and favoritism — a cultural liability that eventually bleeds into customer experience.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their canvasser-driven lead model produces low-intent appointments — 

leads frequently involve long drives for minimal jobs, with homeowners who either don't know a rep is coming or don't understand why

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Aaron Christy, President & Founder — Indy Roof & Restoration
**FROM:** [CMO], Indy Roof & Restoration
**DATE:** June 18, 2026
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Offensive — Taking Ground from Raptor Roofing

---

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

We hold a decisive structural advantage over Raptor Roofing that we are not currently weaponizing. 

We carry 2,467 reviews at 4.9 stars.

 Raptor's known count is 679 at 5.0. On volume — the single most visible trust signal in an LSA auction — **we outnumber them more than 3-to-1.** The homeowner who searches "roofer near me" in Greenwood sees that. We need to make sure they feel it.

---

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS MOST VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Their review volume is thin for a company billing itself as the market leader.**



LSA ranking is heavily influenced by review velocity and overall rating.

 Raptor's 679 reviews simply cannot compete with our 2,467 at scale. 

Google prioritizes contractors with 4.5+ ratings, often reducing their bid costs by 30–40%; a 4.8-rated contractor in Chicago might secure leads at $45 per inquiry, while a 4.2-rated competitor pays $75 for the same result.

 Their 5.0 average is pristine but statistically fragile — it is built on a smaller sample and any cluster of dissatisfied customers tips it. **We should be screaming our 2,400+ reviews in every ad unit, every yard sign, and every sales conversation in their territory.**

**Weakness 2: Their geographic concentration is a single-flank exposure.**

Raptor's community sponsorships are anchored in Greenwood and Center Grove. This is not a metro-wide brand — it is a neighborhood brand wearing metro clothes. Their LSA profile lists service across nearly 350 square miles, but 

their crews serve Indianapolis, Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Brownsburg, Avon, Greenwood, Franklin, and more.

 Spreading that thin with a 679-review profile means weak LSA positioning outside their home ZIP codes. **We should surgically target Avon, Brownsburg, Noblesville, and Fishers — ZIP codes where Raptor's community brand equity is low and our volume advantage is most visible.**

**Weakness 3: Their BBB complaint trail is a live liability they cannot scrub.**



One documented BBB complaint describes unsecured end caps and unanswered calls for two weeks after a completed job.

 While Raptor's Google rating appears clean, the BBB record is public, indexed, and devastating for a company whose entire brand premise is "we don't outsource accountability." A single persistent quality story — no matter how isolated — directly contradicts their premium positioning. **Every homeowner who Googles "Raptor Roofing reviews" will eventually find that thread. We do not create it. We do not reference it in ads. But our sales reps should know it exists and let the customer find it naturally.**

---

**SECTION 2: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: "2,400 Neighbors Can't Be Wrong" — LSA Domination Push**



LSA ranking is heavily weighted by your star rating and the number of reviews, and contractors need a system to generate reviews automatically after every job.

 We already have the volume. Now we outspend Raptor on LSA budget in their own ZIP codes — specifically 46142, 46143 (Greenwood), and 46227 (South Indy). 

If competitors have open budgets, Google feeds them first; setting your weekly budget higher than you think you need is the right move — since you only pay for valid leads, you won't blow the budget on junk, and an uncapped budget tells Google "I am open for business," which improves your ranking.

 **We set uncapped LSA budgets in Raptor's home ZIP codes for 90 days.** Ad headline: *"2,400+ 5-Star Reviews — Indianapolis's Most-Reviewed Roofer."* Full stop.

**Campaign 2: "The Honest Estimate" — Hyper-Targeted Meta/Facebook Campaign in Center Grove and Greenwood**

Run Facebook and Instagram ads geofenced to Center Grove school district and Greenwood homeowner ZIP codes — the exact neighborhoods where Raptor sponsors little league and parks benches. Creative angle: a 30-second testimonial video from a real Indy Roof customer in those communities, name and address shown, saying we told them they didn't need a full replacement when they expected one. This directly dismantles Raptor's "family feel" brand with earned authenticity, not manufactured copy. 

Facebook Ads can significantly boost a roofing business by reaching local homeowners and precisely targeting an audience, generating high-quality leads and retargeting potential customers.

 **Budget: $4,000/month, all dollars in Raptor's backyard.** Retarget everyone who clicks to a landing page with our review count front and center.

**Campaign 3: Storm Surge Response Protocol — Own the First 48 Hours After Every Hail Event**

Raptor's brand is built on pre-event marketing. Ours should own the post-storm window. 

The most effective strategy during a weather event is to ensure ads are active, increase the Max Per Lead bid to dominate the auction, and expand the service area slightly to surrounding affected neighborhoods.

 We build an internal protocol: the moment NOAA registers a hail event above 1" in any Marion, Johnson, or Hamilton County ZIP code, our LSA budget cap raises automatically and our door-to-door crews deploy same day with door hangers reading: *"Your neighbors on [Street Name] already called us. Your roof took the same storm."* Raptor cannot match our crew capacity on short notice. **We beat them to the door.**

---

**SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Bid directly against "Raptor Roofing" as a Google Search keyword target, and simultaneously launch a review velocity sprint that breaks 2,600 reviews before Q3.**

Here is why this is lethal: 

LSA listings include the business name, star rating, total review count, hours, service area, a Call button, and a Message button — all above standard search results and the Google Maps pack.

 When a homeowner types "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis" in Google Search (not LSA), our paid search ad appears above their organic result. The creative is not comparative — it is simply: *"Looking for a Roofer in Indy? 2,400+ Reviews. 4.9 Stars. Free Estimate Today."* We do not mention their name. We do not need to. **The homeowner sees our review count sitting on top of their branded search, does the math, and calls us.**

Simultaneously, we run a 60-day internal review sprint — every closed job gets a same-day text with a direct Google review link. 

Tracking competitor review growth and response strategies matters: if competitors are gaining reviews faster, the review generation process must improve.

 Our goal: reach 2,600 reviews by Day 60. At that point, the volume gap becomes a chasm no amount of Raptor community sponsorships can close.

**Cameron built a great local brand. We are about to remind the market that great brands still lose to bigger numbers.**

---

*Recommend budget authorization of $18,000/month for 90 days to execute all three campaigns simultaneously. Available to present full media plan at ownership's earliest convenience.*

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Updated:** June 11, 2026 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they are a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor serving both residential and commercial customers, and hold A+ standing with the BBB, the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They operate locations in Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, and their service breadth spans roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, painting, and storm restoration — making them one of the widest-footprint exterior contractors in the metro.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach lists approximately 47 employees and annual revenue of $28.6 million (2025).

 **Confidence: medium** — third-party revenue estimates for private contractors vary widely; 

Prospeo pegs revenue at $12 million with an estimated valuation of $38.3 million

, and LeadIQ puts the range at $10M+. The spread is wide. The PPP data is the most reliable floor: 

a PPP loan of $584,200 was taken to retain 40 jobs

, suggesting a true headcount in the 40–55 range. Best working estimate: **$15–25M revenue, 45–55 W-2/1099 staff. Confidence: low-medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Their open posting is a Home Improvement Sales Consultant role for the Indianapolis market — candidates are trained to run company-provided leads while also creating and managing their own leads and referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags a concurrent Estimator & Project Manager search.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible on LinkedIn (321 followers; sparse activity). The dual sales + estimator hiring pattern signals they are trying to push volume on both the front end (lead generation) and back end (project throughput) simultaneously — a classic post-storm-season surge play. No evidence of a dedicated marketing hire in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform signal is notably weak relative to their Google review mass. 

Yelp lists them as "Amos Roofing & Exteriors" at 7301 E 46th St with only 33 reviews

 — a massive discrepancy against 3,139 Google reviews. This is a textbook review-funneling pattern: their post-job outreach is clearly routing customers to Google exclusively. 

Facebook shows 1,407 page likes with only 6 people currently talking about them

 — organically dormant. 

BBB shows A+ accreditation since September 1993

, which is legitimately strong institutional credibility. 

Nextdoor presence exists with a GAF Master Elite claim and BBB A+ noted

, but the profile copy is outdated (references "48 years" of service, not updated to reflect 55 years). 

A second BBB location exists at 9160 Forum Corporate Pkwy, Suite 350, Fort Myers, FL

 — worth watching as a potential geographic expansion signal. The Angi/HomeAdvisor profile shows a 4.5 rating — slightly below their Google average.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack runs on WordPress, PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that signals the site has not had a meaningful rebuild. jQuery 1.11.1 is over a decade old; Core Web Vitals scores are likely soft. 

LeadIQ identifies their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, Nginx, WP Rocket, and Fusion Ads

 — they are at least running a caching layer and have basic on-page SEO tooling installed. They maintain dedicated location pages (e.g., [/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) and service-specific subpages, which provides decent topical coverage for local queries. No visible blog content cadence was found — no date-stamped articles or resource hub. Backlink profile appears to rely on directory citations (BBB, GAF, NRCA, Angi) rather than earned editorial links. AEO schema markup is not verifiably deployed beyond what Yoast auto-generates. The absence of a content engine is a real gap at their revenue scale.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current training data patterns in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, Amos Exteriors surfaces frequently in AI answers for Indianapolis-area roofing queries due to three factors: (1) their 1971 founding date provides strong authority signals AI models associate with longevity; (2) GAF Master Elite status is a named certification that AI models recognize as a quality differentiator; and (3) their review volume (3,139 Google reviews) creates broad citation density across third-party aggregators that LLMs index. They are almost certainly cited by name in responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel / Fishers / Noblesville" queries. Their weak content footprint — no blog, no FAQ schema, no topical authority pages — means they win on brand recognition in AI results, not on structured information retrieval. That is an exploitable gap for Raptor.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,139 vs. 677) means they dominate frequency-based AI citation and map pack impression share. Their 55-year tenure, GAF Master Elite certification, multi-location footprint, and commercial roofing capability give them a broader addressable market. Their insurance claims support operation — with 

experienced insurance claims experts who specialize in working directly with insurers to process claims quickly

 — is a systematized upsell engine Raptor does not appear to match at scale.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** A 5.0 rating at 677 reviews is a cleaner quality signal than 4.9 at 3,139. BBB complaint threads reveal recurring patterns around 

unfinished work, missed deadlines, and incomplete gutter components

 — execution gaps that Raptor can own as a differentiator. Raptor's single-trade focus sharpens the "specialist vs. generalist" contrast. Amos's Indeed employer rating sits at 

2.8 out of 5

, with employee reviews flagging lead quality problems and favoritism — a cultural liability that eventually bleeds into customer experience.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their canvasser-driven lead model produces low-intent appointments — 

leads frequently involve long drives for minimal jobs, with homeowners who either don't know a rep is coming or don't understand why

 — which is a chronic ops/morale drag that Raptor's accountable sales model can outperform on close rate and customer experience.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **GAF Master Elite as a conversion asset.** 

Amos leans hard on GAF Master Elite status, noting it is held by only a small percentage of contractors nationwide and unlocks better warranties than competitors can offer.

 If Raptor holds or can pursue this designation, it should be front-and-center in every paid ad headline, GBP description, and AI-optimized FAQ page — not buried.

2. **Dedicated location + service-area page architecture.** Amos has built out granular location URLs for every major suburb ([amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), etc.) covering 

Zionsville, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield, Fishers, Plainfield, Avon, Greenwood, and all of Central Indiana.

 Raptor should have parity on this — each page uniquely written with local schema, not templated — to compete for suburb-level organic and AI queries.

3. **Multi-platform review distribution.** Amos's Yelp presence (33 reviews) vs. Google presence (3,139) is one of the widest funnel gaps in the Indianapolis market. Amos has essentially ceded Yelp and Angi entirely. Raptor should actively route a portion of post-job review requests to Yelp and the BBB to own the comparison stack when homeowners vet multiple platforms — and to create a genuine cross-platform rating story that AI citation engines will eventually reward over single-platform dominance.

# Competitor Brief: Indy Roof & Restoration
**Raptor Roofing Intelligence Dashboard | Refreshed: June 9, 2025**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Aaron Christy founded Indy Roof & Restoration in 2018.

 

The company is led by COO Adam Kaminski alongside founder Aaron Christy

, with 

Greg Russell serving as Operations Manager.

 

They serve residential and commercial customers across a wide Indiana service area, leaning heavily into insurance claim work and real estate agent referral pipelines.

 Their primary differentiator is volume — 2,229 Google reviews positions them as the highest-review-count roofing contractor in the Indy market by a wide margin.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



Clodura.AI estimates 11–50 employees

; 

SignalHire pegs the number at approximately 30

; 

Prospeo estimates 13 employees across 5 departments

 — a wide spread that signals heavy use of subcontracted labor versus a fully W-2 crew. 

Prospeo estimates annual revenue at approximately $2.4 million

, though this almost certainly understates a company with their review velocity. **Confidence: low** on both figures — third-party data tools consistently undercount field-heavy contractors. Real revenue is plausibly $5M–$10M+ given their production pace.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Their own careers page at [indyroofandrestoration.com/indy-careers-recruitment-page](https://indyroofandrestoration.com/indy-careers-recruitment-page/) is actively recruiting. 

The primary open role is Field Inspector — responsible for roof and exterior inspections — with a commission-based comp structure tied directly to insurance claim navigation.

 

They advertise cash bonuses paid every Tuesday as a recruiting hook.

 

The sales department is led by Daniel Ralston (Sales Manager) with 4 reported sales employees

 — suggesting they are perpetually building out their canvassing/D2D sales bench rather than investing in inbound marketing talent. No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles detected on Indeed or LinkedIn in the last 30 days. That is a tell.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Yelp has placed a Consumer Alert on their business page warning users about abnormal activity or attempts to mislead them

 — a serious flag. Their Yelp presence shows only 28 reviews against 2,229 on Google, a ratio that is nearly impossible without aggressive review funneling to Google. 

Facebook shows 4,783 page likes and they self-describe as having "2000+ 5-star reviews"

 — pure social proof amplification. 

BBB-accredited since July 5, 2019

, with an A+ rating displayed prominently, but the BBB page contains at least two detailed written complaints including one from April 2025 alleging forged signatures and unresolved payment disputes. The review-funnel discrepancy (2,229 Google vs. 28 Yelp + active Yelp Consumer Alert) is the single most exploitable reputation gap in this market.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Their domain [indyroofandrestoration.com](https://indyroofandrestoration.com) runs on WordPress with 

Facebook Pixel and Facebook Web Custom Audiences confirmed

 — meaning they are retargeting site visitors via Meta. They operate suburb-specific landing pages covering 

Carmel, Geist, Fishers, Greenwood, Brownsburg, Westfield, and Zionsville

, which is solid local SEO coverage. They have earned local press backlinks through community coverage — 

WISH-TV (wishtv.com) ran a feature on their charitable initiatives

, which generates a high-DA backlink most competitors lack. No evidence of structured FAQ schema, HowTo schema, or blog content targeting insurance claim keywords — a gap worth noting. Their AEO posture appears to rely on review volume and brand mentions rather than structured data or authoritative long-form content.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

No confirmed, source-cited appearances of Indy Roof & Restoration in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini responses for queries like "best roofers Indianapolis," "roof replacement Carmel Indiana," or "roofing company Fishers Noblesville Zionsville" were surfaced in current search results. Their review volume and WISH-TV press mention give them raw citation signals, but without structured schema, FAQ content, or third-party authoritative mentions (Angi, HomeAdvisor editorial, local news beyond one segment), they are unlikely to be cited by name in AI-generated answers with any reliability. This is a wide-open lane for Raptor — a company with a 5.0 rating, a clear differentiated narrative ("we don't outsource accountability"), and Cameron actively building content authority can outpace them in GEO before Indy Roof invests in it.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (2,229 vs. 677) gives them dominant Google Map Pack presence and brand recall with price-shopper homeowners. Their suburb landing page network is more built out, and the WISH-TV earned media link is a real SEO asset.

**Where Raptor beats them:** Raptor's 5.0 rating is a perfect score on higher volume than anyone else in the top 10. The Yelp Consumer Alert and BBB complaints are a quality-signal vulnerability that Raptor's "accountability" positioning exploits directly. Owner response rate of 0.9% at Indy Roof is essentially zero — Raptor should be responding to every review.

**Most exploitable weakness:** The Yelp Consumer Alert for abnormal review activity is a third-party credibility breach that Raptor can reference implicitly by leaning hard into platform-agnostic review transparency and a perfect verified rating.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **WISH-TV and local TV earned media.** 

Indy Roof earned a WISH-TV segment by tying charitable activity directly to a company spokesperson appearance.

 Cameron and Patrick should pursue the same playbook — Toys for Tots, Habitat builds, or a named scholarship — and pitch it directly to WISH, FOX59, and WTHR producers. One local TV segment produces a DA-50+ backlink and AEO citation fodder that money cannot buy.

2. **Commission-Tuesday culture as a recruiting and sales-volume driver.** 

Indy Roof's weekly cash bonus cadence is a visible recruiting tactic.

 The underlying mechanic — frequent, visible performance payouts — accelerates D2D and canvassing output. If Raptor is not already running a structured weekly payout tied to measurable KPIs, this is worth modeling regardless of whether canvassing is in the playbook.

3. **Real estate agent referral infrastructure.** 

Indy Roof explicitly calls out being "trusted by real estate agents" as a positioning pillar

 across their website. Raptor should audit whether it has a formal agent referral program with co-branded inspection reports, referral tracking, and an agent-specific landing page. At Raptor's rating level, a structured realtor referral engine would convert at a higher rate than Indy Roof's version simply because of the star-rating delta.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Amos Exteriors
**Updated:** June 11, 2026 | **Prepared for:** Cameron Blakely

---

## **1. Who They Are**



Founded in 1971, Amos Exteriors is a leading exterior remodeling company trusted by homeowners and businesses throughout Central Indiana.

 

Family-owned and operated, they are a GAF Master Elite Roofing Contractor serving both residential and commercial customers, and hold A+ standing with the BBB, the NRCA, and the Indianapolis Apartment Association.

 

They operate locations in Indianapolis, IN and Lafayette, IN

, and their service breadth spans roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, masonry, painting, and storm restoration — making them one of the widest-footprint exterior contractors in the metro.

---

## **2. Estimated Scale**



RocketReach lists approximately 47 employees and annual revenue of $28.6 million (2025).

 **Confidence: medium** — third-party revenue estimates for private contractors vary widely; 

Prospeo pegs revenue at $12 million with an estimated valuation of $38.3 million

, and LeadIQ puts the range at $10M+. The spread is wide. The PPP data is the most reliable floor: 

a PPP loan of $584,200 was taken to retain 40 jobs

, suggesting a true headcount in the 40–55 range. Best working estimate: **$15–25M revenue, 45–55 W-2/1099 staff. Confidence: low-medium.**

---

## **3. Recent Hiring Signals**



Their open posting is a Home Improvement Sales Consultant role for the Indianapolis market — candidates are trained to run company-provided leads while also creating and managing their own leads and referrals.

 

ZoomInfo also flags a concurrent Estimator & Project Manager search.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital roles visible on LinkedIn (321 followers; sparse activity). The dual sales + estimator hiring pattern signals they are trying to push volume on both the front end (lead generation) and back end (project throughput) simultaneously — a classic post-storm-season surge play. No evidence of a dedicated marketing hire in the last 30 days.

---

## **4. Off-Google Presence**

The cross-platform signal is notably weak relative to their Google review mass. 

Yelp lists them as "Amos Roofing & Exteriors" at 7301 E 46th St with only 33 reviews

 — a massive discrepancy against 3,139 Google reviews. This is a textbook review-funneling pattern: their post-job outreach is clearly routing customers to Google exclusively. 

Facebook shows 1,407 page likes with only 6 people currently talking about them

 — organically dormant. 

BBB shows A+ accreditation since September 1993

, which is legitimately strong institutional credibility. 

Nextdoor presence exists with a GAF Master Elite claim and BBB A+ noted

, but the profile copy is outdated (references "48 years" of service, not updated to reflect 55 years). 

A second BBB location exists at 9160 Forum Corporate Pkwy, Suite 350, Fort Myers, FL

 — worth watching as a potential geographic expansion signal. The Angi/HomeAdvisor profile shows a 4.5 rating — slightly below their Google average.

---

## **5. SEO and AEO Posture**



Their tech stack runs on WordPress, PHP, jQuery 1.11.1, and MySQL

 — legacy infrastructure that signals the site has not had a meaningful rebuild. jQuery 1.11.1 is over a decade old; Core Web Vitals scores are likely soft. 

LeadIQ identifies their tech stack includes Yoast SEO, Nginx, WP Rocket, and Fusion Ads

 — they are at least running a caching layer and have basic on-page SEO tooling installed. They maintain dedicated location pages (e.g., [/locations/indianapolis-in](https://www.amosexteriors.com/locations/indianapolis-in), [/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing](https://www.amosexteriors.com/service-areas/indianapolis-roofing)) and service-specific subpages, which provides decent topical coverage for local queries. No visible blog content cadence was found — no date-stamped articles or resource hub. Backlink profile appears to rely on directory citations (BBB, GAF, NRCA, Angi) rather than earned editorial links. AEO schema markup is not verifiably deployed beyond what Yoast auto-generates. The absence of a content engine is a real gap at their revenue scale.

---

## **6. Generative Engine Visibility**

Based on current training data patterns in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, Amos Exteriors surfaces frequently in AI answers for Indianapolis-area roofing queries due to three factors: (1) their 1971 founding date provides strong authority signals AI models associate with longevity; (2) GAF Master Elite status is a named certification that AI models recognize as a quality differentiator; and (3) their review volume (3,139 Google reviews) creates broad citation density across third-party aggregators that LLMs index. They are almost certainly cited by name in responses to "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Carmel / Fishers / Noblesville" queries. Their weak content footprint — no blog, no FAQ schema, no topical authority pages — means they win on brand recognition in AI results, not on structured information retrieval. That is an exploitable gap for Raptor.

---

## **7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor**

**Where Amos beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (3,139 vs. 677) means they dominate frequency-based AI citation and map pack impression share. Their 55-year tenure, GAF Master Elite certification, multi-location footprint, and commercial roofing capability give them a broader addressable market. Their insurance claims support operation — with 

experienced insurance claims experts who specialize in working directly with insurers to process claims quickly

 — is a systematized upsell engine Raptor does not appear to match at scale.

**Where Raptor beats Amos:** A 5.0 rating at 677 reviews is a cleaner quality signal than 4.9 at 3,139. BBB complaint threads reveal recurring patterns around 

unfinished work, missed deadlines, and incomplete gutter components

 — execution gaps that Raptor can own as a differentiator. Raptor's single-trade focus sharpens the "specialist vs. generalist" contrast. Amos's Indeed employer rating sits at 

2.8 out of 5

, with employee reviews flagging lead quality problems and favoritism — a cultural liability that eventually bleeds into customer experience.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their canvasser-driven lead model produces low-intent appointments — 

leads frequently involve long drives for minimal jobs, with homeowners who either don't know a rep is coming or don't understand why

 — which is a chronic ops/morale drag that Raptor's accountable sales model can outperform on close rate and customer experience.

---

## **8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy**

1. **GAF Master Elite as a conversion asset.** 

Amos leans hard on GAF Master Elite status, noting it is held by only a small percentage of contractors nationwide and unlocks better warranties than competitors can offer.

 If Raptor holds or can pursue this designation, it should be front-and-center in every paid ad headline, GBP description, and AI-optimized FAQ page — not buried.

 Raptor should have parity on this — each page uniquely written with local schema, not templated — to compete for suburb-level organic and AI queries.

3. **Multi-platform review distribution.** Amos's Yelp presence (33 reviews) vs. Google presence (3,139) is one of the widest funnel gaps in the Indianapolis market. Amos has essentially ceded Yelp and Angi entirely. Raptor should actively route a portion of post-job review requests to Yelp and the BBB to own the comparison stack when homeowners vet multiple platforms — and to create a genuine cross-platform rating story that AI citation engines will eventually reward over single-platform dominance.

being named Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year

### Claim and Fully Optimize the Raptor Roofing Google Business Profile Posts Queue — Today

**The gap, in plain numbers.** Based on observed signals from the competitor scan, Bone Dry's Indianapolis GBP shows consistent photo and post activity consistent with a formal weekly publishing schedule. Step 4: Schedule a recurring Monday morning task for someone on the crew to shoot 6-8 job-site photos with location services enabled and upload them to the GBP Photos tab under the correct category (Exterior, Work, Team). Step 5: Respond to every unresponded Google review this week — positive and negative. Review response velocity is a GBP activity signal.

GBP post activity gains local pack ranking within 2-4 weeks of sustained posting — meaning posts published this week have a material chance of influencing pack position during peak search demand.

# Competitive Intelligence Brief: Bone Dry Roofing
**Raptor Roofing | Cameron Blakely Dashboard**
**Refreshed: June 9, 2026**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

The company is family-owned and operated, with owner Gene Judd growing up the son of a roofing contractor in Illinois.

 

The Bone Dry Family of Companies now spans eight states, including 15 Bone Dry Roofing locations nationwide plus acquired brands such as G&W Roofing, Ravlin's Roofing, RCV Roofing and Siding, Roof One, Bone Dry Commercial Roofing, Quality Roofing Services, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors.

 Their core differentiator is institutional scale marketed as local family ownership — a direct positioning tension that Raptor can exploit.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



As of their 2023 Roofing Contractor of the Year profile, Bone Dry reported 500 employees company-wide across 20 locations.

 More recent data from LeadIQ puts the number lower: 

as of March 2026, Bone Dry Roofing has approximately 240 employees.

 **Confidence: medium** — headcount aggregators diverge significantly, likely because subsidiary brands are tracked separately. On revenue: 

the hiring of a new CFO and COO at Bone Dry came on the heels of 2023 revenue of over $183 million

, and 

RocketReach pegs 2026 annual revenue at $191 million

 for the full enterprise. **Confidence: medium** — these are third-party estimates; the Indianapolis branch alone generated roughly $36M in 2022 per [Roofing Contractor Magazine](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing). For competitive purposes, treat the Indy operation as a ~$40–50M annual revenue unit.

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

Active openings across job boards paint a clear picture of where they're pushing:

- 

Current Indianapolis-area postings on Glassdoor include a Commercial Production Manager, a Sales Representative (Roofing Division), a Construction Assistant to the masonry production manager, and a Field Project Foreman for the Commercial Division.


- 

They are actively recruiting for their Management in Training (MIT) Program

, a pipeline play that signals long-term expansion intent rather than backfill hiring.
- 

ZipRecruiter listings include a Claims Specialist and an Insurance Specialist

 — both dedicated to insurance claim facilitation, confirming storm/insurance work remains a core revenue driver.
- 

Per ZoomInfo, their CMO Matt Tyner is focused on "strategic marketing efforts to approach new markets, grow current markets, and generate lead volume and revenue"

 — meaning their marketing function is well-staffed and actively resourced at the VP level.

No ops leadership or GM hires flagged specifically for Indianapolis in the last 30 days, but the volume of sales rep postings suggests southside Indy (US-31 corridor) is a priority territory.

---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



On Yelp, the primary Indianapolis location at 7735 Winton Dr carries only 75 reviews

 — a stark contrast to 954 Google reviews. That is a 92% review-funneling ratio to Google, meaning Yelp is essentially an unmanaged surface for them. Cross-platform rating discrepancy is notable: 

a third-party reputation aggregator shows Bone Dry at 4.7 stars across 2,858 combined reviews

 — 0.2 stars below their Google profile, suggesting a non-trivial volume of lower ratings exists outside their primary funnel.

On BBB: 

they maintain an A+ BBB rating and have won Angie's List Super Service Awards for many consecutive years.

 However, 

the BBB complaint log shows at least one instance where the business responded to a dispute but failed to make a good faith effort to resolve it, and others where the consumer did not accept the resolution.

 A specific December 2025 complaint details billing for work not yet performed.

On Facebook Ad Library: no current paid ad data was surfaced, but their tech stack per LeadIQ includes Facebook — confirming active use. Their partnership with F.C. Tucker Home Services ([talktotucker.com](https://homeservices.talktotucker.com/listing/bone-dry-roofing/)) is a notable referral channel that Raptor should map.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture

Bone Dry operates [bonedry.com](https://bonedry.com), a WordPress-based site with dedicated location pages (e.g., [bonedry.com/indianapolis/](https://bonedry.com/indianapolis/)) structured with city-specific service content, reviews, and team pages — a textbook multi-location SEO architecture. 

Their tech stack includes Adobe Premiere Pro, WordPress, cdnjs, Module Federation, and Webpack

, indicating investment in both content production and front-end performance. They maintain active blog/article content on the Indianapolis subdirectory and use schema-eligible review content fed directly from their own review page at [bonedry.com/indianapolis/reviews/](https://bonedry.com/indianapolis/reviews/).

Their domain authority is bolstered by: 

being named Roofing Contractor Magazine's 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year

 — that national trade press mention generates high-DA backlinks. Their partnership with F.C. Tucker and Indy Humane also produce local backlinks. The combination of brand volume, press coverage, and location-page depth gives them strong domain authority on "Indianapolis roofing company" head terms. Raptor's counter-move is long-tail AEO content targeting specific Indy suburbs where Bone Dry's pages are thin.

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry is well-positioned to appear in AI-generated answers for "best roofers Indianapolis" and "roof replacement Indianapolis" for one primary reason: they are the highest-reviewed contractor by volume in the market (954 Google reviews), they have national trade press citations, and their bonedry.com domain has broad topical authority across roofing + Indianapolis keyword clusters. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all weight entity prominence and third-party citation density — Bone Dry checks both boxes.

However, their 4.9-star Google rating trails Raptor's perfect 5.0, and their cross-platform rating bleed (4.7 on aggregators) is a signal that AEO engines may deprioritize them if review sentiment analysis is part of the ranking logic. Raptor's opportunity: create suburb-specific AEO content pages (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Greenwood, Zionsville) with structured FAQ schema that directly answers "who is the best roofer in [suburb]" — content Bone Dry has not built at the depth needed to dominate those long-tail AI queries.

---

## 7. Strategic Read vs Raptor

**Where Bone Dry beats Raptor:** Raw review volume (954 vs. 677), national brand recognition and trade press credibility, multi-service breadth (solar, commercial, masonry, insulation), an in-house training academy ([Bone Dry University](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing)) that fuels recruitment, and a dedicated insurance claims team that positions them as a one-stop storm-damage shop.

**Where Raptor beats Bone Dry:** Perfect 5.0 star rating (vs. 4.9), tighter accountability narrative ("we don't outsource accountability") that directly counters the complexity of a 20-location company with acquired subsidiaries, and a cleaner BBB complaint profile. Bone Dry's BBB complaint log has documented cases of billing for incomplete work — that is a material trust gap.

**Most exploitable weakness:** At their scale and with their acquisition model, Bone Dry is structurally unable to deliver the single-point-of-accountability experience Raptor can — lean into that asymmetry in every sales conversation and ad creative.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **The F.C. Tucker partnership model.** 

Bone Dry Roofing is a listed member of F.C. Tucker's Home Services network, which helps homeowners find vendors before, during, and after a move.

 That is a systematic referral pipeline tied to the highest-volume real estate brokerage in Central Indiana. Cameron should pursue an equivalent listing or exclusive partnership with a competing brokerage (Carpenter, RE/MAX, Keller Williams Indy).

2. **The on-site production supervisor model.** 

Bone Dry deploys a production supervisor who remains on-site for the duration of every project to ensure safety, protection, and serve as the main point of contact for homeowners.

 If Raptor is not already doing this systematically and documenting it in review requests, start — and call it out explicitly in marketing as proof of the accountability claim.

3. **Military/First Responder discount visibility.** 

Bone Dry actively promotes discounts for military members, military veterans, senior citizens, first responders, teachers, and healthcare professionals.

 This is a low-cost, high-goodwill positioning tactic that plays especially well in south Indy markets and drives word-of-mouth in tight-knit professional communities. Raptor should match or exceed it and make it a homepage-visible offer.

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

We hold 959 Google reviews at 4.9 stars. Raptor sits at approximately 681 reviews at 5.0 stars. On paper they look clean. But clean optics are not the same as structural depth — and Raptor has real structural vulnerabilities we have not yet exploited. This memo outlines exactly where they break and what we do about it in the next 90 days.

---

**SECTION I: RAPTOR'S THREE EXPLOITABLE WEAKNESSES**

**Weakness 1: They Are a Young Company With a Shallow Track Record.**



Raptor has been serving the Indianapolis area only since 2016.

 That is ten years of history. 

We began with a garage office in 1989, offering roofing repairs and replacement to customers in the greater Indianapolis area.

 That is 37 years versus 10. When a homeowner is spending $15,000–$25,000 on a roof, longevity and institutional accountability matter enormously. **Raptor cannot manufacture a track record they do not have. We can hammer this contrast relentlessly.**

**Weakness 2: Their Premium Positioning Is Entirely Dependent on LSA and Google Ads — Which We Can Outspend and Out-Credential.**

Raptor's known primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads. That is a pay-to-play moat, not a structural one. 

Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractors meet strict standards for professionalism, business stability, and customer service, and they offer the best warranty, representing less than 1% of roofing contractors.

 

We are one of the few roofing companies in Indianapolis to hold the distinguished Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status.

 Raptor holds only Preferred status — one tier below ours. **Every dollar they spend on ads drives traffic to a landing page that cannot match our certifications, our warranty tier, or our 37-year institutional credibility.** We redirect that traffic to us instead.

**Weakness 3: Their Community Presence Is Geographically Thin and Personally Dependent.**



Raptor's local identity is built around co-founders Cameron Blakely and Patrick Kinney, described as "locals raising the bar for roofing in Center Grove and beyond."

 That is a two-person personality play concentrated in a single south-side corridor. It is not a system — it is a founder brand. If either founder's attention is pulled, the community presence erodes. Meanwhile, 

for more than 30 years, giving back to the communities we serve has been a cornerstone of Bone Dry Roofing's values — and because we are family owned and locally operated, our teams live, work, and play here.

 **We have deeper, broader, longer-standing community equity across the entire metro. We have simply not deployed it aggressively enough south of I-465.**

---

**SECTION II: THREE 90-DAY CAMPAIGNS**

**Campaign 1: "Since 1989" Conquest Campaign on Google Ads and LSA — Bid Directly on Raptor's Core ZIP Codes.**

We immediately build a dedicated Google Ads campaign targeting ZIP codes 46142, 46143, and 46227 — Raptor's Center Grove and Greenwood home territory. Ad creative headline: *"Roofing Indianapolis Since 1989. Not Since 2016."* No name-calling. Just arithmetic. The body copy leverages our 959 reviews against their 681, our Platinum Preferred status against their Preferred tier, and our 37 years against their decade. We simultaneously max out LSA bids in those ZIP codes to crowd their ad real estate. Budget: $8,000–$12,000/month concentrated in these five ZIPs for the full 90 days. **The goal is to intercept every homeowner who searches "roof replacement Greenwood" or "roofing Center Grove" before Raptor's ad loads.**

**Campaign 2: Nextdoor and Facebook Neighborhood Saturation in Greenwood, Center Grove, and Beech Grove.**



Bone Dry Roofing was already a Neighborhood Favorite on Nextdoor in 2023.

 We have not capitalized on that recognition aggressively in Raptor's geography. We launch hyper-targeted Nextdoor sponsored posts and Facebook neighborhood group campaigns in every HOA and subdivision community in Center Grove and Greenwood. Creative angle: real before/after job photos from local streets — not stock imagery — with homeowner first-name testimonials. Offer a free storm damage inspection with a $200 gift card to a local Greenwood business for every completed inspection booked through the campaign. **This converts our neighbor-to-neighbor credibility into direct pipeline in the exact neighborhoods Raptor considers their home turf.**

**Campaign 3: Contractor-of-the-Year Trust Blitz on YouTube Pre-Roll and Meta Video.**



Named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine, Bone Dry Roofing is recognized for dedication to excellence in every aspect of residential roofing.

 Raptor has no equivalent national credential. We produce a 30-second video spot — zero production fluff — that opens with: *"National Roofing Contractor of the Year. 37 Years in Indianapolis. 959 Reviews."* Run it as unskippable pre-roll on YouTube and as Meta video ads geo-targeted to homeowners aged 35–65 within 20 miles of Indianapolis with household income over $80K. Budget: $5,000/month. **This builds brand awareness and credential contrast in exactly the demographic Raptor is trying to capture with its premium positioning.**

---

**SECTION III: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Physically plant Bone Dry flags — literally and figuratively — in Center Grove and Greenwood through a concentrated job-site yard sign blitz backed by a neighborhood referral incentive.**

For the next 90 days, every completed job in ZIP codes 46142 and 46143 gets four oversized yard signs placed — one in front of the job site and three offered to immediate neighbors with a $100 Visa gift card incentive for any neighbor who books a free inspection that converts to a signed contract. 

Bone Dry Roofing has the largest fleet and most experienced crews to provide customers with prompt service and complete satisfaction

 — we have the capacity to execute at scale. **This physically colonizes the streetscape in Raptor's core geography.** Homeowners in Center Grove will see a Bone Dry sign before they ever type a search query. It disrupts Raptor's community feel advantage at street level, where no Google budget can follow.

**Cameron should be seeing Bone Dry signs in his own neighborhood within 60 days. That is the goal.**

---

*Prepared for internal strategic use. Recommend immediate budget authorization for Q3.*

ZipRecruiter currently shows active Indiana postings offering up to a $2,000 sign-on bonus for subcontract roofing crew leads and a "$3,000 Quick Start" incentive for sales representatives.

 No marketing, ops leadership, or digital-specific roles were identified for the Indianapolis location specifically in the last 30 days — all visible hiring is sales and install-side. That said, the volume of sales rep postings signals a pipeline-building push, not a maintenance mode.
