Erie Home's national brand scale and the volume of third-party editorial coverage (Roofing Contractor, This Old House, Qualified Remodeler, Trustpilot, GuildQuality) give them strong AI citation signals.

## 2. Tactic of the Week

Bone Dry's PR agency executed media relations campaigns specifically leveraging philanthropic initiatives — including free roof donations and community programs — to generate consistent local coverage and set the company apart from competitors.

 The mechanism is not goodwill alone. It is backlink arbitrage: each story syndicated through regional news networks lands on a separate referring domain. The [April 2026 Bone Dry release](https://kdhnews.com/online_features/press_releases/bone-dry-roofing-provides-roof-inspection-services-to-homeowners-on-indianapolis-east-side/article_d411055e-f05b-56fd-ba09-beca52a5ab16.html) appeared on at minimum two confirmed regional outlets (kdhnews.com, wboc.com) from a single press release distribution — two new referring domains from one piece of work, delivered in under 48 hours. Bone Dry does this repeatedly. 

Over the 16-month agency partnership alone, they engaged local online, print, and broadcast media primarily in Indianapolis and Nashville.

 That cadence compounds. Raptor has zero visible press mentions surfaced across all searches run for this brief. The backlink gap of approximately 195 referring domains versus Bone Dry is not a function of Raptor doing SEO poorly — it is a function of Raptor not having a press and content program at all.

2. Write a 400-word press release in AP style. Use a dateline (Indianapolis, IN), include a direct quote attributed to the company, include the company's boilerplate, and include a contact name and phone number. Do not use a quote from a named team member if Raptor prefers to keep staff anonymous — attribute the quote to "a Raptor Roofing spokesperson."

Distribute through [PR Newswire's local Indiana distribution](https://www.prnewswire.com/) or through [Send2Press](https://www.send2press.com/), which feeds the BLOX Digital network that syndicates to regional TV and newspaper sites across Indiana. Organic outreach to individual journalists is slower and unreliable for this purpose.

4. Post the same release on Raptor's own website as a News or Blog post. This creates an internal page that can accumulate internal links and signals topical authority over time.

5. Claim the RooferRate profile and any other unclaimed directory listings this same week. Each claimed profile with consistent NAP data is a citation that reinforces the entity trust that makes press coverage more authoritative.

**The SUCCESS METRIC**

In 30 days, check two things. First, run a backlink check in Ahrefs or Moz (free trial available) and count new referring domains added in the past 30 days — the target is a minimum of 3 net new referring domains from this one release. Second, check whether Raptor's name appears in any new third-party editorial or roundup content by searching "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis" in Google News. A single well-placed community story can trigger secondary coverage (local TV segments, HOA newsletters, neighborhood Facebook groups) that generates additional organic mentions. Both signals compound over time. The goal is not one release — it is establishing the cadence. Bone Dry has been doing this for years. Raptor starts the clock this week.

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989 by Gene Judd out of a garage in Speedway, Indiana, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

Headquartered in Indianapolis, they have expanded to offices in Ohio, Kentucky, Missouri, Tennessee, Colorado, and Florida.

 

They have grown further through M&A, with the Bone Dry Family of Companies now spanning eight states and including brands such as G&W Roofing, Roof One, Bone Dry Commercial Roofing, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors.

 Their public-facing differentiator is scale dressed up as family ownership — not a franchise, but a roll-up operating like one.

LeadIQ pegs approximately 240 employees as of March 2026

, while 

RocketReach estimates 181 employees and $191 million in revenue for the enterprise.

 The Indianapolis location alone is a fraction of that headcount. **Confidence: medium.** On revenue, 

ZoomInfo notes that the hiring of a new CFO and COO came on the heels of 2023 revenue exceeding $183 million

 — the most reliable figure in the data set. **Revenue confidence: medium-high** (sourced from [ZoomInfo](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/bone-dry-roofing-inc/545924884) and [Roofing Contractor Magazine](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing)).

ZipRecruiter shows active Indianapolis postings for Commercial Sales Representatives and Sales Representatives targeting the Southside/Greenwood market specifically.

 

Indeed shows open roles for an Insurance Claims Specialist and an Insurance Specialist — both dedicated to helping customers file storm damage claims

, which signals a deliberate push into insurance-driven replacement revenue. 

An Assistant Production Manager posting on ZipRecruiter is also active, responsible for material sourcing alongside the General Manager.

 No marketing or CMO-level hire detected in the last 30 days; 

their current CMO, Matt Tyner, was brought in specifically to drive new market entry and lead volume.



---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Yelp shows the Winton Dr location with 75 reviews

 — a sharp undercount relative to 2,447 Google reviews. Classic review-funneling: they steer satisfied customers to Google and let Yelp languish. No meaningful Yelp engagement visible. 

Paid social is largely absent — they don't appear to be running significant PPC campaigns, and their Facebook ads are described as basic branding plays rather than aggressive lead-gen.

 On BBB, the profile is complete with full executive listing but 

recent complaint activity includes a June 2025 tarp dispute on a tornado-damaged duplex, with the homeowner alleging incomplete coverage that caused additional interior damage

 — exactly the kind of execution failure that a premium competitor should amplify. 

GuildQuality reviews surface a recurring pattern of crews showing up unannounced and projects being abandoned before full completion.

 They are active on GuildQuality as a third-party review channel, which Raptor should monitor for unfiltered sentiment.

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture



A November 2025 third-party audit found that Bone Dry's location pages suffer from near-identical duplicate content, creating index inefficiencies and weakening topical authority with search engines.

their mobile speed score is reported at 29 and desktop at only 65

, a significant paid-visibility gap. 

Their tech stack includes WordPress, cdnjs, and Adobe Premiere Pro

 — nothing indicative of AEO-forward structured data investment. Their blog exists but is thin; no evidence of E-E-A-T-optimized long-form content targeting suburb-level queries (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville).

**BONE DRY ROOFING — INTERNAL STRATEGIC MEMO**
**CONFIDENTIAL**

**TO:** Ownership — Gene Judd, Billy Smith, Tony Merlie
**FROM:** Matt Tyner, Chief Marketing Officer
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Offensive — Indianapolis Metro vs. Raptor Roofing
**DATE:** July 16, 2026

---

**SITUATION**

Raptor Roofing is a real threat in specific corridors — Greenwood, Center Grove, and the south-side I-65 corridor — and they are growing fast. 

Their Google profile was showing a perfect 5.0 rating as recently as July 2025.

 We cannot ignore that. But they are smaller, newer, and structurally exposed in ways we are not. The goal of this memo is to exploit those gaps with precision over the next 90 days.

---

**SECTION ONE: WHERE RAPTOR IS MOST VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Shallow Review Volume Makes Their 5.0 Fragile and Statistically Unconvincing.**

Raptor has a perfect score, but on a fraction of our volume. 

Bone Dry carries an average rating of 4.8 stars across over 5,000 reviews.

 A 5.0 on 690 reviews is a thin veneer. Sophisticated homeowners doing comparison research — especially on larger replacement jobs — understand that 2,451 verified reviews at 4.8 represents a far more statistically reliable signal than 690 at 5.0. **We need to make that math visible in our own ad copy and sales materials.** The message: "2,451 real jobs. 4.8 stars. That's not a rating — that's a track record."

**Weakness 2: They Are a Single-Market Operator with No Institutional Infrastructure.**



Bone Dry's Indianapolis office is the headquarters of a company that has been family-owned and operated since day one — not a franchise.

 

Bone Dry Roofing stretches across seven states and operates 17 residential and three commercial roofing offices.

 Raptor, by contrast, is a south-side Indianapolis shop. Their warranty, their callbacks, their post-job service — it all depends on one small team. **When we position against them, we lean hard into institutional staying power.** 

Most roofing contractors only last a few years. Bone Dry has been proudly serving customers for over three and a half decades.

 Raptor cannot say that. In a category where homeowners worry about warranty redemption, that asymmetry is devastating if communicated correctly.

**Weakness 3: Their Lead Source Concentration Is a Single Point of Failure.**

Raptor's primary lead engine is Google LSA and Google Ads. That means they have almost no diversified digital presence — no earned media, no multi-channel retargeting, no brand insulation if Google suspends or down-ranks their profile. 

LSA downsides include unpredictable lead quality, dependency on Google's verification status, and the risk of suspension or revocation, which can be appealed but isn't guaranteed to be resolved quickly.

 **If we flood the same LSA auction and simultaneously build brand equity on channels they don't play in — Meta, YouTube pre-roll, direct mail in their core zip codes — we deny them the comparison-shop moment and own the homeowner before they ever search.**

---

**SECTION TWO: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: LSA Domination + Review Velocity Push — Launch Week 1**



Reviews directly impact LSA ranking. More positive reviews mean higher placement. Review volume and ratings are major ranking factors for Local Services Ads.

 We currently hold a massive volume lead. We need to convert that advantage into LSA rank supremacy in the Greenwood, Center Grove, and Southport zip codes — Raptor's home territory. Assign a dedicated LSA manager to audit every lead weekly and dispute invalid charges. 

Agencies frequently recover 15–20% of LSA budgets simply by disputing junk leads.

 Run uncapped budgets during peak storm response windows. 

Companies that answer 95% or more of their LSA leads consistently outrank those responding to 70–80% of leads, and responding within five minutes can improve conversion rates 8x.

 Operationally, we need a dedicated phone coverage protocol for LSA leads during business hours with a target answer time under 60 seconds.

**Campaign 2: "35 Years vs. a Few Years" — Brand Conquest Campaign on Meta and YouTube**

Build a Meta and YouTube pre-roll campaign targeting homeowners aged 35–65 in Johnson County and southern Marion County zip codes — Raptor's backyard. **The creative angle: trust is earned over decades, not months.** Ad creative: side-by-side visual — "Founded 1989 | 2,451 reviews | 35 years in Indianapolis" vs. a blurred generic "new roofing startup" silhouette. No name-calling. Just contrast. 

Bone Dry Roofing was named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine

 — that national award becomes the visual anchor of every display unit. Retarget anyone who visits our site within the prior 30 days with a direct testimonial video from a Greenwood or Center Grove homeowner. This is a brand siege on the neighborhoods Raptor has built their identity around.

**Campaign 3: Google Ads Keyword Conquest — Bid on Raptor's Brand Terms and Intercept Their Comparison Shoppers**



Bidding on competitor brand names as keywords — known as "conquesting" — is a common aggressive tactic that is generally allowed, as long as the trademarked name is not used in the ad copy itself.

 We run a tight conquest campaign bidding on "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis" and variations. The ad creative does not mention them by name — it instead reads: "Before You Decide — See Why 2,451 Indianapolis Homeowners Chose Bone Dry." Landing page: a direct comparison of years in business, review volume, manufacturer certifications, and warranty terms. 

Bone Dry is one of the few roofing companies in Indianapolis to hold both the Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status

 — credentials Raptor, as an Owens Corning Preferred-only contractor, cannot match. Make that table visible and damaging.

---

**SECTION THREE: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Own Greenwood and Center Grove physically and digitally before the next hail event.**

Raptor has built their brand equity and community identity in these two markets specifically. Their sponsorships, their reviews, their LSA targeting — it all concentrates here. **Our most threatening move is a coordinated ground-and-air blitz into those two markets before the next significant weather event hits, so that when hail falls, our name is already in every homeowner's head.**

Tactically: deploy two canvassing crews into Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhoods in August with door hangers and yard sign placements from completed jobs. Simultaneously, launch a direct mail campaign to all homes in 46143, 46142, and 46077 zip codes featuring our review count, our 35-year history, and a QR code to a "Get a Second Opinion" landing page — specifically built for homeowners already in a competitor's sales process. 

Enable emergency tarp service, emergency leak repair, and storm damage assessment as separate job types in our LSA profile before storm season peaks. When a hailstorm hits, homeowners search these exact terms — and the roofers who already have them enabled capture the surge while competitors scramble to update their profiles after the fact.



**The goal is simple: when the next storm hits Johnson County, Bone Dry gets the call — not Raptor.**

---

**BOTTOM LINE**

Raptor is executing well for a company their size. But they are playing a small game. We have the reviews, the credentials, the institutional credibility, and the marketing infrastructure to suffocate their growth in the specific geography they call home. This quarter, we stop playing defense.

Requesting budget authorization for Campaign 1–3 execution by August 1.

— Matt Tyner, CMO

## Bone Dry Roofing — Competitive Intelligence Brief
**Refreshed: June 30, 2025 | Raptor Roofing Dashboard**

---

## 1. Who They Are



Founded in 1989 by Gene Judd out of a garage in Speedway, Indiana, Bone Dry Roofing has grown into one of the largest residential roofing companies in the Midwest.

 

Headquartered in Indianapolis, they have expanded to offices in Ohio, Kentucky, Missouri, Tennessee, Colorado, and Florida.

 

They have grown further through M&A, with the Bone Dry Family of Companies now spanning eight states and including brands such as G&W Roofing, Roof One, Bone Dry Commercial Roofing, and Nu-Tec Roofing Contractors.

 Their public-facing differentiator is scale dressed up as family ownership — not a franchise, but a roll-up operating like one.

---

## 2. Estimated Scale



Roofing Contractor Magazine reported 500 employees as of their 2023 Contractor of the Year profile.

 

LeadIQ pegs approximately 240 employees as of March 2026

, while 

RocketReach estimates 181 employees and $191 million in revenue for the enterprise.

 The Indianapolis location alone is a fraction of that headcount. **Confidence: medium.** On revenue, 

ZoomInfo notes that the hiring of a new CFO and COO came on the heels of 2023 revenue exceeding $183 million

 — the most reliable figure in the data set. **Revenue confidence: medium-high** (sourced from [ZoomInfo](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/bone-dry-roofing-inc/545924884) and [Roofing Contractor Magazine](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/98973-2023-residential-contractor-of-the-year-bone-dry-roofing)).

---

## 3. Recent Hiring Signals

The hiring posture is heavy on revenue-generating roles. 

Their [Lever ATS board](https://jobs.lever.co/bonedry) shows active Indianapolis openings across Commercial, Customer Service, Roofing, Sales, and Solar teams.

 

ZipRecruiter shows active Indianapolis postings for Commercial Sales Representatives and Sales Representatives targeting the Southside/Greenwood market specifically.

 

Indeed shows open roles for an Insurance Claims Specialist and an Insurance Specialist — both dedicated to helping customers file storm damage claims

, which signals a deliberate push into insurance-driven replacement revenue. 

An Assistant Production Manager posting on ZipRecruiter is also active, responsible for material sourcing alongside the General Manager.

 No marketing or CMO-level hire detected in the last 30 days; 

their current CMO, Matt Tyner, was brought in specifically to drive new market entry and lead volume.



---

## 4. Off-Google Presence



Yelp shows the Winton Dr location with 75 reviews

 — a sharp undercount relative to 2,447 Google reviews. Classic review-funneling: they steer satisfied customers to Google and let Yelp languish. No meaningful Yelp engagement visible. 

Paid social is largely absent — they don't appear to be running significant PPC campaigns, and their Facebook ads are described as basic branding plays rather than aggressive lead-gen.

 On BBB, the profile is complete with full executive listing but 

recent complaint activity includes a June 2025 tarp dispute on a tornado-damaged duplex, with the homeowner alleging incomplete coverage that caused additional interior damage

 — exactly the kind of execution failure that a premium competitor should amplify. 

GuildQuality reviews surface a recurring pattern of crews showing up unannounced and projects being abandoned before full completion.

 They are active on GuildQuality as a third-party review channel, which Raptor should monitor for unfiltered sentiment.

---

## 5. SEO and AEO Posture



A November 2025 third-party audit found that Bone Dry's location pages suffer from near-identical duplicate content, creating index inefficiencies and weakening topical authority with search engines.

 

Their M&A activity has fragmented domain authority by redirecting location pages to separate brand websites (RCV, Whole Sun Solar, G&W), which negatively impacts SEO consolidation.

 On site speed: 

their mobile speed score is reported at 29 and desktop at only 65

 — both well below thresholds that hurt local pack rankings. 

GLSAs were not found active for Bone Dry in Indianapolis at the time of a late-2025 analysis

, a significant paid-visibility gap. 

Their tech stack includes WordPress, cdnjs, and Adobe Premiere Pro

 — nothing indicative of AEO-forward structured data investment. Their blog exists but is thin; no evidence of E-E-A-T-optimized long-form content targeting suburb-level queries (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville).

---

## 6. Generative Engine Visibility

Bone Dry is almost certainly cited in generic AI answers for "best roofers Indianapolis" purely on volume signals — 2,447 Google reviews and a national trade award create the citation fodder that LLMs index. 

Their 2023 Roofing Contractor Magazine "Residential Contractor of the Year" designation

 is exactly the type of third-party editorial signal that surfaces in ChatGPT and Perplexity answers. However, their weak suburb-level page structure means they are unlikely to appear in tightly geo-specific queries like "roofing company Fishers Indiana" or "roof replacement Zionsville." Raptor's opportunity: Bone Dry dominates broad Indy queries in AI engines; Raptor can own the high-intent suburb layer (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Zionsville, Greenwood) by producing genuinely differentiated location pages with specific project data, named neighborhoods, and permit references — content Bone Dry cannot replicate at scale without exposing their duplicate-page problem further.

## 7. Strategic Read vs. Raptor

**Where they beat Raptor:** Raw review volume (2,447 vs. 681) gives them default AI citation authority and map-pack weight. Their national award, multi-state brand footprint, and dedicated insurance claims staff create institutional credibility that a single-market operator can't match on surface metrics. Their in-house Bone Dry University recruitment machine also builds a talent pipeline Raptor can't ignore as it scales.

**Where Raptor beats them:** 5.0 vs. 4.8 — that gap is exploitable in paid media headlines and in AI-answer contexts where rating precision matters. Raptor's 0.8 owner response rate is not listed, but Bone Dry's is also low; neither is clean here. Raptor's accountability narrative ("we don't outsource accountability") directly attacks Bone Dry's documented execution failures at scale. Bone Dry has a CMO but a broken paid media engine; Raptor has the ability to be faster and tighter in market.

**Most exploitable weakness:** Their GLSA gap in Indianapolis combined with a 29 mobile speed score means they are likely losing map-pack clicks to anyone running a tighter technical SEO and paid-local game right now.

---

## 8. What Raptor Should Watch or Copy

1. **Insurance Claims Staffing as a Revenue Play.** 

Bone Dry is actively hiring dedicated Insurance Claim Specialists to guide customers through storm damage filings.

 This is a sales-cycle compression tactic — controlling the adjuster conversation keeps the job in-house. Cameron should evaluate whether a single trained project manager playing this role during storm season creates a measurable close-rate lift before committing to a full hire.

2. **GuildQuality as a Third-Party Trust Layer.** Bone Dry uses [GuildQuality](https://www.guildquality.com/profile/bone-dry-roofing) as an independent survey platform that feeds verified reviews to lenders, realtors, and insurance agents. This is an off-Google trust signal that shows up in B2B referral channels Raptor isn't currently playing in. Worth evaluating as a referral-partner credentialing tool.

3. **"Roofing Contractor of the Year" Award as Paid and Organic Fuel.** 

Bone Dry has plastered the 2023 national award across every page of their site and in paid creative.

 Cameron should be actively pursuing Indiana Roofing Contractors Association recognition or Owens Corning Top of the House award tiers — any third-party award creates the editorial backlink and AI-citation signal that scales Raptor's generative engine visibility without incremental ad spend.

**BONE DRY ROOFING — INTERNAL STRATEGIC MEMO**
**CONFIDENTIAL**

**TO:** Ownership — Gene Judd, Billy Smith, Tony Merlie
**FROM:** Matt Tyner, Chief Marketing Officer
**RE:** 90-Day Market Share Offensive — Indianapolis Metro vs. Raptor Roofing
**DATE:** July 16, 2026

---

**SITUATION**

Raptor Roofing is a real threat in specific corridors — Greenwood, Center Grove, and the south-side I-65 corridor — and they are growing fast. 

Their Google profile was showing a perfect 5.0 rating as recently as July 2025.

 We cannot ignore that. But they are smaller, newer, and structurally exposed in ways we are not. The goal of this memo is to exploit those gaps with precision over the next 90 days.

---

**SECTION ONE: WHERE RAPTOR IS MOST VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Shallow Review Volume Makes Their 5.0 Fragile and Statistically Unconvincing.**

Raptor has a perfect score, but on a fraction of our volume. 

Bone Dry carries an average rating of 4.8 stars across over 5,000 reviews.

 A 5.0 on 690 reviews is a thin veneer. Sophisticated homeowners doing comparison research — especially on larger replacement jobs — understand that 2,451 verified reviews at 4.8 represents a far more statistically reliable signal than 690 at 5.0. **We need to make that math visible in our own ad copy and sales materials.** The message: "2,451 real jobs. 4.8 stars. That's not a rating — that's a track record."

**Weakness 2: They Are a Single-Market Operator with No Institutional Infrastructure.**



Bone Dry's Indianapolis office is the headquarters of a company that has been family-owned and operated since day one — not a franchise.

 

Bone Dry Roofing stretches across seven states and operates 17 residential and three commercial roofing offices.

 Raptor, by contrast, is a south-side Indianapolis shop. Their warranty, their callbacks, their post-job service — it all depends on one small team. **When we position against them, we lean hard into institutional staying power.** 

Most roofing contractors only last a few years. Bone Dry has been proudly serving customers for over three and a half decades.

 Raptor cannot say that. In a category where homeowners worry about warranty redemption, that asymmetry is devastating if communicated correctly.

**Weakness 3: Their Lead Source Concentration Is a Single Point of Failure.**

Raptor's primary lead engine is Google LSA and Google Ads. That means they have almost no diversified digital presence — no earned media, no multi-channel retargeting, no brand insulation if Google suspends or down-ranks their profile. 

LSA downsides include unpredictable lead quality, dependency on Google's verification status, and the risk of suspension or revocation, which can be appealed but isn't guaranteed to be resolved quickly.

 **If we flood the same LSA auction and simultaneously build brand equity on channels they don't play in — Meta, YouTube pre-roll, direct mail in their core zip codes — we deny them the comparison-shop moment and own the homeowner before they ever search.**

---

**SECTION TWO: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN 90 DAYS**

**Campaign 1: LSA Domination + Review Velocity Push — Launch Week 1**



Reviews directly impact LSA ranking. More positive reviews mean higher placement. Review volume and ratings are major ranking factors for Local Services Ads.

 We currently hold a massive volume lead. We need to convert that advantage into LSA rank supremacy in the Greenwood, Center Grove, and Southport zip codes — Raptor's home territory. Assign a dedicated LSA manager to audit every lead weekly and dispute invalid charges. 

Agencies frequently recover 15–20% of LSA budgets simply by disputing junk leads.

 Run uncapped budgets during peak storm response windows. 

Companies that answer 95% or more of their LSA leads consistently outrank those responding to 70–80% of leads, and responding within five minutes can improve conversion rates 8x.

 Operationally, we need a dedicated phone coverage protocol for LSA leads during business hours with a target answer time under 60 seconds.

**Campaign 2: "35 Years vs. a Few Years" — Brand Conquest Campaign on Meta and YouTube**

Build a Meta and YouTube pre-roll campaign targeting homeowners aged 35–65 in Johnson County and southern Marion County zip codes — Raptor's backyard. **The creative angle: trust is earned over decades, not months.** Ad creative: side-by-side visual — "Founded 1989 | 2,451 reviews | 35 years in Indianapolis" vs. a blurred generic "new roofing startup" silhouette. No name-calling. Just contrast. 

Bone Dry Roofing was named the 2023 Residential Roofing Contractor of the Year by Roofing Contractor Magazine

 — that national award becomes the visual anchor of every display unit. Retarget anyone who visits our site within the prior 30 days with a direct testimonial video from a Greenwood or Center Grove homeowner. This is a brand siege on the neighborhoods Raptor has built their identity around.

**Campaign 3: Google Ads Keyword Conquest — Bid on Raptor's Brand Terms and Intercept Their Comparison Shoppers**



Bidding on competitor brand names as keywords — known as "conquesting" — is a common aggressive tactic that is generally allowed, as long as the trademarked name is not used in the ad copy itself.

 We run a tight conquest campaign bidding on "Raptor Roofing Indianapolis" and variations. The ad creative does not mention them by name — it instead reads: "Before You Decide — See Why 2,451 Indianapolis Homeowners Chose Bone Dry." Landing page: a direct comparison of years in business, review volume, manufacturer certifications, and warranty terms. 

Bone Dry is one of the few roofing companies in Indianapolis to hold both the Platinum Preferred and ShingleMaster Select contractor status

 — credentials Raptor, as an Owens Corning Preferred-only contractor, cannot match. Make that table visible and damaging.

---

**SECTION THREE: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Own Greenwood and Center Grove physically and digitally before the next hail event.**

Raptor has built their brand equity and community identity in these two markets specifically. Their sponsorships, their reviews, their LSA targeting — it all concentrates here. **Our most threatening move is a coordinated ground-and-air blitz into those two markets before the next significant weather event hits, so that when hail falls, our name is already in every homeowner's head.**

Tactically: deploy two canvassing crews into Center Grove and Greenwood neighborhoods in August with door hangers and yard sign placements from completed jobs. Simultaneously, launch a direct mail campaign to all homes in 46143, 46142, and 46077 zip codes featuring our review count, our 35-year history, and a QR code to a "Get a Second Opinion" landing page — specifically built for homeowners already in a competitor's sales process. 

Enable emergency tarp service, emergency leak repair, and storm damage assessment as separate job types in our LSA profile before storm season peaks. When a hailstorm hits, homeowners search these exact terms — and the roofers who already have them enabled capture the surge while competitors scramble to update their profiles after the fact.



**The goal is simple: when the next storm hits Johnson County, Bone Dry gets the call — not Raptor.**

---

**BOTTOM LINE**

Raptor is executing well for a company their size. But they are playing a small game. We have the reviews, the credentials, the institutional credibility, and the marketing infrastructure to suffocate their growth in the specific geography they call home. This quarter, we stop playing defense.

Requesting budget authorization for Campaign 1–3 execution by August 1.

— Matt Tyner, CMO

Bone Dry Roofing is almost certainly cited in AI-generated answers for "best roofers Indianapolis" and related queries. The inputs that drive GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) citations — review volume, third-party directory presence, named awards, press mentions — all favor Bone Dry heavily.

**SITUATION SUMMARY**

Raptor is not a mature competitor. 

The company only completed its rebrand from Raptor Restoration to Raptor Roofing in January 2025.

 That is a structural vulnerability we have not yet pressed. They are building a brand identity in real time while we have over three decades of market presence. This is a window. Here is how we close it.

**SECTION 1: WHERE RAPTOR IS VULNERABLE**

**Weakness 1: Their review volume is thin and their brand is less than two years old.**

Raptor is running their entire positioning on a 5.0 star rating. That number is real, but 

as of mid-July 2025, they held fewer than 500 Google reviews,

 while we sit at 2,452. Any homeowner who does a side-by-side comparison sees a company with a fraction of our proven track record. **Their perfect score is a fragile identity built on low volume — and it is the first thing a skeptical buyer questions.** We do not attack their reviews directly; we simply make our own volume impossible to ignore.

**Weakness 2: They are single-channel dependent and highly exposed on paid search.**

Raptor's primary lead sources are Google LSA and Google Ads. 

LSA rankings are not purely pay-to-win — contractors who dominate the top spots often win on responsiveness, not just budget, and companies that answer 95% or more of their LSA leads consistently outrank those responding to 70–80% of leads.

 A company that rebranded 18 months ago almost certainly does not have the operational infrastructure to answer at that rate consistently. We do. We use that against them. Additionally, 

roofing is among the more competitive and higher-cost categories within home services, since storm-driven demand spikes and high job values both push bidding activity upward.

 If we aggressively enter the same LSA market, we drive their cost per lead up while leveraging our superior review volume to rank above them.

**Weakness 3: Their geographic community positioning is narrow and imitable.**

Raptor has planted a flag specifically in Greenwood and Center Grove with family-feel sponsorships. 

Center Grove Community School Corporation serves 7,735 students

 — a finite, addressable community that Raptor is trying to own. **They are not embedded yet. They are still auditioning.** A competitor with our resources can walk into those same zip codes, outspend them on sponsorships, and make their "community feel" look like what it is — a marketing tactic, not a legacy. Their slogan "we don't outsource accountability" is aspirational copy from a company that did not even carry its current name until 2025. We have been accountable in Indianapolis since 1989.

**SECTION 2: THREE CAMPAIGNS TO LAUNCH IN 90 DAYS**

Launch a full-funnel creative campaign built around our review volume advantage. Ad creative: side-by-side graphic — "Would you trust the company with 2,452 reviews or 692?" Run this on Meta (Facebook/Instagram) targeting homeowners aged 35–65 in Johnson County, Marion County, and Hamilton County zip codes. Set a $15,000/month Meta budget concentrated on Greenwood (46142, 46143), Center Grove (46143), Carmel, and Fishers. 

Meta platforms work differently from Google — they interrupt people who aren't actively searching,

 meaning we build brand preference before the homeowner ever opens Google. When they do open Google, they already know our name. Do not mention Raptor by name in any ad. The comparison speaks for itself.

**Campaign 2: LSA Siege — Out-Answer, Out-Rank, Out-Spend**

We activate an immediate LSA budget increase targeting every zip code where Raptor is currently appearing. 

Answering LSA calls within 15 seconds is the gold standard for responsiveness — we implement call forwarding to ensure someone always answers and we never let an LSA call go to voicemail during business hours.

 We staff a dedicated LSA response role — one person, one job, answer every call in under 20 seconds. 

LSAs capture customers who are ready to call immediately, while Google Ads capture customers who are researching and comparing options.

 We run both, simultaneously, in Raptor's target geography. Our goal is not to match their spend — it is to be the name that always answers when theirs does not.

Deploy a neighborhood-level campaign in Johnson County and Center Grove built around our founding year. Sponsor Center Grove Trojans athletics, the Greenwood Farmers Market, and the Johnson County Fair — wherever Raptor is visible, we are more visible. 

Bone Dry started humbly in a small garage in 1989 and built up one customer at a time to become one of the largest residential, family-owned roofing companies in the area.

 That is a genuine story. **SECTION 3: THE SINGLE MOST THREATENING MOVE THIS QUARTER**

**Target their Google Ads keywords with conquest campaigns using our review volume as the creative weapon.**

We build a dedicated landing page at bonedry.com/indianapolis-roofing-reviews that simply displays our 2,452 reviews with a conversion form. See Why Bone Dry Has Been Indy's Most-Reviewed Roofer Since 1989. Free Estimate Today."** 

Many roofing contractors focus entirely on bids and ignore Quality Score — a better Quality Score reduces cost per click while improving position, and competitor analysis often reveals gaps in ad relevance or landing page experience that, once fixed, let you outrank better-funded competitors at a lower cost.

 Our landing page, built around review volume and local longevity, will have a higher Quality Score than any page Raptor can produce. **We do not just outspend them — we outrank them at a lower cost per click while the ad itself reminds every searcher that we have four times their proven customer base.** That is the move that costs Cameron sleep.

**BOTTOM LINE**

Raptor is good at what they do. But they are a new brand masquerading as an institution. We are the institution. We have the reviews, the years, the infrastructure, and the certifications. 

As an Owens Corning Platinum Preferred Contractor and CertainTeed ShingleMaster Select Contractor, Bone Dry delivers warranty levels Raptor cannot match.
